rows.contact_address: Praia de Botafogo, 190 - Rio de Janeiro
rows.notice_text:
PROJETO PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZÔNIA - ASL

Acordo de Doação Nº TF - B6898 / Projeto Nº P158000

 

Aviso Específico de Licitação (AEL)

 

CONTRATAÇÃO DE SERVIÇO ESPECIALIZADO EM ELABORAÇÃO DE RELATÓRIO DE GESTÃO INSTITUCIONAL PARA O PROJETO ASL BRASIL

PROJETO PAISAGENS SUSTENTÁVEIS DA AMAZONIA – FASE 2

(DE-ASL2-POA3-MMA-2026-0017)

 

AEL0024/2026 - BR-FGV- 572837 -NC-RFQ

 

 

  1. DESCRIÇÃO DO OBJETO

Contratação de serviço técnico especializado em organização, sistematização, consolidação, revisão editorial, tratamento gráfico, editoração, diagramação, acessibilidade e preparação para publicação do Relatório intitulado Comunicado de Gestão Institucional da SBIO/MMA (Unidade de Coordenação do Projeto UCP), período 2023-2026.

 

 

  1. CONTEXTO

O Projeto Paisagens Sustentáveis da Amazônia (ASL Brasil), que tem como objetivos ampliar e aperfeiçoar o gerenciamento de Unidades de Conservação estaduais e federais, aumentar a área sob recuperação da vegetação e incentivar o uso sustentável da floresta, e fortalecer as cadeias produtivas dos produtos da biodiversidade na Amazônia.

 

O projeto é gerido pelo Global Environment Facility (GEF), o ASL Brasil é parte do Programa Regional Amazon Sustainable Landscapes, que envolve oito países na fase 1, 2 e 3 Brasil, Colômbia, Peru, Bolívia, Equador, Guiana, Suriname e Venezuela. O Banco Mundial é a agência implementadora do programa, tendo como diretriz principal a visão integrada do bioma.

 

No Brasil, o Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA), por meio da Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBio), é a instituição coordenadora do projeto, responsável pela supervisão, articulação institucional e monitoramento da implementação. Assim como, Unidade Operativa do projeto responsável pela implementação de ações do projeto.

 

A Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBIO), do Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA), desempenha papel estratégico na formulação, coordenação e implementação de políticas públicas voltadas à conservação da biodiversidade, à gestão sustentável das florestas, à proteção da fauna e ao fortalecimento da governança ambiental no Brasil. Suas ações estão alinhadas aos instrumentos de planejamento governamental, aos compromissos nacionais e internacionais assumidos pelo País e às prioridades estabelecidas no âmbito do Ministério.

 

No período de 2023 a 2026, a SBIO vem conduzindo um conjunto de iniciativas voltadas à implementação de políticas, programas, projetos e instrumentos normativos que contribuem para a conservação da biodiversidade, a recuperação de ecossistemas, o fortalecimento da bioeconomia, a gestão territorial, a valorização dos povos e comunidades tradicionais e o cumprimento dos compromissos internacionais relacionados à Convenção sobre Diversidade Biológica (CDB), à Convenção-Quadro das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (UNFCCC), à Agenda 2030 para o Desenvolvimento Sustentável e à Convenção sobre a Conservação das Espécies Migratórias de Animais Silvestres (CMS).

 

Nesse contexto, torna-se necessária a elaboração de um Relatório intitulado Comunicado de Gestão Institucional da SBIO (2023–2026), com o objetivo de consolidar, sistematizar e apresentar, de forma integrada e acessível, os principais resultados alcançados pela Secretaria no período. O documento deverá constituir-se em um instrumento de comunicação institucional voltado à transparência, à prestação de contas e à divulgação das ações e dos impactos das políticas públicas implementadas pela SBIO, traduzindo informações técnicas em linguagem clara e acessível aos diferentes públicos.

 

A elaboração do comunicado deverá considerar a integração entre os principais instrumentos de planejamento, monitoramento e gestão governamental, incluindo o Plano Plurianual (PPA), os Acordos de Gestão Anuais, o Planejamento Estratégico do MMA, o Planejamento Estratégico da SBIO, os compromissos decorrentes das Conferências das Partes (COPs) e demais referenciais institucionais pertinentes. Como fontes de informação deverão ser utilizados os instrumentos normativos e estratégicos da Secretaria, relatórios técnicos dos departamentos, relatórios de execução de projetos e demais documentos institucionais relevantes.

 

Além da consolidação de indicadores e evidências quantitativas, o comunicado deverá apresentar, de forma clara e acessível, os resultados e informações institucionais definidos e validados pela SBIO/MMA. Para favorecer a comunicação com os diferentes públicos, deverão ser empregados recursos editoriais e gráficos, como infográficos, mapas, quadros, tabelas, linhas do tempo, fotografias e demais elementos visuais, elaborados a partir dos dados e conteúdos disponibilizados pela Secretaria.

 

Considerando o volume de informações a serem organizadas e a necessidade de tratamento editorial e gráfico, revisão, tradução, diagramação, acessibilidade e preparação do material para publicação, faz-se necessária a contratação de empresa especializada para executar esses serviços. A definição do conteúdo técnico, das fontes, das mensagens institucionais, dos resultados a destacar e a validação das informações permanecerão sob responsabilidade da SBIO/MMA.

 

  1. UNIDADE DEMANDANTE

A unidade de execução do projeto demandante desta contratação é a Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV). Esta aquisição está vinculada à estratégia de fortalecimento da comunicação institucional do Projeto ASL Brasil e enquadra-se nas atividades de divulgação e sensibilização.

A unidade operativa demandante desta aquisição é a Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBIO), do Ministério do Meio Ambiente e Mudança do Clima (MMA).

 

  1. ESPECIFICAÇÕES

 

OBJETO DO SERVIÇO:

O serviço especializado tem por objetivo organizar, sistematizar, consolidar e apresentar as informações referentes à gestão da Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBIO/MMA), no período de 2023 a 2026, com base nos dados, documentos, conteúdos, fontes e orientações disponibilizados ou indicados pela SBIO/MMA. O trabalho compreenderá a organização e estruturação das informações conforme modelo e diretrizes definidos pela Secretaria; transposição e consolidação de dados; elaboração de gráficos, tabelas, mapas, infográficos, linhas do tempo e demais recursos visuais; adequação e revisão editorial dos textos fornecidos; tradução; editoração; diagramação; acessibilidade; incorporação dos ajustes solicitados; e preparação dos arquivos finais para publicação. O conteúdo técnico e a validação das informações serão de responsabilidade da SBIO/MMA. Como resultado, deverá ser entregue o “Comunicado de Gestão Institucional da SBIO/MMA (2023–2026)”, revisado, diagramado e finalizado para divulgação institucional em meio digital.

 

ATIVIDADES A SEREM DESENVOLVIDAS

O fornecedor deverá desenvolver as atividades descritas a seguir, de forma integrada e em articulação com a equipe técnica da Secretaria Nacional de Biodiversidade, Florestas e Direitos Animais (SBIO/MMA):

Reuniões

  • Participar de reuniões de alinhamento com a equipe da SBIO/MMA para recebimento de orientações, acompanhamento do cronograma e dos fluxos de trabalho, apresentação das versões produzidas e registro dos ajustes solicitados;

Organização e sistematização de informações

  • Receber, organizar, classificar e sistematizar as informações secundárias necessárias à elaboração do relatório, a partir de fontes oficiais, bases de dados e documentos institucionais, incluindo, entre outros, a Estratégia e Plano de Ação Nacionais para a Biodiversidade (EPANB), o Plano Nacional de Recuperação da Vegetação Nativa (PLANAVEG), as listas nacionais de espécies ameaçadas, relatórios técnicos dos departamentos da SBIO, relatórios de execução de projetos, instrumentos normativos, documentos estratégicos, bases de dados oficiais e demais materiais pertinentes ao período de referência;

Sistematização das informações

  • Sistematizar e consolidar os dados e as informações secundárias, organizando-os de acordo com a estrutura e as correlações com os instrumentos de planejamento e gestão institucional previamente indicadas pela SBIO/MMA, incluindo o Plano Plurianual (PPA), os Acordos de Gestão, o Planejamento Estratégico do MMA e da SBIO, bem como os compromissos, metas e agendas nacionais e internacionais pertinentes às áreas de atuação da Secretarial;

rows.notice_text:
Country: Republic of Mozambique

Name of Project:  Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2)

Grant number:    IDA-E4810

Job title: Senior Economist

Reference Number: MZ-MTL-564463-CS-INDV

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2) project and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve provision of high-level economic and financial advisory services to the PMU and the Ministry of Transport and Logistics. The core objective of the assignment is to strengthen the Government's capacity to assess, negotiate, and manage the economic performance of transport and logistics corridor concessions in a manner that maximises sovereign value capture, ensures macro-fiscal sustainability, and aligns with international standards of regulatory best practice.

The Senior Economist will engage the National Institute of Statistics (INE) to prepare the future transport and logistic satellite account to capture regularly the contribution of the sector in the gross domestic product (GDP). There will be a probationary period of 3 months from the date of signing the contract. The contract will be renewed upon satisfactory performance. The SE will report directly to the Project Coordinator.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address provided below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites qualified individuals ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Expressions of interest must include the following: (i) a CV detailing qualifications, work experience and achievements in comparable work and (ii) a cover letter, specifically addressing how the applicant fulfills each of the mandatory selection criteria listed below.

The criteria for selecting the consultant are:

a) A Master's degree or higher in Economics, Finance, Business Administration, International Banking, or a related discipline from a recognised university.

b) A minimum of 15 years of progressive professional experience in economics, finance, investment banking, or financial advisory roles, with demonstrated exposure to capital markets, regulatory environments, and financial governance at a senior level.

c) Demonstrated expertise in macroeconomic and financial modelling, with ability to develop quantitative analyses of corridor economics, concession financial structures, and fiscal risk.

d) Strong understanding of regulatory frameworks governing infrastructure concessions and public-private partnerships, as well as familiarity with prudential and fiscal governance frameworks applicable to government-held infrastructure assets.

e) Familiarity with World Bank operational procedures, including guidelines applicable to advisory and analytical assignments under Investment Project Financing.

f) Knowledge of the economic and institutional context of Mozambique, including the transport sector, public finance framework, and macroeconomic environment

g) Fluency in English is required, as the majority of analytical outputs and development partner communications will be produced in English.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn  to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Rules for IPF Borrowers of September 2025 ("the Rules"), which sets forth the Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

For more information, please visit the address below during office hours from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Submissions of Interest in Portuguese and English must be sent in writing to the address below (by e-mail only) by 15:00 hours on September 30, 2026, local time, CAT/UTC +2.

 

Ministry of Transport and Logistics,

Attention:Portfolio Coordinator

Avenue: Martires of Inhaminga nr 336, floor 1st

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Project Supervision National Port Community System (PCS)

Reference No: MNE-WBTTFP-94710-DQCBS-25-2.1.6

Published on:  September 18, 2026

 

The Government of Montenegro has received financing in the total amount of USD 15,000,000.00 (equivalent) from the World Bank, toward the costs of the “Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation Phase 2” (TTFP).  Ministry of Transport (MoT) is the umbrella ministry under which the transport sector falls and will serve as the lead implementing body for the project and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan towards payment for Consulting services under the Contract Ref. No: MNE-WBTTFP-94710-DQCBS-25-2.1.6 Consulting Services for Project Supervision National Port Community System (PCS).

 

The Ministry of Transport (the Client) and Ministry of Maritime Affairs (the Beneficiary) are seeking a highly qualified consulting firm with maritime supply chain experience, Port Community System project design and implementation management expertise or Port Community System project supervision,to: i) provide technical advisory support to the Client during the selection and contracting of the supplier of the National Port Community System (the PCS Supplier); and (ii) supervise, on behalf of the Client, the performance of the PCS Supplier Contract for the design, supply, delivery, installation, configuration, integration, testing, commissioning, Operational Acceptance and hand-over of the National PCS Phase 1 focused on the Port of Bar community, including warranty and technical support services of the PCS Supplier

The objective of this service (“the Service”) is to assist the Client in ensuring that the PCS Supplier performs the PCS Supplier Contract in accordance with its technical requirements, Project Plan, Implementation Schedule, applicable World Bank procurement and contract documents, and good international practice for port community systems, so that the PCS is delivered fit for purpose, on time, secure, documented and ready for sustainable operation by the Beneficiary.

 

The Consultant will work closely with relevant stakeholders ensuring compliance with Montenegro’s policies, EU regulations, and international best practices.

 

The services of the consultants or firm are expected to be required for a time period of approximately 640 days between  November, 2026, and April 30, 2028, which marks the end of the project design, supply, implementation, commissioning and maintenance phase 1 period.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” seventh edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Joint ventures should submit letter/confirmation, indicating their intent to form a joint venture if awarded the contract and shall provide the above-mentioned information for each member of the joint venture. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Direct QCBS (modified approach of a Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS)) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

The detailed RFP (Request for Proposal) which include Terms of Reference (TOR) and procedure instructions, can be obtained upon request at the e-mail address given below. Interested consultants may obtain further information at the address below, from 09:00 to 15:00 hour’s local time.

This outer envelope shall be addressed to the Client and bear the submission address, RFP reference number, the name of the assignment, the Consultant's name and address, and shall be clearly marked “Do Not Open Before [date/time]”.

 (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

Country: Republic of Uzbekistan

Implementing Agency: National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan.

Project Name: “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People” (INSON)

Financing Agreement No. 7555-UZ / Grant Agreement No. TF C4589-UZ

Assignment: Occupational Health and Safety Specialist

Package Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-INSON-CS-IC-3.1.1.6

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank for implementation of the “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People” (INSON) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services include providing technical support to the PIU on occupational health and safety (OHS), including monitoring compliance with OHS requirements during construction, rehabilitation and installation works, monitoring contractors’ compliance with the relevant obligations, analysis of risks and incidents, and preparation of recommendations and reports.

The assignment shall be performed on a full-time basis for an initial period of 24 months. The duty station is the PIU office in Tashkent; duty travel to Project sites in the regions of the Republic of Uzbekistan is required.

The detailed Terms of Reference can be found at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YSLdqhtJLjKrK_6IYcKMYneMUIPfNxid/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104755491226149341341&rtpof=true&sd=true

The National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan invites qualified individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (a CV describing relevant experience). Staff of consulting firms may express interest through their employing firm; however, only the experience and qualifications of the respective individual candidate will be considered in the selection.

Consultant Selection Criteria:

Education: Bachelor’s degree or higher in occupational health and safety, environmental or civil engineering, industrial safety, environmental sciences, public health, engineering, or another related field.

Professional experience: at least five (5) years of professional experience in OHS, including at least three (3) years of OHS experience on construction projects.

Specific experience: practical experience in OHS management at construction, rehabilitation or infrastructure sites, contractor monitoring, conducting inspections and risk assessments, incident investigation, and development or application of OHS plans, ESMPs/C-ESMPs, or similar documents.

Environmental and social requirements: familiarity with applicable environmental and social requirements. Experience in projects financed by international financial institutions or development partners, as well as familiarity with World Bank requirements, will be an advantage.

Language skills: excellent command of Uzbek and Russian and a good working knowledge of English.

The candidate ranked first based on the CV evaluation may be invited for an interview to confirm his/her qualifications, experience and availability for the assignment.

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 09:00 to 18:00 (Tashkent time).

Expressions of Interest, supported by CVs, must be submitted in writing to the address below (in person, by mail, or by e-mail) by 28 September 2026.

INSON PIU under NASP

Attention: Mr. M. Khusanov – PIU Coordinator.

Address: 3 Amir Temur Street, Tashkent, Uzbekistan, 100060

Tel.: +998712395976.

rows.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

Philippines - Fisheries Coastal Resiliency Project

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: P174137

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy services for the preparation of Feasibility Studies (FS) of Aquaculture and Fisheries Post Harvest Infrastructure for Fisheries Management Area 9

Reference No.: PH-BFAR RO 10 - FMA9-511923-CS-CQS

 

The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources-Region 10/Regional Project Implementing Unit-9 (BFAR-10/RPIU-9) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the following projects within FMA-9, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services, to wit:

 

FMA Coordination Unit (FCU)

Project Component

Proposed Sub-Project

Project Objective

FCU 7

MARLIN 2.3

Ice Plant and Cold Storage – Ubay, Bohol

  1. To support the local fishery industry and expand markets.
  2. To strengthen the financial resilience of fisherfolk. 
  3. To encourage preservation of aquaculture and captured fishery products.
  4. To increase fish production and sustain food security.
  5. To augment the income of the marginal fisherfolk.

MARLIN 2.2

2-2 Tonner Solar Ice making Machine, Maria Siquijor

FCU 8

Marlin 2.3

Warehouse – Tomas Oppus, Southern Leyte

  1. Provide equipment and supply storage to fisherfolk that will protect their items from harsh weather conditions, rodents and insects, and even from thieves.
  2. Increase profits of fishermen by reducing travel time and cost.
  3. Improve livelihood by ensuring consistent supply of high-quality feeds. 
  4. Function as hub for fish farmers to foster collaboration and knowledge sharing to improve farming practices and collective marketing efforts. 
  5. Centralize inventory management.

FCU 9

Marlin 2.3

Ice Plant with Cold Storage Facility – Aurora, Zamboanga del Sur

To provide a facility for storing perishable fishery products such as fresh fish and those which require low temperature storage to avoid spoilage.

Marlin 2.3

Common Post Harvest Facility – Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Sur

The purpose of the subproject is to create a temporary or transit point for fishery products from FMA9. This is to ensure the process is regulated and post-harvest losses are minimized.

FCU 10

Marlin 2.3

  1. Fish Processing Plant 
  2. Ice Plant and Cold Storage  Balingasag, Misamis Oriental

To help to attain the 2 out of 3 objectives of the Human Goal of the FMA-9 Framework Plan, to wit:

  1. By 2034, at least 50% of the fishing organizations and value chain players in the fisheries sector are empowered; and
  2. By 2034, reduce poverty of at least 5% among fisherfolks from the average baseline of 28.06 poverty incidence.

To enhance the post-harvest capabilities of the municipality, where one of the established Mariculture Parks in Region 10 is situated. This also includes its neighboring areas and the Northern Mindanao Aqua-Industrial Business Corridor (ABC).

FCU 10

Marlin 2.3

  1. Fish Port
  2. Ice Plant with Cold Storage

Talisayan, Misamis Oriental

To help to attain the 2 out of 3 objectives of the Human Goal of the FMA-9 Framework Plan, to wit:

  1. By 2034, at least 50% of the fishing organizations and value chain players in the fisheries sector are empowered; and
  2. By 2034, reduce poverty of at least 5% among fisherfolks from the average baseline of 28.06 poverty incidence.

To enhance the post-harvest capabilities of the municipality, where one of the established Mariculture Parks in Region 10 is situated. This also includes its neighboring areas and the Northern Mindanao Aqua-Industrial Business Corridor (ABC).

FCU 13

Marlin 2.3

Ice Plant and Cold Storage – Brgy. Pagatpatan, Butuan City

To provide a resilient fisheries ice plant and cold storage for various fishery products and its components for the fisherfolk engaged both in capture and aquaculture sector.

Marlin 2.3

Warehouse – Cabadbaran, Agusan del Norte

To provide a resilient fisheries warehouse facility for various fishery products and its components for the fisherfolk engaged both in the capture and aquaculture sector. 

The subproject aims to support the operation of the existing Tolosa and Kalibunan Mariculture Parks.

FCU 13

Marlin 2.3

Warehouse/Fish Processing Plant – Malimono, Surigao del Norte

To provide a resilient fisheries common post-harvest facilities for various fishery products and its components for the fisherfolk engaged both in capture and aquaculture sector.

 

The Consultancy Services (“the Services”) for the preparation of Feasibility Studies (FS) of Aquaculture and Fisheries Post Harvest Infrastructure for Fisheries Management Area 9, shall follow the guidelines as outlined in Annex 7 in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR), Guidance for Various Analysis and Project Documents, Fisheries Infrastructure Assessment Tool (FIAT), World Bank-FAO, 2022, and WB Environmental and Social Standards. The FS shall include:

  1. The compilation of all relevant data for each location that are missing from Annex B in the TOR, such as the state of the resources to be harvested, landing statistics by species and season, topographic surveys including cadastral and land ownership details, bathymetric surveys, geotechnical investigations, resource networks, access routes, parking facilities, etc. If the data is not available, discuss precautionary values to be adopted with the stakeholders in consultation with Component 1;
  2. Alternative and/or sustainable technologies to be adopted in the detailed design;
  3. Preparation of outline design solutions (preliminary design) for the site in question; 
  4. Preparation of budgetary estimate of costs;
  5. Preparation of an Environmental Examination (EE) (desk study) of the Environmental and Social assessment. This is not an ESIA;
  6. Preparation of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), according to the Philippine EIS System, and ECC Application and Issuance of ECC Terms and Conditions;  
  7. Preparation of Social-related plans needed for the approval of Infrastructure projects, such as Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Resettlement Action Plan (SEP), Indigenous Peoples Plan (IPP), Social Development Plan (SDP), Information, Education and Communication Campaigns (IEC);
  8. Detailed project constraints and risk assessment;
  9. Detailed identification of risk and impacts with mitigation measures based on the Environmental and Social Standards of World Bank;
  10. Financial and economic evaluation, including Net Present Value (NPV), Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR) and Internal Rate of Return (IRR);
  11. Confirm the TORs for the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) field studies and impact assessment report (see Task 2 and detailed ESIA requirements in Annex D in the attached TOR); 
  12. Preparation of ESIA budget estimate; and
  13. Preparation of TOR per Sub-Project (see Name of Project and Location below).
  1. Ice Plant and Cold Storage Facility (IPCS), Ubay, Bohol
  2. 2.2 Tonner Solar Ice Making Machine with Cold Storage, Maria, Siquijor
  3. Warehouse, Tomas Oppus, Southern Leyte
  4. Ice Plant and Cold Storage Facility (IPCS), Aurora, Zamboanga del Sur
  5. Common Post Harvest Facility in Dapitan City
  6. Fish Processing Plant in Balingasag, Misamis Oriental
  7. Ice Plant and Cold Storage Facility in Balingasag, Misamis Oriental
  8. Reconstruction and Expansion of Existing Landing Quay and Ancillary Equipment in Talisayan, Misamis Oriental
  9. Ice Plant and Cold Storage Facility in Talisayan, Misamis Oriental
  10. Warehouse, Cabadbaran, Agusan Del Norte
  11. Ice Plant and Cold Storage Facility (IPCS), Butuan City
  12. Post Harvest Facility, Malimono, Surigao Del Norte

 

The implementation period is expected to cover 15 calendar days, with the assignment scheduled to commence upon the receipt of Notice to Proceed.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest, or can be obtained at the address given below.

 

The (BFAR-10/RPIU-9) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: 

 

  1. Qualification of Consulting Firm

To effectively carry out the tasks for the consulting services, the consultancy firm should have gained experience at least five (5) years in the conduct of Feasibility Study on Aquaculture and Fisheries Infrastructure or related projects in the Philippines.

 

Further, the firm is preferably ISO 9001-2015 certified and should be able to field key professional personnel with adequate educational and technical background, experience and capability in the fields of port planning, engineering[1] [2] , economics, finance and management. Any changes or replacements of assigned personnel shall be subject to BFAR NPMO review and approval.

 

 

  1. Qualification of Key Staff

 

All the structures to be designed are located in a highly corrosive marine environment and the key staff are required to be knowledgeable of the impacts of marine corrosion on structures and equipment. The following are the minimum qualifications of key staff:

 

  1. Team Leader must be a licensed Agricultural and Biosystems Engineer or Civil Engineer with at least five (5) years as Team Leader in similar projects.
  2. Economists/Financial Specialist must be a degree holder in Economics/Business related courses with at least five (5) years as Economist/Financial Specialist in projects of similar nature.
  3. Planner/ Engineer must be a licensed Engineer/Architect with at least ten (5) years as Planner Engineer in projects of similar nature.
  4. Project Development Specialist must be a  degree holder in Management/Business with at least five (5) years as Project Development Specialist in projects of similar nature.
  5. Environmental Specialist must be a degree holder in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering and other related courses with at least  five (5) years in the position in projects of similar nature.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 as revised last February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 8:00AM-5:00PM.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in one (1) original and three (3) certified true copies, and a scanned copy will be submitted to the address below not later than October 10, 2025, 5:00PM:

 

 

BUREAU OF FISHERIES AND AQUATIC RESOURCES-10/REGIONAL PROJECT IMPLEMENTING UNIT (BFAR-10/RPIU-9)

Macabalan, Cagayan de Oro City

E-mail: bac.r10@bfar.da.gov.ph

 

 

 

 

ATTY. ROLAND B. INTUD

BAC Chairperson

Le Gouvernement du Mali a obtenu de la Banque mondiale deux crédits destinés au financement des activités du Projet Mali Nafa Soro Siraw (Mali-NSS). L’Unité Nationale de Coordination du Projet Mali Nafa Soro Siraw (Mali-NSS) a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des fonds pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif à l’audit des conventions pluriannuelles de maîtrise d’ouvrage déléguée (MOD) exécutées par l’AGEROUTE. Ces conventions concernent notamment les opérations pluriannuelles d’entretien routier et leur mise en œuvre avec les structures publiques concernées.

 

 

OBJECTIF GÉNÉRAL

 

L’objectif général de la mission est de réaliser un audit indépendant des conventions pluriannuelles de maîtrise d’ouvrage déléguée exécutées par l’AGEROUTE, afin d’évaluer leur gestion, leur conformité, leur performance et leur efficacité, et de formuler des recommandations visant à améliorer leur mise en œuvre.

 

 

OBJECTIFS SPÉCIFIQUES 

 

Les objectifs spécifiques de l’audit sont :

 

  1. examiner le cadre juridique et institutionnel des conventions et apprécier la conformité de leur mise en œuvre ;

 

  1. apprécier le respect des engagements contractuels des différentes parties et analyser les conditions d’exécution des conventions ;

 

  1. évaluer les performances techniques, financières et opérationnelles, ainsi que les dispositifs de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques ;

 

  1. identifier les insuffisances, risques et dysfonctionnements et proposer des mesures correctives ainsi qu’un plan d’amélioration.

 

L’Unité Nationale de Coordination du Projet invite les consultants (cabinets) à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les cabinets intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services.

 

 

LES CRITÈRES POUR L’ÉTABLISSEMENT DE LA LISTE RESTREINTE

 

  • être un Cabinet ou groupement de cabinets régulièrement constitué, disposant des capacités professionnelles et techniques nécessaires et justifiant d’au moins cinq (5) ans d’expérience générale dans l’audit de projets, programmes, conventions ou opérations du secteur des transports ;
  • disposer d’une (1) expérience avérée en audit technique, financier, institutionnel et de performance, notamment dans le domaine de l’entretien routier et des infrastructures de transport ;
  • avoir réalisé au moins cinq (5) missions similaires, dont des missions d’audit de conventions, contrats, projets ou programmes routiers ou d’infrastructures financés sur ressources publiques ou extérieures.

 

À ce titre, le consultant (cabinet) devra fournir les pièces à conviction y afférentes (attestation de service fait ou bonne fin d’exécution ; les pages de garde et de signature des contrats, ou tout document équivalent permettant de vérifier les références présentées).

 

 

DUREE ET LIEU DE CONSULTATION :

 

            La mission couvrira les travaux de préparation, de collecte et d’analyse documentaire, les travaux de terrain auprès de l’AGEROUTE et des parties prenantes concernées, les vérifications techniques, financières et institutionnelles, les restitutions et la production du rapport final.

 

 

La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est estimée entre huit (08) et douze (12) semaines, incluant les travaux de terrain, les analyses, les restitutions et la finalisation du rapport définitif.

 

Les consultants seront classés par la justification et par ordre du plus grand nombre de marchés similaires réalisés.

 

La méthode de sélection est la sélection fondée sur les qualifications du consultant (SQC) conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale et aux dispositions du dossier de consultation.

 

Les cabinets intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’Unité Nationale de Coordination du Projet Mali-NSS, sise à Médina-Coura, Rue 47, Porte 212, Bamako, République du Mali, de 8 heures à 16 heures : Tél. : +223 20 21 57 25 / 20 21 40 33 ; Fax : +223 20 21 92 30 ; E-mail : uncpaar5@gmail.com  ou dkmariko049@gmail.com.

AMI N° : ZR-PURUK-543687-CS-CQS

Date de publication : 01 juin 2026

Date de clôture : 15 juin 2026

Source de financement               : Banque mondiale (Crédit IDA N° 72160-ZR)

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) a obtenu un prêt de la Banque mondiale (BM) à hauteur de 100 millions USD pour financer le Projet d’Urgence et de Résilience Urbaine de Kananga (PURUK). Le Ministère de l’Urbanisme et de l’Habitat, à travers l’Unité de Gestion du Projet PURUK, envisage d’utiliser une partie de ces fonds pour couvrir les paiements relatifs au recrutement d’un cabinet d’Assistance Technique mentionnée en titre.
  2. Les prestations du consultant consistent à : (i) Appui à la finalisation du Plan décennal et à la structuration d’un cadre programmatique d’investissements, (ii) Identification et priorisation des sous-projets, (iii) Études de faisabilité, et (iv) Synthèse.
  3. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PURUK invite, par le présent avis d’appel à manifestation d’intérêt, des candidats firme éligibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Candidats intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications et l’expérience pertinente requises pour exécuter la mission.
  4. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont : (i) le consultant doit être une société, un cabinet ou un bureau d’études spécialisé dans le domaine, (i) disposer d’au moins dix (10) ans d’expérience en préparation d’opérations d’infrastructure urbaine en Afrique subsaharienne, (iii) il (elle) doit prouver document à l’appui qu’il (elle) a déjà réalisé, seul ou en tant que chef de fil d’un groupement, au cours de 5 dernières années (2020-2025), au moins deux (2) missions similaires de préparation de pipeline d’investissements urbains idéalement dans le cadre d’opérations financées par la Banque mondiale ou un bailleur équivalent. Une expérience préalable en RDC sera très fortement valorisée.
  5. La durée de la mission est de dix mois.    
  6. L’attention des consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 des règlements de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), cinquième édition, septembre 2023, qui énoncent la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.
  7. Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur les qualifications du consultant telle que décrite à la Section VII, paragraphe 7.11 du règlement de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), cinquième édition, septembre 2025. Les consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et ou d’une sous-traitance
  8. Les candidats intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires (les termes de références) à l’adresse ci-dessous de 9 heures à 16 heures locales et sur le site Media Congo.
  9. Les manifestations d’intérêt, écrites en langue française doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous en personne, par courrier, accompagné d’une version électronique en format Word ou PDF copiable sur une clé USD ou envoyé par courrier électronique en format PDF copiable aux adresses : ugpuruk@gmail.com, jeanmichelmbungu@gmail.com et spm.puruk.cosmos@gmail.com au plus tard le 15 Juin 2026 à 00h00', Heure locale de Kananga (TU+2), et porter clairement la mention : AMI N° : ZR-PURUK-543687-CS-CQS – Recrutement d’un Cabinet d’Assistance Technique pour l’Appui au Ministère de l’Urbanisme et de l’Habitat dans la finalisation du Plan décennal et la préparation de son pipeline d’investissements en République Démocratique du Congo.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND PUBLIC WORKS

SOUTHERN AFRICA TRADE AND CONNECTIVITY PROJECT (P164847)

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

NAME OF PROJECT: SOUTHERN AFRICA TRADE AND CONNECTIVITY PROJECT (P164847)

Credit No:                    6870-MW

Grant No:                    D804-MW

Assignment Title:        PROCUREMENT OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR PROJECT END LINE EVALUATION

 

Reference No.:             MW-MTPW-571610-CS-QCBS

 

Date of issue:               17th September, 2026

 

 

 

BACKGROUND

1) The Government of Malawi (GoM) has obtained a credit and grant from the International Development Association (IDA) under the Southern Africa Trade and Connectivity Project  to support efforts to reduce trade costs and time, increase access to improved infrastructure, and increase value chain development in targeted corridors of Malawi and Mozambique, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2) The consulting services (“the Services”) include;

  1. Assess the extent to which the project has achieved its Development Objective and component level outcomes as defined in the Project Appraisal Document (PAD).
  2. Evaluate the relevance of the project’s design and its continued alignment with the development priorities of Malawi.
  3. Assess the effectiveness and impact: understand the changes (positive or negative, intended or unintended) that the project has contributed to.
  4. Examine efficiency: evaluate how well resources were used compared to results achieved.
  5. Ensure accountability: provide evidence to the Government of Malawi and other stakeholders that resources were used responsibly.
  6. Support sustainability: Assess the extent to which observed results are likely to be sustained institutionally, financially, and technically after project closure, and identify key risks to sustainability.

The overall contract duration shall not exceed four and a half (4.5) months (18 weeks). Notwithstanding this duration, all services, deliverables, revisions and final outputs shall be completed no later than 30 June 2027. This date shall constitute a firm contractual deadline. The Consulting firm shall make any adjustments necessary to the work plan, implementation schedule, sequencing of activities and allocation of resources, at no additional cost to the Client, to ensure that all services and deliverables are completed by this date.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the website and address given below.

3) The Ministry of Transport and Public Works now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

a) Core business of the firm(s) and years in business;

b) Relevant similar experience, which should specifically include the below: The consulting firm must demonstrate:

  • A minimum of 5 years of experience in project evaluation, particularly for large-scale development projects funded by international financial institutions. Firms with more experience will have an added advantage.
  • Proven expertise in designing, implementing and writing evaluations of regional trade, private sector development, and transport facilitation projects and regional integration in Southern Africa.
  • Proven experience in conducting impact evaluations. The firm shall submit either: copies of its two most recent impact evaluation reports; or references from two clients clearly demonstrating that the firm has successfully conducted impact evaluations.
  • Strong analytical and report-writing skills.
  • Experience in conducting quantitative and qualitative research.
  • Proven experience in working with multilateral donors (e.g., World Bank, AfDB, EU) and government agencies in Sub-Saharan Africa.
  • An understanding of World Bank policies and procedures for project evaluation.
  • Fluency in English is required; knowledge of Portuguese is an advantage.
  • Experience conducting participatory, co-creative validation workshops.

c)  Technical and Managerial capability of the firm. (Provide only the structure of the organization,        general qualifications and experience, and number of key staff. Do not provide detailed CV of the staff. Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage).

The firm may propose other experts required to execute this assignment.

 

TEAM COMPOSITION

The Consulting firm's personnel, nominated for this assignment, shall be suitably qualified and experienced. As a guide, the following is an indication of the minimum level of training and experience expected of the key members:

  1. Team Leader- with a minimum of Master’s degree in Economics, Public Policy, Transport Planning, Business Administration, International Trade, Statistics, Monitoring and Evaluation and at least 15 years’ experience in leading complex evaluating donor-funded infrastructure or (e.g. World Bank, AFDB) regional trade facilitation projects and have undertaken at least 3 similar recent assignments.
  2. International Trade Facilitation Expert -with a minimum of a Master’s degree in International Trade, Economics, Public Policy, Business Administration, Logistics and Supply Chain Management or any related field and a minimum of 10 years’ experience in trade facilitation, customs modernization, or regional integration and have undertaken at least 3 similar recent assignments.
  3. Private Sector Development Expert – with a minimum of Master’s degree in Business Administration, Economics or related field, and a minimum of 10 years experience on private sector development issues and in depth understanding of agribusiness supply chains. Prior experience in the private sector is a strong advantage.
  4. Transport Corridor Expert with- a Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Transport Planning, Infrastructure Management, or a related field and a minimum of 10 years’ experience in corridor-level infrastructure planning and development, performance-based contracting and transport sector audits or multimodal transport systems and logistics integration and have undertaken at least 3 similar recent assignments.
  5. Monitoring, Evaluation and Research Specialist: with a Master’s degree in Statistics, Economics, Monitoring and Evaluation, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or related field, with at least eight (8) years of experience in monitoring and evaluation, socio-economic assessments, and development project evaluations. The expert shall demonstrate experience in quantitative and qualitative research methodologies, including surveys, statistical analysis, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, stakeholder consultations, and data triangulation, and shall have undertaken at least three (3) similar assignments.

4) The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 07:30 to 16:30 hours, local time.

DEMANDE DE MANIFESTATION D'INTÉRÊT

 (SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS)

SÉLECTION DE FIRMES/CABINETS

N° du Projet : P 169315

DON IDA N° D5620-BI

 

Manifestation d’Intérêt pour la Sélection d’un Bureau pour les Etudes techniques y compris études séparées d'EIES et Surveillance et Contrôle des travaux des Adductions d’Eau Potable suivantes: 

- Lot n°1 :

1.Etudes techniques des travaux de l'AEP Muremera-Buganuka : 23 km (TNG-04).

2. Etudes techniques des travaux de l'AEP Gatobo-Musumba: 2 km (TNG-02).

- Lot n°2 : Etude techniques des travaux de l'AEP Gitwenzi-Mivo-Gahengeri-Shango :13 km (NGZ-04).

Référence STEP: BI-TURIKUMWE PIU-549326-QCBS-CS

Date : le 11./09/2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale d’un montant de 60 millions de Dollars des Etats Unis d’Amériques pour financer le Projet  de Développement Communautaire Intégré au Burundi «PRODECI-TURIKUMWE» et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce Don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant: « les Etudes techniques y compris études séparées d'EIES et Surveillance et Contrôle des travaux d’Adduction d’Eau Potable du Lot 1 (1. Etudes techniques des travaux de l'AEP Muremera-Buganuka : 23 km (TNG-04). 2. Etudes techniques des travaux de l'AEP Gatobo-Musumba : 2 km (TNG-02), et du Lot 2 (Etude techniques des travaux de l'AEP Gitwenzi-Mivo-Gahengeri-Shango :13 km (NGZ-04)), dans les communes de Ngozi et Tangara ».

2. Les services de consultants (« les services ») comprennent :

a. Pour lesETUDES TECHNIQUES Y COMPRIS LES ETUDES SEPAREES D'EIES/PGES

 l’évaluation environnementale et sociale et les diligences environnementales et sociales adéquates, soit l’EIES assortie de son PGES ou PGES et éventuellement la production des Plans particuliers Environnementaux et sociaux selon le niveau des risques environnementaux et sociaux, recherche des matériaux (en y impliquant le Laboratoire National du Bâtiment et des Travaux Publics « LNBTP» pour les essais), Avant-Projet Détaillé, Propositions pour l’entretien des Adductions d’Eau Potable  et Préparation du Dossier d’Appel d’Offres (DAO) pour l’exécution des travaux.

b. Pour la SURVEILLANCE ET LE CONTRÔLE DES TRAVAUX DE CONSTRUCTIONS DES ADDUCTIOND D’EAU POTABLE DU LOT 1 ET DU LOT 2

La mission consiste à assurer les prestations de maîtrise d’œuvre comprenant la supervision et le contrôle des travaux d’infrastructures, le suivi des mesures environnementales, sociales, hygiènes et sécurité ainsi que la lutte contre les VGB pour le compte des communes de NGOZI et TANGARA.

Les termes de références détaillés pour cette mission peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

3. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PRODECI-TURIKUMWE invite pour le moment les Cabinets de consultants éligibles (« Consultants ») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications et l'expérience requises pour exécuter les services.

Le Cabinet recherché doit disposer des capacités techniques (équipements, matériel, personnel, etc.) et financières suffisantes pour l’accomplissement de la mission.

Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

Pour les deux phases, chaque Consultant (Bureau) recherché est un bureau spécialisé dans la conduite des études techniques, environnementales et sociales et dans la surveillance et contrôle des travaux d’Adductions d’Eau Potable. Il devra justifier d’une expérience avérée d’au moins 5 ans dans le domaine et avoir :

  • Expérience générale : Avoir au moins dix (10) ans d’expérience dans les études techniques des travaux des BTP ;
  • Avoir réalisée au moins trois (3) études techniques d’Adductions d’Eau Potable dont trois (3) d’EIES durant les 10 dernières années ;
  • Expérience spécifique : avoir réalisée avec succès au moins deux (2) études techniques et d’EIES et/ou PGES d’alimentation en eau potable pour des tronçons de 10 km et plus, durant les dix (10) dernières années.  
  • Spécialisé dans la conduite (i) des missions de surveillance et le contrôle et (ii) le suivi environnemental et social avec un accent particulier sur l’EAS-HS de ce type d’infrastructures d’AEP.
  • Justifier d’une expérience avérée d’au moins 5 ans dans le domaine des d’Adductions d’Eau Potable
  • Avoir réalisé au moins trois (3) missions réussies de surveillance et contrôle des d’Adductions d’Eau Potabledurant les 10 dernières années ;

NB : Les missions similaires réalisées doivent être accompagnées des preuves de réalisation.

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués au stade de la présélection.

Aucun bureau ne sera attributaire de plus d’un lot

NB : Le PRODECI-TURIKUMWE se réserve le droit d’écarter de la liste restreinte tout cabinet pour lequel il dispose d’éléments documentés établissant, au cours des cinq (5) dernières années, un manquement avéré aux délais contractuels de remise des livrables ou une exécution jugée non satisfaisante par le PRODECI, dûment constatée et notifiée au cabinet.

4. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) datant de juillet 2016, révisé en novembre 2017, Août 2018, novembre 2020, septembre 2023, février et septembre 2025 ». En outre, veuillez-vous référer aux informations spécifiques suivantes sur les conflits d'intérêts liés à cette mission.

Les Consultants ne peuvent être engagés pour des missions qui seraient incompatibles avec leurs obligations présentes ou passées envers d’autres clients, ou qui risqueraient de les mettre dans l’impossibilité de remplir leur mandat au mieux des intérêts de l’Etat du Burundi.

Les consultants ne peuvent être engagés dans les circonstances ci-après :

  1. Aucun Consultant (y compris le personnel et les sous-traitants à son service) ni aucun prestataire affilié (qui le contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’il contrôle lui-même ou qui est placé sous le contrôle commun) ne peut être engagé pour une mission qui, par sa nature, crée un conflit d’intérêt avec une autre de ses missions ;
  2. Aucun Consultant (y compris le personnel et les sous-consultants à son service) ni aucun prestataire affilié (qui le contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’il contrôle lui-même ou qui est placé sous un contrôle commun) ne peut être engagé pour une mission qui, par sa nature, crée un conflit d’intérêts avec une autre de ses missions ;
  3. Les Consultants (y compris les experts, le personnel et les sous-consultants à leur service) qui ont une relation professionnelle ou familiale étroite avec tout cadre de l’Etat du Burundi, de l’organisme d’exécution du Projet, d’un bénéficiaire d’une fraction de financement de la Banque mondiale ou toute autre partie représentant l’Etat du Burundi ou agissant en son nom qui participe directement ou indirectement à tout segment :
  1. de la préparation des Termes de référence de la mission ;
  2. du processus de sélection pour le contrat ; ou
  3. de la supervision du contrat,  ne peuvent être attributaire d’un contrat, sauf si le conflit résultant de ladite relation a été réglé d’une manière que la Banque juge satisfaisante tout au long du processus de sélection ou de l’exécution du contrat.

5. Les cabinets de consultants peuvent s'associer avec d'autres cabinets pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais doivent indiquer clairement si l'association se présente sous la forme d'une coentreprise et / ou d'une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d'une coentreprise, tous les partenaires de la coentreprise seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de la totalité du contrat, s'ils sont sélectionnés.

6. Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de sélection fondée sur la qualité et le coût (SFQC) énoncée dans le Règlement sur la Passation de Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d’Investissement (FPI) version de Juillet 2016, révisée en novembre 2017, Août 2018, novembre 2020, septembre 2023, février et septembre 2025.

7. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues tous les jours ouvrables à l'adresse ci-dessous de 9 heures à 17 heures (heures de Bujumbura) du lundi au jeudi et de 9 heures à 14 heures (heures de Bujumbura) les vendredi.

rows.bid_description:
Selection of Consultancy Services for Detailed Engineering Design and Construction Supervision of:
Water Supply Systems; and
The Kotu Faecal Sludge Treatment Plant, together with the Rehabilitation of Sanitation Infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul.
rows.contact_address:
Mamadi Manjang Highway

rows.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

REPUBLIC OF THE GAMBIA

The Gambia Water and Sanitation Project (WASAP)

Project ID: P513113

Assignment Title:

Consultancy Services for Feasibility Studies, Detailed Engineering Design, Procurement Support, Construction Supervision, and Defects Liability Support for Urban Water Supply Systems in Kombo East and Urban Sanitation Infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul

Reference No.: GM-NAWEC-565968-CS-QCBS

The Republic of The Gambia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Gambia Water and Sanitation Project (WASAP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Feasibility Studies, Detailed Engineering Design, Procurement Support, Construction Supervision, and Defects Liability Support for Urban Water Supply Systems in Kombo East and Urban Sanitation Infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul.

The Greater Banjul Area is the country’s principal urban and economic center. Urban water services face major challenges including production constraints, intermittent supply, ageing infrastructure, limited storage capacity, and high levels of non-revenue water. Similarly, sanitation services in Banjul and Kotu are constrained by deteriorated sewerage assets, underperforming wastewater treatment facilities, and inadequate fecal sludge management infrastructure.  WASAP will support the Government of The Gambia in addressing these challenges through investments aimed at improving service coverage, reliability, resilience, and sustainability of water supply and sanitation services.

The assignment will support the preparation and implementation of priority investments in urban water supply and urban sanitation infrastructure, including:

  • Urban water supply investments in Kombo East and Brikama East comprising boreholes, treatment facilities, storage reservoirs, transmission pipelines, distribution networks, household connections, SCADA systems, and power supply facilities; and
  • Urban sanitation investments including rehabilitation and expansion of wastewater and sewerage infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul, fecal sludge treatment facilities, pumping stations, and associated infrastructure.

Scope of the Services

The consulting services will be undertaken in five phases:

Phase 1: Feasibility Study

  • Review existing studies, plans, records, GIS data and infrastructure information.
  • Conduct socio-economic, service area, demand and affordability assessments.
  • Undertake detailed feasibility studies for urban water supply and sanitation investments.
  • Assess climate resilience, environmental and social requirements, institutional arrangements, technical options and implementation strategies.
  • Conduct economic and financial analyses, including lifecycle costing and investment prioritization.
  • Prepare feasibility reports and preliminary designs.

Phase 2: Detailed Engineering Design

  • Undertake topographic, cadastral, geotechnical, laboratory and utility investigations.
  • Prepare detailed engineering designs for:
    • Water supply facilities including boreholes, treatment systems, reservoirs, transmission mains, distribution networks and SCADA.
    • Sanitation facilities include wastewater treatment systems, fecal sludge treatment plants, sewer networks, pumping stations and sea outfall improvements.
  • Prepare design calculations, drawings, technical specifications, cost estimates, bills of quantities, and O&M documentation.
  • Prepare procurement-ready engineering packages.

Phase 3: Procurement Support

  • Prepare complete bidding documents and technical specifications.
  • Participate in pre-bid meetings and site visits.
  • Provide support during bid evaluation and contract award processes.
  • Respond to technical clarifications and prepare addenda where required.

Phase 4: Construction Supervision and Contract Administration

  • Supervise construction works and administer contracts.
  • Monitor quality assurance, environmental and social compliance, occupational health and safety, cost and schedule performance.
  • Review contractor submissions and oversee testing and commissioning.
  • Support handover and completion.

Phase 5: Defects Liability Support

  • Conduct inspections during the defect’s liability period.
  • Verify correction of defects.
  • Support final completion and contract close-out.

Duration

The estimated duration of the assignment is 46.5 months, including feasibility studies, design, procurement support, construction supervision, and defects liability support.

National Water and Electricity Company Limited (NAWEC), through the WASAP Project Implementation Unit (PIU), now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Shortlisting Criteria

Interested firms should demonstrate:

  • At least 15 years of experience in water supply and sanitation engineering.
  • At least 10 years of experience in feasibility studies, detailed design, and construction supervision of urban water and sanitation infrastructure.
  • Demonstrated experience in water treatment facilities, transmission and distribution networks, reservoirs, SCADA systems, wastewater treatment facilities, sewerage systems, pumping stations, and fecal sludge treatment infrastructure.
  • Successful completion of at least two comparable assignments financed by multilateral development partners within the last seven years.
  • Demonstrated experience in Africa and familiarity with international forms of contract including FIDIC or equivalent.
  • Demonstrated quality assurance, environmental and social management, and occupational health and safety systems.

The qualifications and experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting criteria. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023) setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a Joint Venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected.

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

The TOR and further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours:

MODIFICATION:

DEMANDE DE MANIFESTATION D'INTÉRÊT

 (SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS)

SÉLECTION DE FIRMES/CABINETS

N° du Projet : P 169315

DON IDA N° D5620-BI

 

Manifestation d’Intérêt pour la Sélection d’un Bureau pour les Etudes techniques y compris études séparées d'EIES et Surveillance et Contrôle des travaux de construction  des ECOFO et Infrastructures suivantes :


- Lot n°1 : 

1. Travauxd'extension du lycée communal de Busiga (9 salles de classe, bloc administratif, les latrines et construction de la clôture) : NGZ-1;

 2. Travaux de construction du lycée urbain de Muremera à Buye (9 salles de classe ; construction d’une clôture) : NGZ-2

- Lot n°2   

1. Travaux de construction de l’ECOFO Ngozi IV (14 salles de classe + construction d’un bloc administratif : NGZ-4

2. Travaux de construction de la clôture de la salle polyvalente du lycée communal à Cumba, commune Muyinga : MYN-01

Référence STEP : BI-TURIKUMWE PIU-549327-CS-QCBS

Date : le 11/09/2026]

1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale d’un montant de 60 millions de Dollars des Etats Unis d’Amériques pour financer le Projet  de Développement Communautaire Intégré au Burundi «PRODECI-TURIKUMWE» et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce Don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant: « les Etudes techniques y compris études séparées d'EIES et Surveillance et Contrôle des travaux de construction  des ECOFO et Infrastructures du Lot 1 (1 Travauxd'extension du lycée communal de Busiga( 9 salles de classe, bloc administratif, les latrines et construction de la clôture) :NGZ-1 ;2. Travaux de construction du lycée urbain de Muremera à Buye (9 salles de classe; construction d’une clôture : NGZ-2)  et du Lot 2 (1. Travaux de construction de l’ECOFO Ngozi IV( 14 salles de classe + construction d’un bloc administratif : NGZ-4,  2.Travaux de construction de la  clôture de la salle polyvalente du lycée communal à Cumba, commune Muyinga :MYN-01), dans les communes de Ngozi, et Muyinga»

2. Les services de consultants (« les services ») comprennent :

a. Pour lesETUDES TECHNIQUES Y COMPRIS LES ETUDES SEPAREES D'EIES/PGES

 L’évaluation environnementale et sociale et les diligences environnementales et sociales adéquates, soit l’EIES assortie de son PGES ou PGES et éventuellement la production des Plans particuliers Environnementaux et sociaux selon le niveau des risques environnementaux et sociaux, recherche des matériaux (en y impliquant le Laboratoire National du Bâtiment et des Travaux Publics « LNBTP» pour les essais), Avant-Projet Détaillé, Propositions pour l’entretien des infrastructures et Préparation du Dossier d’Appel d’Offres (DAO) pour l’exécution des travaux.

b. Pour la SURVEILLANCE ET CONTRÔLE DES TRAVAUX DE CONSTRUCTIONS DES ECOFO ET INFRASTRUCTURES DU LOT 1 ET DU LOT 2

La mission consiste à assurer les prestations de maîtrise d’œuvre comprenant la supervision et le contrôle des travaux d’infrastructures, le suivi des mesures environnementales, sociales, hygiènes et sécurité ainsi que la lutte contre les VGB pour le compte des communes de NGOZI et MUYINGA.

Les termes de références détaillés pour cette mission peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

3. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PRODECI-TURIKUMWE invite pour le moment les Cabinets de consultants éligibles (« Consultants ») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications et l'expérience requises pour exécuter les services.

Le Cabinet recherché doit disposer des capacités techniques (équipements, matériel, personnel, etc.) et financières suffisantes pour l’accomplissement de la mission.

Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

Pour les deux phases, chaque Consultant (Bureau) recherché est un bureau spécialisé dans la conduite des études techniques, environnementales et sociales et dans la surveillance et contrôle des travaux des ECOFO et infrastructures. Il devra justifier d’une expérience avérée d’au moins 10 ans dans le domaine et avoir :

  • Expérience générale : Avoir réalisée au moins cinq (5) études techniques des ECOFO et/ou infrastructures similaires dont trois (3) d’EIES durant les 10 dernières années ;
  • Expérience spécifique : avoir réalisée avec succès au moins 3 études techniques et d’EIES des ECOFO et/ou infrastructures similaire de même complexité durant les 5 dernières années.  
  • Spécialisé dans la conduite (i) des missions de surveillance et le contrôle et (ii) le suivi environnemental et social avec un accent particulier sur l’EAS-HS de ce type d’infrastructures.
  • Avoir réalisé au moins trois (3) missions réussies de surveillance et contrôle des infrastructures similaires durant les 10 dernières années ;

NB : Les missions similaires réalisées doivent être accompagnées des preuves de réalisation.

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués au stade de la présélection.

Aucun bureau ne sera attributaire de plus d’un lot

NB : Le PRODECI-TURIKUMWE se réserve le droit d’écarter de la liste restreinte tout cabinet pour lequel il dispose d’éléments documentés établissant, au cours des cinq (5) dernières années, un manquement avéré aux délais contractuels de remise des livrables ou une exécution jugée non satisfaisante par le PRODECI, dûment constatée et notifiée au cabinet.

4. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) datant de juillet 2016, révisé en novembre 2017, Août 2018, novembre 2020, septembre 2023, février et septembre 2025 ». En outre, veuillez-vous référer aux informations spécifiques suivantes sur les conflits d'intérêts liés à cette mission.

Les Consultants ne peuvent être engagés pour des missions qui seraient incompatibles avec leurs obligations présentes ou passées envers d’autres clients, ou qui risqueraient de les mettre dans l’impossibilité de remplir leur mandat au mieux des intérêts de l’Etat du Burundi.

Les consultants ne peuvent être engagés dans les circonstances ci-après :

  1. Aucun Consultant (y compris le personnel et les sous-traitants à son service) ni aucun prestataire affilié (qui le contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’il contrôle lui-même ou qui est placé sous le contrôle commun) ne peut être engagé pour une mission qui, par sa nature, crée un conflit d’intérêt avec une autre de ses missions ;
  2. Aucun Consultant (y compris le personnel et les sous-consultants à son service) ni aucun prestataire affilié (qui le contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’il contrôle lui-même ou qui est placé sous un contrôle commun) ne peut être engagé pour une mission qui, par sa nature, crée un conflit d’intérêts avec une autre de ses missions ;
  3. Les Consultants (y compris les experts, le personnel et les sous-consultants à leur service) qui ont une relation professionnelle ou familiale étroite avec tout cadre de l’Etat du Burundi, de l’organisme d’exécution du Projet, d’un bénéficiaire d’une fraction de financement de la Banque mondiale ou toute autre partie représentant l’Etat du Burundi ou agissant en son nom qui participe directement ou indirectement à tout segment :
  1. de la préparation des Termes de référence de la mission ;
  2. du processus de sélection pour le contrat ; ou
  3. de la supervision du contrat,  ne peuvent être attributaire d’un contrat, sauf si le conflit résultant de ladite relation a été réglé d’une manière que la Banque juge satisfaisante tout au long du processus de sélection ou de l’exécution du contrat.

5. Les cabinets de consultants peuvent s'associer avec d'autres cabinets pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais doivent indiquer clairement si l'association se présente sous la forme d'une coentreprise et / ou d'une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d'une coentreprise, tous les partenaires de la coentreprise seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de la totalité du contrat, s'ils sont sélectionnés.

6. Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de sélection fondée sur la qualité et le coût (SFQC) énoncée dans le Règlement sur la Passation de Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d’Investissement (FPI) version de Juillet 2016, révisée en novembre 2017, Août 2018, novembre 2020, septembre 2023, février et septembre 2025.

7. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues tous les jours ouvrables à l'adresse ci-dessous de 9 heures à 17 heures (heures de Bujumbura) du lundi au jeudi et de 9 heures à 14 heures (heures de Bujumbura) les vendredi.

8. Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être livrées par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, par courrier, ou par e-mail) avant le 10/10/2026 au plus tard à 10 heures avec les mentions :

« Manifestation d’Intérêt pour la Sélection d’un Bureau pour les Etudes techniques y compris études séparées d'EIES et Surveillance et Contrôle des travaux des travaux de construction  des ECOFO et Infrastructures du Lot 1 (1 Travauxd'extension du lycée communal de Busiga( 9 salles de classe, bloc administratif, les latrines et construction de la clôture) :NGZ-1 ;2. Travaux de construction du lycée urbain de Muremera à Buye (9 salles de classe; construction d’une clôture : NGZ-2)  et du Lot 2 (1. Travaux de construction de l’ECOFO Ngozi IV (14 salles de classe + construction d’un bloc administratif : NGZ-4, 2.Travaux de construction de la clôture de la salle polyvalente du lycée communal à Cumba, commune Muyinga : MYN-01), dans les communes de Ngozi, et Muyinga».

Development of Continuous Professional Development Programs, a Sustainable Supervision System, and Methodological Support for Monitoring and Evaluation of a Priority Evidence-Based Social Intervention

Procurement Plan Ref Number

UZ-INSON-CS-CQS-1.1.5.1

Country of Delivery

Republic of Uzbekistan

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank for the implementation of the INSON Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) include the development of a sustainable continuing professional development (CPD) system and modular professional development programs for social workers and other NASP/INSON staff; the development of a sustainable professional supervision system and methodological support for its initial pilot implementation; and methodological support for the monitoring, quality assessment, and further improvement of a priority evidence-based social intervention selected by the Client.

The scope of services includes the preparation and validation of at least six modular professional development programs and related training materials; a limited Training of Trainers (ToT) for 35-40 trainers from 14 regions; development of a professional supervision model, standards, tools, training package and support to a limited supervision pilot; a brief review of evidence-based social interventions and development and testing of monitoring and quality-assessment tools for one priority intervention; as well as knowledge transfer, quality assurance, and recommendations for institutionalization and sustainability.

The duration of the assignment is expected to be twelve (12) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR), including the full scope of services and qualification requirements, can be found at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UBUEjGW-5VAVsiq4cnxi5H8ooq_PSr7K/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104755491226149341341&rtpof=true&sd=true

The National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan now invites eligible consulting organizations (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023) (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The best qualified Consultant will be selected in accordance with the CQS method set out in the Regulations, based on the qualification requirements set out in the TOR and summarized below.

Interested Consultants should meet the following qualification requirements:

  • Legally registered consulting company, university, research institution, or nonprofit organization eligible to enter into contracts in accordance with the applicable procurement rules;
  • At least ten (10) years of institutional experience in social work, social protection, capacity development, social services, or related fields;
  • Demonstrated experience in at least three (3) assignments of comparable complexity related to curriculum development, professional training systems, supervision, quality assurance, or evidence-based social interventions, collectively covering at least two of the above areas;
  • Demonstrated experience in providing technical assistance and adapting methodologies to different institutional and cultural contexts;
  • Experience working with government institutions and development partners;
  • Availability of sufficient technical, managerial, and administrative staff capacity to perform the assignment, together with internal quality assurance procedures.

Further information can be obtained through piuinsonprocurement@gmail.com during office hours from 09:00 to 17:00 Tashkent time.

Expressions of interest demonstrating relevant qualifications and experience must be delivered electronically to piuinsonprocurement@gmail.com by 25 September, 2026.
