Selection Method

Consultant’s Qualifications Based Selection (CQS)

 

The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), intends to engage a qualified consulting firm to support the preparation and implementation of an Aged Asset Replacement Program covering selected hydropower generation and power network assets.

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise the development of an Aged Asset Replacement Policy and Plan, identification and prioritisation of replacement projects, environmental and social screening and assessment, preparation of an implementation and procurement framework, and development of procurement documentation for the first batch of priority investments.

The Services will cover:

•    Review of EFL’s existing aged asset replacement policies and procedures, including risk evaluation and recommended improvements.

•    Stakeholder consultations and preparation of a stakeholder engagement plan aligned with applicable environmental and social requirements.

•    Development of a new Aged Asset Replacement Policy consistent with Good International Industry Practice and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework.

•    Assessment of the Wainiqeu and Nagado hydropower stations and the identified network substations, switchboards, transformers and related assets.

•    Project identification, prioritisation, cost estimates, economic analysis, environmental and social screening, risk classification and preparation of proportionate management instruments.

•    Development of a procurement strategy, technical specifications, bills of quantity and draft bidding documents, including relevant environmental and social provisions.

•    Knowledge transfer and training for relevant EFL personnel, together with a final implementation roadmap and recommendations.

 

Implementation period: The assignment is expected to be completed within thirty (30) weeks from the date of contract signing.

 

Terms of Reference: The detailed Terms of Reference are attached to this REOI as Appendix 1.

Energy Fiji Limited now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications and should clearly indicate whether the association is a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. Consultancy Services for Replacement of Ageing Assets

 

  1. Background and Context

Fiji's energy sector plays a central role in the economic development, investment in climate resilience renewable energy projects, and ensure long-term sustainability of the Fijian Economy. The country's electricity supply is dominated by Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), a majority owned government utility responsible for the generation, transmission, distribution, and retail of electricity. EFL currently produces approximately 93 percent of electricity, with Independent Power Producers (IPPs) contributing the remaining balance.

EFL is the primary electricity provider in Fiji, responsible for the generation, transmission, and retail of electricity across the four (4) main islands of Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Ovalau and Taveuni. Formerly known as the Fiji Electricity Authority (FEA) which was established under the Electricity Act in 1966, it was corporatized in 2018 to operate as a public company limited by shares.

 

Some of EFL’s major power generation assets (Renewable/thermal) have gone past their useful or replacement life due to their old age. The age of these generation assets is over 20 years or more. Some generators have long been out of production with spare parts no longer available or have become obsolete.

EFL has over the years worked on a number of projects to replace its ageing assets in both the Generation and Network Areas. Some were funded through debt funding and the remaining through EFL’s internal cashflow with progress subject to availability of funds.

The Government of Fiji (GoF), supported by the World Bank under the proposed Fiji Energy Transformation Project, is committed to assisting Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) in the implementation of EFL’s Aged Asset Replacement program, and the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) is used to support this ageing assets screening and preparation.

 

  1. Objective of the Assignment

The primary objectives of this consultancy are to:

  1. Develop an Aged Asset Replacement policy for EFL, aligned with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Standards (ESS);
  2. Establish an Aged Asset Replacement Plan; and
  3. Develop a framework for the implementation/procurement of the Aged Asset Replacement Plan in an efficient, cost-effective and transparent manner, aligned with the World Bank’s ESS.

The Aged Asset Replacement Policy should address the following:

  1. Facilitate broad interest in the implementation/procurement of the Aged Asset Replacement plan;
  2. Establish clear, transparent, and competitive procurement processes for the implementation of the Aged Asset Replacement Plan;
  3. Promote energy security and affordability for all Fijian consumers.
  4. Promote Good International Industry Practices (GIIP) in terms of environmental sustainability and social safeguards.

Specifically, the Consultancy should address the following:

  1. Identify ageing assets to be replaced or rehabilitated. A list is provided, with detailed information below.
  2. Promote energy-efficient replacement technologies
  3. Conduct a comprehensive E & S risk screening and assessment, including the corresponding mitigation measures / management plans, for all identified generation and substation upgrade, covering hazardous material handling, recovery (likelihood ACM in the switchboards, PCB and SF6 in the transformers etc.), waste disposal, emissions, and community impacts.
  4. Investment needs, and cost benefits analysis
  5. Facilitate broad interest in the implementation/procurement of the Aged Asset Replacement plan;
  6. Proposed implementation plan, including procurement packaging
  7. Draft bidding documents, BoQ and Technical Specifications, or other procurement documents.
  8. Promote energy security and affordability for all Fijian consumers including community safety awareness, emergency preparedness, and communication strategies to inform residents of planned outages or risks.

 

  1. Scope of Work

The aged assets include both aged hydropower stations and power network.

Two hydropower power stations are proposed to be assessed:

  1. Wainiqeu Hydro Power Station: Upgrade of Power Station and Equipment. Rehabilitate Penstock pipeline, weir and headpond
  2. Nagado Hydro Power Station: Upgrade of Power Station and Equipment. Rehabilitate Penstock pipeline, weir and headpond

  • Prepare a stakeholder engagement plan in accordance with ESS requirements.

  1. Required Qualifications and Expertise

The Consultant shall require a team with a combination of project management, contract management, and energy sector expertise. The core team should include:

Team Leader / Project Manager

  • Minimum 8 years of experience in managing social and gender related issues on energy projects.

  • Minimum 8 years of experience in financial analysis, cost estimation or financial modelling for power or infrastructure projects.
  • Experience supporting CAPEX/OPEX estimation and tender price evaluations for EPC or consultancy contracts.
  • Familiarity with taxation and payment structures for international consultancy services is desirable.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Procurement or related discipline.

Annex. E&S Screening, Risk Classification, and E&S Assessment and Management

 

E&S Screening and Risk Classification

As part of the project identification and prioritization process, the Consultant shall conduct an Environmental and Social (E&S) screening of all assets and sub-projects identified for potential inclusion under the Aged Asset Replacement Program. The purpose of this screening is to identify, at an early stage, the nature and significance of potential environmental and social risks and impacts associated with each sub-project, and to classify them accordingly to inform prioritization and downstream assessment requirements under Task 5.

The E&S screening shall be carried out in accordance with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and shall include the following activities:

(a) Screening Checklist Development. The Consultant shall develop a standardized E&S screening checklist, to be reviewed and approved by EFL and the World Bank, covering the following parameters for each sub-project or asset replacement activity:

  • Nature, scale, and location of the proposed asset replacement works (e.g., generation assets, transmission and distribution infrastructure, substations, switchboards, transformers, and hydropower plant components);
  • Proximity to environmentally sensitive areas, including watercourses, riparian zones, protected areas, forests, and ecologically significant habitats;
  • Proximity to communities, settlements, sacred sites, and areas of cultural heritage significance;
  • Land access requirements, including temporary or permanent land acquisition, easements, or restrictions on land use;
  • Potential for generation of hazardous waste, including oils, asbestos-containing materials (ACM), SF6 gas, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), and other legacy contaminants associated with aging electrical infrastructure;
  • Potential for impacts on labor and working conditions, occupational health and safety, and community health and safety during works; and
  • Potential for disproportionate impacts on vulnerable or marginalized groups, including women, youth, and indigenous communities.

(b) Application of the Screening Checklist. The Consultant shall apply the approved screening checklist to each sub-project or asset cluster identified in Task 4, drawing on available data, site reconnaissance findings, and stakeholder inputs gathered under Task 2. For hydropower-related asset replacements, the screening shall additionally assess:

  • The potential for works to alter water release regimes, turbine operations, or intake structures in ways that may affect downstream river flows, including environmental flows (eflows);
  • Potential impacts on aquatic ecosystems, freshwater biodiversity, and ecosystem services dependent on river flows; and
  • Any associated civil works within or adjacent to river corridors, including intake structures, penstocks, tailraces, and powerhouses.

(c) E&S Risk Classification. Based on the screening outcomes, the Consultant shall assign each sub-project or asset replacement activity a preliminary E&S risk classification consistent with the World Bank ESF risk categories (High, Substantial, Moderate, or Low). The classification shall consider both the type and scale of potential impacts and the sensitivity of the receiving environment and social context.

(d) Screening Report. The Consultant shall prepare an E&S Screening Report summarizing the results of the screening exercise for all sub-projects. The report shall include, for each sub-project: the completed screening checklist, the preliminary E&S risk classification, the rationale for the classification, and recommended E&S assessment and management measures required under Task 5. The Screening Report shall form an input to the Project Identification deliverable and shall be shared with EFL, the Ministry of Finance, and the World Bank for review and clearance prior to finalization.

The outcomes of the E&S screening shall directly inform the selection and sequencing of sub-projects for the first batch of implementation, ensuring that sub-projects with manageable E&S risks are prioritized, and that appropriate assessment and management measures are in place before procurement commences.

 

 

Environmental and Social Assessment and Management

Building on the E&S screening conducted under Task 4, the Consultant shall undertake Environmental and Social (E&S) assessments and prepare the corresponding management instruments for the sub-projects identified for the implementation under the Aged Asset Replacement Program. All assessments and instruments shall comply with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), applicable national environmental legislation of Fiji (including the Environment Management Act 2005 and associated regulations), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP).

    1. Scope and Approach

The E&S assessment shall cover all sub-projects in the first batch, as identified and screened under Task 4, including but not limited to:

  • Replacement of aged switchboards, transformers, and associated substation equipment across EFL's network;
  • Rehabilitation or replacement of generation assets at EFL's hydropower stations as identified under in the main text; and
  • Any associated civil, structural, or access works.

The scale and depth of assessment shall be proportionate to the E&S risk classification assigned to each sub-project under Task 4.

 

    1. Environmental and Social Assessment — Hydropower Asset Replacement

For asset replacement activities at hydropower stations, the Consultant shall prepare a standalone E&S assessment addressing the specific environmental and social sensitivities associated with hydropower infrastructure. The ESIA shall be prepared by qualified environmental and social specialists and shall include, at minimum, the following components:

 

(a) Description of the Existing Environment and Baseline Conditions

The Consultant shall compile and, where necessary, supplement existing baseline data to characterize the environmental and social baseline for each hydropower site and its area of influence, including:

  • Hydrology and water resources: river flow regimes, seasonal variability, historical discharge data, and existing water abstractions or diversions;
  • Aquatic ecology: species composition, abundance, and distribution of freshwater fish, macroinvertebrates, and other aquatic biota in rivers upstream and downstream of each facility;
  • Riparian and terrestrial ecology: vegetation communities, wildlife habitats, and any protected or endemic species in the project area;
  • Water quality: existing water quality conditions in receiving waterbodies;
  • Ecosystem services: identification and characterization of ecosystem services provided by river systems and dependent on flow regimes, including provisioning services (fisheries, water supply for downstream communities and agriculture), regulating services (flood attenuation, water purification), and cultural services (recreational, spiritual, and cultural values associated with rivers); and
  • Social baseline: communities and livelihoods dependent on river resources downstream of each facility, including subsistence fishing, smallholder irrigation, and cultural or ceremonial uses of water.

 

(b) Environmental Flow (E-Flow) Assessment

Given the small scale of the hydropower facility, the Consultant shall conduct a proportionate desktop E-flow review rather than a full E-flow assessment study. The review shall be commensurate with the nature of the asset replacement works and the associated level of hydrological risk.

The desktop review shall:

  • Document the existing operational flow regime at the facility, including any minimum flow release requirements specified in the facility's existing operating licence, consent conditions, or EFL operational procedures;
  • Confirm whether the proposed asset replacement works involve any physical changes to the intake structure, diversion weir, penstock, or tailrace that could alter the volume, timing, or continuity of water diverted or released — and if no such changes are proposed, note this explicitly as a basis for scoping out a detailed E-flow assessment;
  • Apply a simple hydrological desktop method — such as the Tennant (Montana) Method using available mean annual flow data — to provide a reference check on whether existing minimum flow releases at the facility are broadly consistent with accepted thresholds for maintaining basic ecological functions in the downstream river reach; and
  • Based on the above, conclude either that: (i) existing minimum flow provisions are adequate and no additional E-flow measures are required; or (ii) a gap exists that warrants a specific operational protocol or condition to be incorporated into the ESMP.

 

(c) Impact Assessment

The Consultant shall identify, predict, and evaluate the significance of potential environmental and social impacts associated with hydropower asset replacement works, covering both the construction and operational phases. Key impact pathways to be assessed shall include:

  • Changes to downstream flow regimes during works (e.g., dewatering, cofferdam installation, temporary flow diversion) and their effects on aquatic habitats, species, and ecosystem services;
  • Alteration of sediment transport and geomorphic processes resulting from changes to turbine operation or intake structures;
  • Impacts on aquatic biodiversity, particularly fish passage and migration, arising from works at intake or tailrace structures;
  • Risks of water quality degradation from construction activities, including turbidity, sedimentation, and potential release of oils, lubricants, or hazardous materials;
  • Hazardous waste generation and management, including oils, asbestos-containing materials, PCBs, SF6 gas, and other materials associated with aged electrical and mechanical equipment;
  • Community health and safety risks
  • Impacts on downstream communities dependent on river-based livelihoods and ecosystem services.

 

    1. Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs)

The Consultant shall prepare ESMPs for each sub-project in the first batch, integrating findings from the E&S assessment (for hydropower facilities) and the E&S screening assessments. The ESMPs shall:

  • Describe, for each identified impact, the proposed hierarchy of mitigation measures (avoidance, minimization, mitigation, and compensation or offset where residual impacts remain);
  • Include specific management measures for: hazardous waste handling and disposal (oils, ACM, PCBs, SF6); erosion and sediment control during civil works; hydropower operational protocols to maintain E-flows during construction phases; worker health and safety; community health and safety;
  • Specify monitoring requirements, including parameters to be monitored, monitoring locations, frequency, responsible parties, and reporting arrangements, with particular attention to downstream aquatic ecology and water quality monitoring at hydropower sites;
  • Define institutional responsibilities for ESMP implementation, supervision, and reporting within EFL;
  • Include a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) consistent with World Bank ESF requirements, covering all project-affected communities; and
  • Include an estimated budget for ESMP implementation.

 

    1. Stakeholder Engagement and Disclosure

In coordination with Task 2, the Consultant shall support EFL in conducting targeted stakeholder consultations on the E&S assessment and ESMP findings for each sub-project. Consultations shall be conducted in accordance with the Stakeholder Engagement Plan developed under Task 2, and shall be culturally appropriate and accessible to women, indigenous communities, and other vulnerable groups. Consultation records, including attendance, issues raised, and responses, shall be documented and appended to the ESIA and ESMP.

 

    1. Integration of E&S Requirements into Bidding Documents

The Consultant shall work closely with the procurement specialist engaged for Task 6 to ensure that all relevant E&S requirements are systematically integrated into the bidding documents for the asset replacement sub-projects. This shall include:

(a) E&S Specifications and Requirements. The Consultant shall prepare an Environmental and Social Requirements (ESR) section to be included within the bidding documents for each contract package, covering: Contractor obligations with respect to ESMP implementation, including preparation and submission of a Contractor Environmental and Social Management Plan (C-ESMP) prior to commencement of works; specific technical requirements for hazardous waste management (oils, ACM, PCBs, SF6, and other hazardous materials from aged equipment), including approved disposal or recycling methods, handling procedures, and documentation requirements;

(b) E&S Performance Standards in Contract Conditions. The Consultant shall recommend appropriate contract conditions and performance standards to ensure contractor compliance with E&S requirements, including provisions for: submission and approval of the C-ESMP as a condition precedent to commencement of works; regular E&S reporting by the contractor;  and consequences for non-compliance, including stop-work orders and financial remedies.

(c) E&S Rated Criteria. The Consultant shall recommend criteria for evaluating contractor E&S capacity and performance as part of the qualification and evaluation criteria for each bidding package, covering contractor experience with E&S management on similar infrastructure projects, availability of qualified E&S personnel, and approach to hazardous materials management.

Sincerely,

 

Nguyen Duc Phong

rows.notice_text:
REPÚBLICA DEL ECUADOR

MINISTERIO DE INFRAESTRUCTURA Y TECNOLOGÍA - MIT

“PROYECTO DE VIVIENDA Y DESARROLLO URBANO INCLUSIVOS Y

RESILIENTES EN ECUADOR”

CONTRATO DE PRÉSTAMO BIRF 9598-EC

SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS PARA LA “ELABORACIÓN DEL

DISEÑO URBANO-ARQUITECTÓNICO DEFINITIVO DE LA PRIMERA INICIATIVA BARRIAL (OBRA DE CONFIANZA), LA ELABORACIÓN DE LA AGENDA BARRIAL Y LA ELABORACIÓN DEL DISEÑO URBANO-ARQUITECTÓNICO DEFINITIVO DE LA OBRA PRIORIZADA, BARRIO LAS ACACIAS (GADM MANTA)”.

CÓDIGO DE REFERENCIA: EC-MIT-555609-CS-QCBS

 

La República de Ecuador ha recibido un Préstamo del Banco Mundial para el financiamiento del “PROYECTO DE VIVIENDA Y DESARROLLO URBANO INCLUSIVOS Y RESILIENTES EN ECUADOR”, y parte de los recursos de ese préstamo serán destinados a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

 

La presente consultoría se enmarca en el objetivo general del Componente 2 y se ejecuta dentro del Subcomponente 2.2, como parte del Programa de Mejoramiento Integral de Barrios (MIB), el cual tiene como finalidad mejorar la calidad de vida de la población residente en los barrios priorizados, mediante la implementación, ampliación y mejora del espacio público y la infraestructura urbana, la reducción de la vulnerabilidad frente a amenazas naturales y climáticas, y la promoción de procesos de participación comunitaria que fortalezcan la cohesión social y la apropiación del entorno urbano.

Como resultado de la implementación del Programa de Mejoramiento Integral de Barrios (MIB), se generan productos técnicos y operativos que estructuran la intervención integral a escala barrial, entre los cuales se incluyen:

 

  1. Primera Iniciativa Barrial (Obra de Confianza): Obra definida por el barrio en un proceso participativo, es una construcción de rápida y fácil ejecución, de alto impacto social que demuestra compromiso entre residentes, actores locales, GAD y ahora el Ministerio de Infraestructura y Tecnología (MIT), cuyo propósito es generar confianza y entusiasmo, mientras avanza la Agenda Barrial.
  2. Agenda Barrial: La Agenda Barrial es un instrumento técnico-social estratégico de planificación territorial a escala barrial, elaborado de manera participativa con la población, el Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado, el ahora Ministerio de Infraestructura y Tecnología (MIT) y otros actores locales.

 

Este instrumento define la hoja de ruta para el desarrollo integral del barrio en el corto, mediano y largo plazo, mediante la identificación y priorización de las necesidades del territorio, e incorpora mecanismos de gobernanza local a través de procesos metodológicos adaptados a contextos de vulnerabilidad climática, riesgos naturales y exclusión social.

 

Asimismo, la Agenda Barrial permite la elaboración de diagnósticos urbano- arquitectónico y social, la identificación de riesgos, oportunidades y necesidades, y la priorización participativa de soluciones de hábitat que orientan una hoja de ruta técnica, para la inversión pública, constituyéndose en un insumo para la ejecución posterior de estudios, diseños y obras físicas que determinará un portafolio de proyectos conforme el Hito de Implementación – Paso 8, Elaboración de la Agenda Barrial del Manual Operativo del Proyecto (MOP).

  • Portafolio de proyectos: es un listado de proyectos dentro del polígono barrial específico y su entorno inmediato que han sido identificados, analizados y priorizados participativamente en el desarrollo de la Agenda Barrial. Es una herramienta que contiene fichas técnicas de cada proyecto en las cuales indica información pertinente como ubicación, presupuesto estimado, justificación, importancia, viabilidad y el impacto que genera, así como, el diseño del proyecto a nivel de idea, incluyendo el contenido mínimo establecido en la ficha técnica adjunta (Anexo 10).
  1. Obra Priorizada: Obra definida por el barrio en un proceso participativo, es una obra de mayor escala, que materializa la visión definida por la comunidad e identificada en el proceso de la Agenda Barrial, busca cumplir todos los objetivos del Programa de Mejoramiento Integral de Barrios (MIB).

El alcance, la metodología e hitos del presente proceso se encuentran determinados en el término de referencia y sus anexos.

Los términos de referencia detallados para la presente consultoría podrán consultarse en el siguiente enlace: https://www.mit.gob.ec/postulaciones/

El MIT, invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles (“Consultores”) a manifestar sus expresiones de interés en la prestación de los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deberán proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para realizar los Servicios.

La presente contratación está dirigida a firmas consultoras o asociaciones de firmas legalmente constituidas, con experiencia demostrable en estudios urbanos, diseño urbano–arquitectónico, gestión y participación social y formulación de instrumentos de planificación participativa a escala barrial o urbana.

La firma consultora deberá:

  1. Estar legalmente constituida y habilitada para prestar servicios de consultoría en el país, de conformidad con la normativa vigente.
  2. Acreditar experiencia general en la ejecución de estudios o consultorías vinculadas a planificación urbana, mejoramiento barrial, diseño urbano–arquitectónico, gestión y participación social y/o proyectos de inversión en hábitat y vivienda.
  3. Acreditar experiencia específica en al menos uno de los siguientes ámbitos:
  • Proyectos de mejoramiento integral de barrios u operaciones similares.
  • Formulación participativa de agendas barriales, planes o programas a escala barrial o urbana.
  • Estudios y diseños definitivos de espacio público, equipamientos comunitarios o intervenciones urbanas en contextos similares al barrio.
  1. Preferentemente, acreditar experiencia previa en proyectos financiados por organismos multilaterales (Banco Mundial u otros), o en proyectos con requerimientos de salvaguardas socioambientales y enfoques transversales similares.

Los criterios para la selección de la lista corta son los siguientes:

Experiencia mínima exigida para la firma consultora

Tipo

Descripción

Monito mínimo por proyecto

Experiencia general

 

Experiencia general. de diseño participativo; proyectos de mejoramiento integral de barrios con componentes sociales y urbanos; proyectos urbanos temporales o planificados con las comunidades; planes de ordenamiento barrial o esquemas urbanos comunitarios; modelos de gestión.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Name of Project

Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499) - Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP)

Loan No/Credit No/Grant Number

GFPP Grant No. TF0D0728

Assignment Title

International Environmental and Social (E&S) Specialist

Procurement Plan Ref Number

FJ-EFL-567224-CS-INDV

Reference No.

EOI-04/2026

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

 

The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of preparing the Fiji Energy Transformation Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise specialist environmental and social support to EFL's Project Preparation Unit. The Consultant will lead preparation of appraisal-stage environmental and social instruments, integrate requirements of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework into technical and procurement outputs, support policy and regulatory reviews, and prepare a procurement-ready terms of reference for a separate assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional Environmental and Social Management System.

 

The Services will cover:

• general environmental and social support to the Project Preparation Unit, including screening, risk-register management, ESCP inputs, coordination and practical capacity building;

• preparation of E&S scoping studies with critical-habitat screening, a site-specific ESMP for aging asset replacement, an RPF, negotiated land agreement due diligence, an integrated SEP, and LMP;

• preparation of a procurement-ready TOR for development and operationalization of EFL's institutional ESMS;

• environmental and social review of Electricity Act amendments, Rooftop Solar PV Policy, and private-sector renewable-energy participation;

• E&S inputs to the National control-centre upgrade, , aging power-infrastructure, grid-interconnection, hydropower and solar PV/BESS studies and concept designs; and

• monthly and quarterly reporting, disclosure support and an appraisal-stage E&S readiness summary.

 

Implementation period: The assignment is expected to be part-time for the full GFPP implementation period, estimated at [24 months], subject to satisfactory performance and availability of GFPP financing.

 

Terms of Reference: The detailed Terms of Reference are attached to this REOI as Appendix 1.

 

Energy Fiji Limited now invites eligible individual consultants ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the applicable provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers concerning conflict of interest.

 

EOI Evaluation Criteria

Criterion

Weight

1. Relevant E&S assessment and management experience for infrastructure or energy projects

25%

2. Demonstrated application of the World Bank ESF or IFC Performance Standards and preparation of ESMP, land/resettlement, SEP/GRM and LMP instruments

30%

3. Experience in biodiversity and critical-habitat screening, ESS5 land due diligence, and ESS7 engagement and FPIC

20%

4. Relevant renewable-energy, grid infrastructure, hazardous-materials, Pacific or Fiji experience, including familiarity with iTaukei land tenure and governance

15%

5. Qualifications, writing, coordination, consultation and capacity-building capability

10%

Total

100%

 

Form and content of the Expression of Interest:

Expressions of interest should contain only the information necessary to assess the criteria above. Consultants should submit a curriculum vitae and a concise statement demonstrating relevant assignments and experience.

A financial proposal is not required at this stage.

The Consultant assessed as best qualified against the criteria will be invited to negotiate a contract in accordance with the applicable procurement arrangements.

Submission

Further information may be obtained by emailing tenders@efl.com.fj during office hours, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM Fiji Time, Monday to Friday, no later than three clear days before the closing date.

Expressions of interest must be uploaded to the EFL e-Tender Portal (TenderLink) at https://www.tenderlink.com/efl by registering your company, by 4:00 PM (1600 hrs) Fiji Time on Wednesday, 30th September 2026.

EOI documents may be viewed and downloaded from www.efl.com.fj(opens in new window) or https://www.tenderlink.com/efl(opens in new window).

Submissions by email or facsimile will not be accepted. Hard-copy submissions to the tender box at EFL Head Office, Suva, will not be accepted.

 

 

Appendix 1 - Terms of Reference

TERMS OF REFERENCE

INTERNATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL (E&S) SPECIALIST

Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499)

Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) - Energy Fiji Limited (EFL)

1. Introduction and Background

Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) is preparing the Fiji Energy Transformation Project (P518499), a World Bank-supported initiative estimated at USD 230 million. The project aims to accelerate renewable-energy development, modernize the power grid, rehabilitate aging infrastructure, and reform the power sector to attract private investment in solar energy. Key interventions span Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni, including solar PV/BESS parks of more than 50 MW each, grid-evacuation infrastructure, transmission-line upgrades and modernization of existing power stations.

The Initial Environmental and Social Review Summary has classified the project's environmental and social risks as Substantial, reflecting biodiversity impacts, customary iTaukei land tenure, community health and safety, labor influx, SEA/SH risks, and supply-chain concerns associated with PV modules and battery energy storage systems.

EFL is establishing a Project Preparation Unit (PPU) to prepare the project for appraisal and Board approval. The E&S Specialist will lead preparation of required E&S instruments, integrate E&S requirements into technical and procurement outputs, and prepare the TOR for a separate capacity-building assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional ESMS.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The objective is to ensure that GFPP-financed preparation activities and the investments they support comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework, the project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, applicable Fiji law, and Good International Industry Practice.

3. Scope of Work

The Consultant will perform the following tasks, organized into five functional areas:

3.1 General E&S Support to the PPU

• Serve as the PPU's E&S focal point and advise the Project Manager and technical teams on application of the ESF.

• Screen preparation activities and concept designs, identify applicable standards and instruments, and maintain an E&S Risk Register with actions, responsibilities and status.

• Prepare ESCP inputs, TORs for specialized studies, and E&S requirements for technical specifications and bidding documents; oversee related consultant outputs.

• Provide practical ESF training and on-the-job support to the PPU and relevant EFL staff.

• Coordinate with the World Bank, relevant Fiji agencies, TLTB, technical consultants and EFL departments, and maintain records of key decisions and actions.

3.2 Preparation of E&S Instruments Required by Appraisal

This is the most critical function of the assignment. The E&S Specialist will prepare the following appraisal-stage instruments and related outputs:

a. E&S Scoping Studies with Critical Habitat Screening

• Lead scoping studies for solar PV/BESS parks on Vanua Levu and Taveuni, grid-evacuation infrastructure, and new or upgraded transmission lines.

• Conduct structured Critical Habitat screening under ESS6 using available biodiversity data, including IUCN Red List species, Fiji endemic avifauna information, and protected-area registries.

• Where critical habitat is identified or cannot be ruled out, prepare detailed assessments and, where necessary, a Biodiversity Management Plan with offset strategies, no-go zones and seasonal restrictions.

• Include baseline social surveys, land-tenure mapping, community presence, vulnerable-group identification, and climate-resilience considerations such as cyclone, flooding and sea-level-rise risks.

b. Environmental and Social Management Plan - Aging Asset Replacement

• Prepare a site-specific ESMP for rehabilitation and replacement of aging power infrastructure under Component 3, covering baseline conditions, construction and operational risks, hazardous materials including PCBs, asbestos and e-waste, mitigation, monitoring, emergency response, contractor requirements, responsibilities, schedules and costs.

c. Resettlement Policy Framework

• Prepare an RPF consistent with ESS5 covering legal and institutional arrangements and gap analysis; eligibility and cut-off dates; entitlements and replacement-cost valuation; livelihood restoration; procedures for site-specific plans; consultation and grievance arrangements; monitoring, responsibilities and budget provisions.

d. Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence Report

• Identify and document all project sites or corridors where land or access rights have been or may be secured through negotiated settlement or other voluntary arrangement, and verify consistency with ESS5 and Fiji law.

• Prepare an inventory of leases, easements, access and land-use agreements, donations, transfers and other consensual arrangements, recording parcels, rights-holders, status, duration, consideration, benefits and supporting evidence.

• Assess whether each arrangement is voluntary, transparent, informed and free from coercion; whether formal, informal, customary, secondary and shared rights-holders were identified and represented; and whether participants had sufficient information, time, advice and a genuine right to refuse.

• For customary land and resources, screen whether ESS7 and FPIC apply. Where required, document a culturally appropriate collective process through institutions selected by affected iTaukei communities, with participation of women, youth and potentially excluded rights-holders. Do not infer FPIC solely from approvals by TLTB, agencies or individual owners.

• Where applicable, confirm and document eligibility cut-off dates, culturally appropriate public notice, valuation and compensation or benefit methodology, replacement-cost consistency, implementation status, grievances and corrective actions.

• Conclude for each arrangement whether ESS5 criteria are demonstrated and identify any additional instrument, remedial action, responsible party and completion deadline required before access or civil works.

e. Integrated Stakeholder Engagement Plan

• Prepare a project-level SEP consistent with ESS10, including stakeholder analysis, differentiated engagement for disadvantaged or vulnerable groups, disclosure, responsibilities, schedule, monitoring and reporting.

• Include a culturally appropriate consultation plan for communities potentially affected by solar PV/BESS and associated infrastructure, covering languages, timing, representation, feedback, land arrangements, benefit sharing and any ESS7 FPIC process.

• Establish an accessible project grievance mechanism and a confidential, survivor-centered SEA/SH reporting and referral pathway.

f. Labor Management Procedures

• Prepare LMP consistent with ESS2 for direct, contracted, community and primary supply workers, including applicable law and gaps, terms and conditions, OHS, emergency preparedness, accommodation, labor influx, child and forced labor, PV/BESS supply-chain due diligence, codes of conduct, worker grievances, contractor obligations and training.

g. TOR for Development and Operationalization of EFL's ESMS

• Prepare a procurement-ready TOR and supporting inputs for a separate assignment to develop and operationalize EFL's institutional ESMS including potential staffing and structure to ensure the ESMS is properly resourced, strategically aligned, and embedded within EFL for lasting effectiveness.

• Define objectives, scope, methodology, deliverables, schedule, expertise, coordination, knowledge transfer and acceptance criteria. Cover policy and governance; screening; stakeholder, labor, land, biodiversity, pollution, community-safety, cultural-heritage, contractor and supply-chain management; incident response; monitoring; reporting; tools; templates; training; and a time-bound implementation plan.

• Consult relevant EFL departments. This assignment does not include development or implementation of the ESMS.

3.3 Policy and Regulatory Support

• Review proposed amendments to Fiji's Electricity Act from an E&S perspective, identify gaps with the World Bank ESF and international good practice, and recommend measures for the revised policy.

• Review the proposed Rooftop Solar PV Policy from an E&S perspective, including potential effects on consumers, community uptake and grid workers.

• Advise on E&S requirements for private-sector renewable-energy participation, including application of IFC Performance Standards and World Bank ESF requirements to PPP or private-investment components.

• Assess EFL's potential for an Environmental and Social Policy and support EFL's E&S team to derive and implement a practical policy.

3.4 E&S Inputs to Technical Studies and Infrastructure Components

• National Control Center Upgrade: identify E&S risks associated with civil works, OHS, asbestos and PCBs, and recommend mitigation for technical specifications.

• Modernization of Nabouwalu Government Station: conduct site-specific screening, identify community-proximity, worker-community and hazardous-material risks, and prepare an ESMP if required.

• Aging Infrastructure Rehabilitation: supplement the Component 3 ESMP with screening and, where feasible, inspection of all proposed sub-sites for hazardous materials, cultural heritage and social risks.

• Power Grid Interconnection, Vanua Levu-Taveuni: support feasibility and engineering studies with environmental and social routing-alternatives analysis and identification of a preferred route based on E&S criteria.

• Hydropower: prepare assessment TOR requirements covering direct, indirect, induced and cumulative life-cycle impacts across the relevant catchment, including flows, sediment, biodiversity, ecosystem services, water use, livelihoods, land, safety, cultural heritage, associated facilities, alternatives, mitigation, monitoring and adaptive management.

• Solar PV/BESS Parks: provide E&S inputs to concept designs for two parks of more than 50 MW each, including environmentally and socially informed site-selection criteria and ESF compliance review.

3.5 Monitoring, Reporting and Disclosure

• Submit monthly E&S progress reports covering instrument preparation, risk-register actions, engagement, grievances, emerging issues and preparation-phase ESCP commitments.

• Prepare quarterly stakeholder-engagement summaries.

• Coordinate disclosure through EFL and other required channels and make accessible copies available to affected communities.

• Prepare an appraisal-stage E&S readiness summary recording instrument status, review, disclosure, outstanding actions and post-appraisal timelines.

4. Methodology

• Desktop review of project, legal, technical and E&S documentation and available baseline data.

• Structured screening, site visits and physical inspections where feasible.

• Stakeholder consultations with EFL, government agencies, TLTB, affected communities, technical consultants and the World Bank.

• Application of the World Bank ESF, ESCP, applicable Fiji law, GIIP and the mitigation hierarchy.

• Iterative preparation, review and revision of instruments, with clear evidence trails, action tracking and quality assurance.

• Practical knowledge transfer and on-the-job support to EFL and PPU personnel.

5. Key Deliverables

All deliverables shall be submitted in English, professionally edited, and formatted in accordance with any World Bank templates provided.

6. Reporting and Coordination

The E&S Specialist will report to the PPU Project Manager on a day-to-day basis. For technical E&S matters, the Specialist will coordinate closely with World Bank E&S Specialists and participate in World Bank supervision missions and project-preparation meetings.

The Specialist will also coordinate with:

• EFL's full-time Environmental Officer and Social Officer, once recruited;

• GFPP technical consultants in engineering, energy and finance;

• iTaukei Land Trust Board on land-tenure and customary-engagement matters;

• Department of Environment and other relevant Fiji government agencies; and

• external E&S consultants engaged for specialized studies.

7. Required Qualifications and Experience

7.1 Education

• University degree, at minimum Bachelor's level, in environmental science, social science, natural-resource management, engineering or a closely related field. A postgraduate qualification in environmental or social assessment is strongly preferred.

7.2 Professional Experience

• At least seven years of relevant experience in E&S assessment and management for infrastructure or energy projects.

• Demonstrated application of the World Bank ESF or IFC Performance Standards and preparation of ESMPs, land or resettlement instruments, SEPs/GRMs and LMPs.

• Experience in biodiversity and critical-habitat screening, ESS5 land and resettlement due diligence, and ESS7 engagement and FPIC.

• Experience with hazardous materials, renewable energy, grid infrastructure or power generation is desirable.

• Pacific or Fiji experience, including familiarity with iTaukei land tenure and governance, is strongly preferred.

• Strong writing, coordination, consultation and capacity-building skills in multicultural settings.

8. Duration and Location

• Duration: Part-time for the full GFPP implementation period, estimated at [24 months], subject to satisfactory performance and GFPP availability.

• Location: Remote-based, with regular travel to project sites on Vanua Levu, Taveuni and other islands as required for scoping, consultation and supervision.

Reference No.: NP-MOALD-568188-CS-QCBS- PMU - YR3

 

The Government of Nepal has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Food and Nutrition Security Enhancement Project II (FANSEP II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include ENDLINE SURVEY of FANSEP II project implementation in 16 rural municipalities of 8 project districts.  The Endline Survey will, to the extent possible, revisit same households surveyed during the Baseline Survey, to construct a panel dataset that permits before-after (baseline-endline) and treatment-comparison (with-without) impact analysis. The baseline sample comprised 1,750 treatment households (5% of 35,000 households project coverage) and 750 comparison households, totaling 2,500 households. The Endline Survey will target the same panel of 2,500 households.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment and checklist of documents to be submitted can be downloaded from the website https://fansep.moald.gov.np/notice-board/

 

Food and Nutrition Security Enhancement Project II now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) (including joint ventures) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: firms general and specific experience of conducting study by collecting data from big sample size using electronic devices and analyze it to prepare report having at least 3 years long experience in consulting services (of each partner, in case of JV) with managerial capacity. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 9:00-17:00 hours on office days.

REPUBLIQUE DU NIGER

Fraternité – Travail – Progrès

MINISTERE DE L’AGRICULTURE ET DE L’ELEVAGE

 

PROJET D’APPUI AU DEVELOPPEMENT DES CULTURES IRRIGUEES ET A L’INTENSISIFICATION DE LA PRODUCTION ANIMALE (PACIPA)

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET OU GROUPEMENT DE CABINETS POUR LA MISE EN OEUVRE DE SIX (6) PLANS D’ACTION DE REINSTALLATION DE SOUS PROJETS DE REHABILITATION ET D’AMENAGEMENT HYDRO AGRICOLE DANS LES REGIONS DE ZINDER ET DIFFA

 

Crédit IDA N° 76070-NE

 

N° de référence : NE-LAMP-565743-CS-CQS

 

Cet Avis à Manifestations d’intérêt fait suite à la publication de l’Avis Général de Passation des Marchés (AGPM) publié sur le site de la Banque Mondiale le 05 Août 2025 et sur le Sahel Dimanche du 08 Août 2025.

1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger a sollicité un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour financer le Projet d’Appui au développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant du financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET OU GROUPEMENT DE CABINETS POUR LA MISE EN OEUVRE DE SIX (6) PLANS D’ACTION DE REINSTALLATION DE SOUS PROJETS DE REHABILITATION ET D’AMENAGEMENT HYDRO AGRICOLE DANS LES REGIONS DE ZINDER ET DIFFA.

2. Les services du Consultant (« Services ») comprennent : lire plus bas les Termes de référence.

Objet et objectifs de la prestation

Objet

La mission a pour objet d’appuyer le PACIPA dans la mise en œuvre complète, transparente, inclusive et traçable des six PAR, jusqu’à la production des rapports d’achèvement et à la documentation de la libération des emprises, sans se substituer aux décisions et responsabilités régaliennes de l’État ni à l’obligation de paiement du Projet.

Objectifs spécifiques

Il s’agit plus spécifiquement de :

  • préparer et opérationnaliser le dispositif de mise en œuvre sur chaque site ;
  • informer et consulter les PAP et les autres parties prenantes dans des formats et langues accessibles ;
  • Préparer les dossiers individuels des PAP ;
  • vérifier, mettre à jour et sécuriser les bases de données et dossiers individuels des PAP, sans rouvrir arbitrairement l’éligibilité ;
  • accompagner la formalisation des ententes, la gestion des cas particuliers et la constitution des pièces administratives ;
  • appuyer le PACIPA et les structures compétentes pendant les opérations de compensation et assurer leur traçabilité ;
  • rendre opérationnels les comités locaux de réinstallation et le mécanisme de gestion des plaintes ;
  • assurer un accompagnement spécifique des personnes vulnérables et la prise en compte du genre, de l’EAS/HS et de la sécurité ;
  • documenter la restauration des moyens de subsistance prévue par les PAR et produire les rapports d’achèvement par site.

3. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet d’Appui au développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA) invite les consultants admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressées doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

 

Les qualifications du Cabinet ou groupement des cabinets :

  1. Contexte et justification

Le Gouvernement de la République du Niger, avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale, met en œuvre le Projet d’Appui au Développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA). Le Projet vise à accroître la productivité, la commercialisation et la résilience climatique des productions agricoles et pastorales. Il intervient notamment à travers la réhabilitation et l’aménagement de périmètres hydro-agricoles.

Ces investissements peuvent entraîner des pertes de terres, d’actifs ou de moyens de subsistance. Six Plans d’Action de Réinstallation (PAR) ont ainsi été préparés pour les sites de Harpa, Kakibaré, Kidikidiram, N’Guel Djaobol, Karmakawa et N’Gor Guidiyé. Leur mise en œuvre doit respecter la législation nationale, les instruments environnementaux et sociaux du PACIPA et la Norme environnementale et sociale n°5 (NES 5) de la Banque mondiale.

Compte tenu du nombre de personnes affectées, de la dispersion géographique des sites et de la sensibilité des opérations de compensation, le PACIPA souhaite mobiliser un cabinet ou un groupement de cabinets disposant d’une expérience démontrée dans la mise en œuvre opérationnelle de PAR complexes, particulièrement en contexte rural et hydro-agricole.

  1. Présentation du PACIPA

Le PACIPA est financé à hauteur de 350 millions de dollars pour sa première phase. Il couvre les régions de Diffa, Dosso, Maradi, Tahoua, Tillabéri et Zinder et s’articule autour des composantes suivantes :

Composante 1 : renforcement de la production agricole et pastorale résiliente ;

Composante 2 : amélioration des marchés agricoles et du bétail ;

Composante 3 : facilitation de l’accès au financement ;

Composante 4 : coordination, gestion et renforcement institutionnel ;

Composante 5 : intervention d’urgence (CERC).

  1. Objet et objectifs de la prestation
    1. Objet

La mission a pour objet d’appuyer le PACIPA dans la mise en œuvre complète, transparente, inclusive et traçable des six PAR, jusqu’à la production des rapports d’achèvement et à la documentation de la libération des emprises, sans se substituer aux décisions et responsabilités régaliennes de l’État ni à l’obligation de paiement du Projet.

    1. Objectifs spécifiques de la prestation

Il s’agit plus spécifiquement de :

  • Préparer et opérationnaliser le dispositif de mise en œuvre sur chaque site ;
  • Informer et consulter les PAP et les autres parties prenantes dans des formats et langues accessibles ;
  • Préparer les dossiers individuels des PAP ;
  • Vérifier, mettre à jour et sécuriser les bases de données et dossiers individuels des PAP, sans rouvrir arbitrairement l’éligibilité ;
  • Accompagner la formalisation des ententes, la gestion des cas particuliers et la constitution des pièces administratives ;
  • Appuyer le PACIPA et les structures compétentes pendant les opérations de compensation et assurer leur traçabilité ;
  • Rendre opérationnels les comités locaux de réinstallation et le mécanisme de gestion des plaintes ;
  • Assurer un accompagnement spécifique des personnes vulnérables et la prise en compte du genre, de l’EAS/HS et de la sécurité ;
  • Documenter la restauration des moyens de subsistance prévue par les PAR et produire les rapports d’achèvement par site.

 

  1. Étendus de la prestation et tâches

5.1 Phase de démarrage et appropriation

  • Analyser les six PAR, leurs bases de données, les instruments du PACIPA, les observations de validation et la documentation foncière disponible ;
  • Réaliser une revue de cohérence des listes de PAP, biens affectés, montants, vulnérabilités et pièces justificatives ;
  • Préparer une méthodologie, un plan de déploiement multi-sites, une matrice des risques, un protocole de protection des données et un chronogramme détaillé ;
  • Établir les modalités de coordination avec l’UGP, les UCR, les autorités, le Code rural, l’ONAHA, le BNEE et les autres services concernés.

5.2 Information, consultation et mobilisation

  • Élaborer et mettre en œuvre un plan de communication adapté aux langues et réalités locales ;
  • Divulguer les informations essentielles des PAR : droits, critères, barèmes, calendrier, voies de recours et contacts du mécanisme de gestion de plaintes ;
  • Organiser les consultations, réunions publiques et séances ciblées avec les femmes, jeunes, personnes handicapées et autres groupes vulnérables ;
  • Tenir des registres de participation désagrégés et documenter les préoccupations et réponses apportées.

5.3 Actualisation et sécurisation des dossiers des PAP

  • Contrôler l’identité, les coordonnées, les actifs, les montants et le statut de chaque PAP ;
  • Mettre à jour les changements survenus depuis la date butoir (décès, succession, procuration, incapacité, erreur matérielle), selon une procédure validée par le PACIPA ;
  • Accompagner, lorsque nécessaire, les audiences foraines pour l’établissement des CIN et la délivrance des pièces administratives ;
  • Constituer un dossier individuel complet, une fiche d’entente et une piste d’audit pour chaque PAP ;
  • Mettre en place une base sécurisée, interopérable et assortie d’un registre des modifications.

5.4 Structures locales, conciliation et gestion des plaintes

  • Mettre en place ou redynamiser les CLR ou CAC, CGP et autres instances prévues, puis former leurs membres ;
  • Enregistrer, catégoriser, traiter et suivre les plaintes dans les délais du MGP ;
  • Orienter immédiatement et de manière confidentielle les plaintes sensibles, notamment EAS/HS, vers les mécanismes appropriés ;
  • Appuyer les sessions de conciliation et, le cas échéant, les travaux des commissions administratives compétentes, sans exercer leurs prérogatives ;
  • Produire un tableau de bord des plaintes, décisions, délais et taux de clôture.

5.5 Compensation, accompagnement et libération des emprises

  • Préparer les listes de paiement contrôlées et les dossiers nécessaires à l’opérateur de paiement ;
  • Informer individuellement les PAP et organiser leur mobilisation dans des conditions sûres et dignes ;
  • Observer et documenter les paiements, les échecs de transaction, les absences et les cas litigieux ;
  • S’assurer que les compensations et mesures d’assistance sont réalisées avant la prise de possession des terres et le démarrage des travaux concernés ;
  • Appuyer le suivi des mesures de restauration des moyens de subsistance et l’assistance aux personnes vulnérables ;
  • Documenter la libération volontaire et régulière des emprises, sans coercition.

5.6 Clôture et capitalisation

  • Réconcilier les données des PAR, dossiers individuels, paiements et plaintes ;
  • Identifier les écarts résiduels et proposer un plan d’actions correctives assorti de responsables et délais ;
  • Produire les rapports d’achèvement par site et un rapport consolidé de mission ;
  • Transférer au PACIPA l’intégralité des bases, pièces, supports et outils dans des formats ouverts et exploitables.

6. Résultats attendus

  • R1. Le dispositif de mise en œuvre, de coordination, de communication et de gestion des risques est opérationnel sur les six sites.
  • R2. Toutes les PAP sont informées de leurs droits, des montants, du calendrier et des voies de recours dans un format accessible.
  • R3. Les bases de données et dossiers individuels sont contrôlés, actualisés, sécurisés et traçables.
  • R4. Les structures locales de réinstallation et le mécanisme de plaintes sont fonctionnels et documentés.
  • R5. Les compensations et mesures d’assistance sont suivies, rapprochées et documentées avant libération des emprises.
  • R6. Les personnes vulnérables et les cas particuliers reçoivent un accompagnement adapté.
  • R7. Les écarts résiduels sont identifiés et traités à travers un plan d’actions correctives validé.
  • R8. Les rapports d’achèvement par site et le rapport consolidé sont validés par le PACIPA et, lorsque requis, par la Banque mondiale.

Obligation de résultat organisationnel : La connaissance préalable d’un site ou du PACIPA n’est pas exigée. Le Consultant doit toutefois démontrer sa capacité à être opérationnel rapidement, à reprendre des bases existantes et à assurer un transfert complet et sécurisé des données.

 

9. Responsabilités des parties

9.1 Responsabilités du Consultant

Les responsabilités dévolues au consultant sont :

  • Mobiliser à temps le personnel, les équipements et la logistique prévus dans son offre ;
  • Assurer la qualité, la cohérence et la confidentialité des données ;
  • Faciliter l’identification des huissiers de justice par département afin de superviser les opérations de paiement ;
  • Respecter la NES 5, les autres NES pertinentes, la législation nationale, le code de conduite et les exigences EAS/HS du Projet ;
  • Ne prendre aucun engagement financier ou juridique au nom du PACIPA sans mandat écrit ;
  • Signaler sans délai tout risque de coercition, conflit, fraude, double paiement, atteinte à la sécurité ou violation de données ;
  • Remettre tous les livrables, justificatifs et fichiers sources au PACIPA.

9.2 Responsabilités du PACIPA

Les responsabilités du PACIPA sont :

  • Mettre à disposition les PAR validés, bases disponibles, instruments applicables et contacts institutionnels ;
  • Faciliter les introductions officielles et la coordination avec les autorités et services compétents ;
  • Examiner et valider les outils, listes et livrables dans les délais convenus ;
  • Prendre les décisions institutionnelles et assurer la disponibilité des ressources de compensation ;
  • Contractualiser l’opérateur de paiement, le cas échéant, et autoriser les paiements ;
  • Superviser la prestation par l’UGP et les UCR.

rows.notice_text:
APPEL A CANDIDATURES

ASSISTANT(E) TECHNIQUE CHARGÉ(E) D’ACCOMPAGNER LE MINISTÈRE DE L’INDUSTRIALISATION ET DU DÉVELOPPEMENT DU SECTEUR PRIVÉ (MIDSP) DANS L’IDENTIFICATION, LA STRUCTURATION ET LA MISE EN ŒUVRE DE SES PROJETS PRIORITAIRES ET STRUCTURANTS

    Crédit IDA 78730

    AC N° C-534-PIC3-INV

    Date de lancement :  16 septembre 2026

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a obtenu un financement additionnel de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour financer la mise en œuvre du Projet de Transformation économique pour la croissance inclusive (PIC3). Une partie du crédit sera utilisée pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de consultance cité en objet.

2. La mission principale de l’Assistant technique chargé d’accompagner le Ministère de l’Industrialisation et du Développement du Secteur Privé (MIDSP) dans l’identification, la structuration et la mise en œuvre de ses projets prioritaires et structurants, est d’accompagner le MIDSP dans la préparation d’un cadre stratégique et de réforme intégré fondé sur cinq étapes clairement articulées : diagnostiquer les réalités institutionnelles et sectorielles, prioriser les filières et chaînes de valeur à fort potentiel, formuler les orientations stratégiques, réformes et projets structurants, élaborer le cadre stratégique intégré, puis définir les modalités opérationnelles de mise en œuvre, de coordination et de suivi-évaluation.

3. Les termes de référence détaillés pour la mission peuvent être consultés sur le site www.pic.mg

4. La Coordination Nationale du Projet PIC3 invite les candidats à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services cidessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services. Un consultant sera sélectionné en accord avec les procédures de recrutement de Consultant Individuel de la Banque Mondiale définies dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) pour les Fournitures, Travaux, Services autres que les Services de Consultants », 6ème édition – Février 2025. Les trois (03) candidats jugés pertinents, après évaluation des dossiers, seront invités pour un entretien.

5. L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI », énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

6. Le consultant recherché doit répondre aux qualifications suivantes :

  • Diplôme universitaire de niveau Master au minimum en économie, planification, politiques publiques, développement industriel, gestion de projets, administration publique, entrepreneuriat, finance, droit des affaires ou tout autre domaine pertinent.
  • Expérience professionnelle d’au moins 7 à 10 ans dans l’élaboration de politiques publiques, de stratégies sectorielles, de réformes économiques, de plans d’actions ou de programmes de développement.
  • Expérience confirmée dans les domaines couverts par la mission, notamment le développement industriel, le secteur privé, les PME/PMI, l’entrepreneuriat, l’investissement, l’environnement des affaires ou le développement des chaînes de valeur.
  • Expérience de collaboration avec les administrations publiques et les parties prenantes économiques, notamment les ministères, structures publiques, partenaires techniques et financiers, organisations professionnelles, institutions financières, secteur privé et acteurs régionaux.
  • Maîtrise des outils de planification stratégique, de gestion axée sur les résultats et de suivi-évaluation, ainsi que des méthodes de diagnostic, de formulation de plans d’actions et de conduite de consultations.
  • Excellentes capacités d’analyse, de rédaction, de synthèse et de facilitation, avec une aptitude démontrée à produire des documents stratégiques de qualité, animer des ateliers et travailler avec des équipes multidisciplinaires.
  • Parfaite maîtrise du français écrit et oral.

7. Les candidats intéressés doivent envoyer exclusivement par mail leur dossier de candidature, sous format PDF, composé d’une lettre de motivation, d’un CV détaillé avec les références professionnelles, d’une copie certifiée du diplôme le plus élevé ainsi que les attestations de travail au plus tard le 30 septembre 2026 à minuit à l’adresse : procurement@pic.mg

8. L’objet du mail d’envoi doit porter obligatoirement la mention suivante : AC N° C-534-PIC3-INV « AT ACCOMPAGNEMENT MIDSP »

Le Projet décline la responsabilité de la nonconsidération des candidatures ne respectant pas cette disposition obligatoire.

 

Antananarivo le 16 septembre 2026

Le Coordonnateur National du Projet PIC3

RAKOTONDRAZAKA Ladislas Adrien

EOI 01/2026 for Pre-Feasibility Study for Ground Mounted Solar PLANT with Battery Energy Storage System at TAVAKUBU in LAUTOKA, NASOLO in BA and YAQARA

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST – CONSULTANT’S QUALIFICATIONS BASED SELECTION (CQS)

Name of Project

Fiji Energy Transformation Project Preparation (P515153)

Loan No/Credit No/Grant Number

GFPP Grant No. TF0D0728

Assignment Title

Pre-Feasibility Study for Ground-Mounted Solar PV Plants with Battery Energy Storage Systems at Tavakubu, Nasolo and Yaqara

Procurement Plan Ref Number

FJ-EFL-567207-CS-CQS

Reference No.

EOI-01/2026

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

 

The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), has received financing from the World Bank toward the costs of the Fiji Energy Transformation Project Preparation (P515153), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise a pre-feasibility study for utility-scale ground-mounted solar photovoltaic (PV) plants with battery energy storage systems (BESS) at Tavakubu in Lautoka, Nasolo in Ba, and Yaqara. The assignment will assess site suitability, solar resources, grid readiness, technical configuration, economic viability, environmental and social risks, climate and disaster risks, and project implementation requirements. Following the study, the Technical Advisor will support EFL in preparing technical specifications for procurement of independent power producer arrangements.

The Services will cover:

Phase 1 site screening and project definition for all three sites, including demand growth and grid-readiness review, solar-resource and energy-yield assessment, indicative site layouts and single-line diagrams, access, topography, hydrology, climate and disaster risks, environmental and social red-flag screening, preliminary cost estimates, development timeframes, multicriteria ranking and recommendations.

Phase 2 project preparation for up to two sites selected by EFL, including cadastral, topographic and geotechnical investigations; solar-resource and shading assessment; PV and BESS configuration; energy-yield estimates; static and dynamic grid-impact studies; conceptual interconnection design; cost, revenue and financial sensitivity analysis; environmental and social assessment and management planning; approvals and permitting roadmap; and project development schedules.

Phase 3 technical support to IPP selection, including technical inputs for RFQ and RFP documents, prequalification and eligibility requirements, technical compliance and responsiveness criteria, and bid-evaluation criteria.

Preparation of an inception report, project definition report, separate pre-feasibility reports for selected sites, environmental and social outputs, presentations, model and data files, and procurement technical specifications.

Implementation period: the assignment is expected to be completed within six (6) months from contract execution and issue of the commencement notice.

Terms of Reference: The detailed Terms of Reference are attached to this REOI as Appendix 1 and may also be made available through EFL’s procurement portals.

Energy Fiji Limited now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, latest applicable edition, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

  1. Introduction and Background
    1. About Energy Fiji Limited

Energy Fiji Limited (“EFL”) is a public company limited by shares that was established under the Companies Act (2015), Laws of Fiji. It is supervised by a Board of Directors comprising a Chairman and representatives of its shareholders. Its major shareholders include the Fijian Government and Sevens Pacific Pte. Limited.

 

The Executive Management team of EFL consists of the Chief Executive Officer, Deputy Chief Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer, Chief Finance Officer, General Manager Human Resources, General Manager Generation, General Manager Network, General Manager Customer Services, General Manager System Planning and Control, General Manager Special Projects and Chief Information Officer.

 

EFL is primarily responsible for generation, transmission and distribution of electricity in Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Ovalau and Taveuni in Fiji. It owns over twenty (20) power stations and twenty (20) substations and switching stations on the islands of Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Taveuni and Ovalau. EFL owns, operates and maintains a network of 147km of 132kV transmission lines, 576km of 33kV lines and over 11,200km of 11kV and 415V distribution lines, as at 31st December 2025. It also has over 227,000 customer accounts as at 31st December 2025, made up of domestic, institutional, commercial and industrial customers.

 

EFL has embarked upon an ambitious program of development in order to fulfil its strategic objectives. These include development of new generating and power system projects as well as improving reliability and capacity-building for future load growth. EFL plans to increase the generation capacity of Fiji in order to meet continuing demand growth and intends that this additional capacity will be provided by renewable or at least non-polluting resources. 

    1. Project Background and Overview

Fiji utilizes a diverse array of energy sources, including hydro, diesel, wood, and petroleum products, to fulfill its energy needs. EFL is the primary provider of grid-based power to approximately 90% of the population on the main islands of Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Taveuni and Ovalau. EFL aims to supply at least 90% of its energy requirements through renewable sources by 2035. Having a dependable and high-quality supply of electricity is crucial for driving economic growth. Lack of access to electricity not only diminishes the quality of life but also deprives people from essential services like healthcare, agriculture, education etc.

 

EFL is undertaking the development of a utility-scale ground-mounted solar PV power at the identified sites in Viti Levu. This study aims to delve into the key components of a pre-feasibility study for ground mounted solar PV project with BESS at these sites, focusing on technical and economic analyses. Additionally, it will assess other essential considerations such as environmental, and social aspects in alignment with the IFC Performance Standards, emphasizing their importance for the success and long-term sustainability of the project. Upon completion of the pre-feasibility study, the Technical Advisor is required to assist in preparation of procurement documentation by preparing technical specifications that will be used by EFL for preparing the procurement documentation to select an independent power producer (IPP). The project may subsequently be prepared to be developed through public-private partnership.

 

This project supports Fiji’s National Development Plan target of achieving 100% grid-connected renewable electricity generation by 2035 and EFL’s corporate goal of sourcing more than 90% of its energy from renewable sources by 2035. The installation will enhance grid stability, reduce reliance on fossil fuels, and contribute to sustainable economic growth.

 

    1. Objective of this Assignment

The objective of this solar feasibility study is to determine the practicality and economic viability of installing solar photovoltaic system with battery energy storage system at the proposed sites by evaluating solar resources, technical requirements, financial performance, environmental benefits, and potential risks, and to provide recommendations for project implementation.

 

  1. Scope of Work

EFL has identified  three (3) sites which they intend to develop for solar PV power plant with BESS. Annexure A  shows these  three sites, and these are legally described as follows:

Lease or Title Document Reference

Legal description of Land.

Nasolo - Ba
