EFL would like to procure the services of a Technical Advisor which will be the firm with a qualified team of multi-disciplinary experts comprising international and national consultants for the provision of the scope of work enumerated below. The Technical Advisor will work closely with and directly support EFL for the Project.

 

The Technical Advisor shall carry out the work as per the scope mentioned in this section. For carrying out this project, the Technical Advisor shall draw a detailed action plan which need to be presented during the project inception meeting to be held with EFL. 

 

The feasibility shall be completed in Six (6) months from the execution of Contract and issue of commencement notice.

 

The scope of work will be follows as a minimum, but not limited to:

    1. Phase 1: Site Screening and Project Definition

The Technical Advisor shall conduct initial site assessment to screen the gross area of the three sites based on secondary data available, information collected from stakeholders, data analysis (as required for GIS-based assessment of the sites using satellite imagery available):

 

  1. Demand forecast review for solar energy needs, and grid readiness assessment (including grid availability, access to transmission infrastructure, possible augmentation needs);

 

  1. Site suitability analysis covering but not limited to:
  1. Solar energy resource assessment including hourly, monthly and annual energy yield estimation,
  2. Indicative site layouts and concept single line diagram
  3. Access road availability
  4. Topographical, geographical, and hydrological features;
  5. Disaster risk including earthquake, flood and cyclone and climate change risk assessment;

 

  1. Recommendation on the possibility of including Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) covering capacity/size (to meet the project needs requirements only, for the project to operate as a round-the-clock dispatchable unit), design, technology and location, and its impact to the need of grid connection capacity.

 

  1. Preliminary analysis of potential social and environmental safeguards risks, in line with National regulations and the IFC Performance Standards and climate change risk vulnerability assessment (red flag report) and prepare a preliminary stakeholder map and key considerations.

 

  1. Preparation of preliminary cost estimates (AACEI Level 5 equivalent, capturing (Capex) and operating expenses (Opex)) for respective solar PV plant and accompanying transmission infrastructure including the need for control and communication infrastructure upgrades, etc..

 

  1. Prepare a shortlist of candidate sites based on Phase 1 outcomes, summarizing key site conditions, technical, environmental, and social risks and impacts, and provide recommendation on key next steps for further development, including gaps of project preparation.

 

  1. Indicative development timeframe for each site, based on accessibility, scale of development and grid readiness, and other key considerations affecting development timeframe.

 

  1. Site ranking for the identified three project sites using a multi-criterion assessment framework factoring technical, environmental, and social safeguard considerations, and indicative development timeframe, and provide recommendations for further development.

 

    1. Phase 2: Project Preparation

Based on the results of Phase 1, EFL will select sites for further development. If there are no sites are deemed viable, the consultancy assignment will not continue.

 

For the selected sites, the Technical Advisor shall prepare a comprehensive feasibility study covering the ground mounted solar plant, BESS, transmission interconnection and transmission line as outlined above. It will consist among others engineering, financial, social and environmental due-diligence adhering to the World Banks ESS Standards and analysis of proposed site and develop an optimal solution.

 

The feasibility study report should cover all requirements identified by EFL and mentioned in any relevant laws and regulations as applicable to energy projects in Fiji, and should include the following:

  1. A detailed report on project site and boundary area and approximated site plan, design and layout of the ground mounted solar facility. The report will also cover the right of way analysis for various civil works, transmission lines, among other technical aspects.
  2. Study and survey of water resource availability, geology, meteorology, earthquake and seismic risks, hydrology, and flood risks. Site surveys shall include cadastral and topographic surveys (for contours levels of 2metres or less), and Auto-CAD version of site surveys shall be shared with the deliverables.
  3. Conduct geotechnical investigations based on AS 1726, with one borehole per hectare for at least a depth of 5 metres for field investigations, and laboratory testing based on AS 1289.
  4. Conduct solar resource assessment (including irradiation studies) using satellite and ground-measured solar resource assessment.
  5. Options for placement and arrangement of solar panels and other equipment configuration, including inverters, mounting platforms, transformers etc. and other electrical, electromechanical, auxiliary and protection, control, and monitoring systems that are part of a ground mounted solar PV system.
  6. Shading analysis including near and far shading.
  7. Estimate energy yields. The energy yield should include an assessment of the inter-annual variation and yield confidence levels, and electrical losses from the influence of temperature variances on the efficiency of the plant, and include consideration of site-specific factors, including soiling or rain, and the cleaning regime.
  8. Grid impact and readiness study: conduct static and dynamic grid impact study, and discuss the need for any augmentation needed to accommodate for plant variability, and related costs and curtailment rate.
  9. Based on the preliminary study of BESS use in Phase I and the discussion with EFL, the Technical Advisor will study the use of BESS system based on the specifications of the solar RE and the grid impact assessment. The study will cover the capacity, design, location, other technical specifications of the BESS system.
  10. Single line diagram including conceptual interconnection design.
  11. The cost estimates for development, construction (civil works, right of way) and operations of the solar project, BESS (if applicable) and predicted revenue, based on the available resource data, as well as indicative quotes or comparison with similar projects.
  12. Input technical assumptions for the financial model and run sensitivity studies to identify range of feed-in tariff and acceptable rate of returns.
  13. Conduct social and environmental safeguard assessment in line with National regulations and the IFC Performance Standards, including land acquisition and livelihood impacts, biodiversity and habitat risks, indigenous peoples’ rights, cultural heritage, community health and safety, and stakeholder engagement. Develop an environmental and social assessment and management plan, clear roadmap of required approvals, permits, and mitigation measures to ensure compliance and sustainability. The cost of the implementation of the environmental and social assessment and management plan should be included.
  14. Develop project development schedule for each selected site based on the findings of the feasibility study and assessments.
  15. Provide inputs and work with others who may be appointed by the Client (EFL) to prepare the grid augmentation aspects of the works.

 

 

    1. Phase 3: Technical Support to IPP Selection

Contingent on EFL’s decision, the Technical Advisor will assist EFL for the implementation of the selection of the IPP by providing inputs on technical aspects of the Pre-qualification, and Request for Proposal (RFP) and Request for Bid (RFB) processes.

 

The detailed inputs would include the following:

  1. All equipment specifications
  2. Tentative Design and Construction details
  3. Installation procedures/recommendations for project developers
  4. Commissioning tests and processes of the project, including but not limited to formats of certificates
  5. Performance Parameters, Guarantees and Schedules
  6. Commercial performance guarantees

 

Other Tasks and Responsibilities:

In addition to the above scope of work, the Technical Advisor shall liaise and cooperate, as necessary and throughout the assignment, with other consultants engaged by EFL for the study. All deliverables and key outputs will be developed in English and submitted in soft copies to EFL. Key members of the consulting firm/(s) shall have the ability to conduct meetings and discussions in English.

 

The Technical Advisor shall prepare highlights and/or minutes of all relevant major meetings and other

consultations.

 

The Client would retain the right to: a) decide the number of projects that would proceed from phase 1 to phase 2 (project preparation) and b) implement or not Phase 3 activities.

 

  1. Deliverables

The Technical Advisor shall provide the following deliverables:

 

    1. Inception Report
  • Finalized workplan and schedule (milestones, review meetings), data request list, study methodology outline (including software/tools and versions), and stakeholder engagement plan(as applicable).
  • Finalized project implementation schedule (Gantt chart) covering Phase 1 and Phase 2 activities, key milestones, dependencies, review points, and required inputs from EFL.
  • Format: PDF + editable (Word/Excel).
  • Submission: within 1 week of commencement

 

    1. Project Definition Report
  • Covers all work under Sub-Clause 3.1 (Phase 1: Site Screening and Project Definition)
  • Where software/tools are used (e.g., solar resource assessment), include generated outputs.
  • Format: PDF + editable; Excel calculation files; GIS package (site boundary, constraints, layout files).
  • Submission: within 8 weeks of commencement, with key findings presentation to EFL

 

    1. Pre-Feasibility Report, including Environmental and Social Outputs
  • Covers all work under Sub-Clause 3.2 (Phase 2: Project Preparation)
  • Environmental and Social Assessment and Management Plans – ESIA and ESMP
  • Models and data: study case files (e.g., PSS®E/DIgSILENT/ETAP—version stated), network and load/generation data, contingencies list, protection/limits inputs, and scenario files (as applicable and available).
  • Format: PDF + editable report; native model files in agreed tool; data dictionary.
  • Submission: within 18 weeks of commencement, to be submitted as separate reports for each site, with in-person presentation to EFL

 

    1. Procurement Technical Specifications (Phase 3: Technical Support to IPP Selection)
  • Include all technical sections derived from Sub-Clause 3.1and 3.2 for incorporation into the procurement/bidding documents to be compiled/prepared by others
  • Format: PDF + editable (Word/Excel).
  • Submission: within 24 weeks of commencement. To be submitted as separate package for each site.

 

  1. Supervision and Reporting

The Project Owner is the Chief Executive Officer - EFL. The Technical Advisor will report to and coordinate with General Manager Special Projects of EFL for various project related components and delivery.

 

  1. Expertise and Qualification

The Bidders themselves or with their Joint Venture partners should have previous experience and expertise in Review and Vetting, and /or feasibility stage Design & Engineering of at least seven solar PV power plant projects with BESS in last 7 years.

 

    1. Similar Project Experience
  2. The Bidder shall demonstrate experience as a Technical Advisor / Owner’s Engineer / Consultant in the feasibility or pre-feasibility stage of at least seven solar PV power plant projects incorporating BESS, with a total cumulative PV capacity of not less than 250MW, completed or substantially completed within the last seven years from date of closing of this tender, and currently in operation.
  3. The relevant FS-stage experience shall demonstrate technical scope and complexity comparable to the activities described in Scope of Work.
  4. At least one referenced project shall demonstrate experience in a Pacific island country or a similar island environment, highlighting familiarity with island-grid operation, logistics constraints, and climate-related risks.

 

    1. Staff Qualification and Experience

The Bidder must have as a minimum, qualified and experienced key staff in the following areas:

 

  • Project Management & Coordination
  1. Project Manager with demonstrated experience in managing solar PV projects with integrated BESS, both regionally and internationally
  2. Demonstrated experience of the Project Manager and key staff in handling FIDIC contract conditions, particularly for EPC tender preparation and evaluation.
  3. Strong leadership capability to coordinate multidisciplinary teams including engineers, specialists and relevant stakeholders (such as government agencies and utilities).
  4. Expertise in project risk management, scheduling and tracking (e.g., Primavera P6 / MS Project), and overall project governance.

 

  • Technical Experts
  1. Solar Resource & Energy Yield Analysis Expert, proficient in PVsyst or equivalent tools, with experience in developing energy yield assessments for large-scale solar PV projects.
  2. BESS Sizing & Techno-Economic Optimization Specialist, experienced in modelling tools such as HOMER, REopt, or equivalent.
  3. Electrical Engineers with demonstrated experience in solar PV and BESS system design at feasibility and conceptual design levels.
  4. Power System Study Engineer, experienced in load flow, short-circuit, stability analysis, and grid integration studies.
  5. Power System Protection & Control Engineer, familiar with protection philosophy, relay coordination, and integration with BESS control system.
  6. Communications & SCADA/Control System Engineer, experienced in utility-scale PV/BESS monitoring, control, and communications architectures.
  7. High Voltage Substation & Transmission Conceptual Design Engineer, capable of developing FS-level substation, switching station, and transmission line concepts.
  8. Power Station Conceptual Design Engineer, experienced in preliminary plant layout, electrical balance of plant, and integration of PV+BESS systems.
  9. Civil/Structural Engineer experienced in site assessment and conceptual civil design for PV and BESS facilities.
  10. Geology & Geotechnical Engineer to perform desktop geotechnical assessment and site feasibility analysis.

 

  • Financial & Regulatory Experts
  1. Financial Modelling & Economic Analysis Expert with experience in renewable energy and BESS project.
  2. Regulatory & Permitting Specialist with understanding of environmental permitting requirements and international BESS safety standards.

 

  • Environmental & Social Specialists
  1. Environmental & Social Safeguard Expert(s), experienced in IFC Performance Standards and relevant national environmental and social regulations.
  2. Land & Site Assessment Specialist with capability to assess land suitability, hydrology, flood risk, and land use constraints for large-scale solar PV projects.

 

All identified Key Staff and their Curriculum Vitae (CV) should be included in the bid submission.

 

      1. Minimum Team-Level Qualifications
  2. Degree-qualified engineers in relevant disciplines, with FS/conceptual design experience for large-scale PV + BESS.
  3. Experience thresholds (Key Experts):
  • 15 years or more of experience for the Team Leader / Project Manager.
  • 8 – 10 years or more of experience for Discipline Leads / Key Specialists.
  • 3 – 5 years or more of experience for Supporting staff working under the supervision of Key Experts.
  1. Standards and codes: Working knowledge of Australian/New Zealand standards, IEC for PV/BESS, IEEE for grid interconnection (as applicable), and applicable Fijian standards, grid codes and environmental requirements.
  2. Context familiarity (advantageous): Prior individual experience of Key Experts in Fiji/Oceania (contractors, supply chains, logistics) and knowledge of Fiji’s regulatory and permitting processes.
  3. Language: Fluency in English (verbal and written).
      1. FS-Critical Competencies
  1. Feasibility-level technical review & conceptual design, including plant layout concepts and integration of PV, BESS and grid interconnection.
  2. Energy yield & sizing methods appropriate to FS stage, and ability to justify key assumptions and loss factors.
  3. Power system study scoping suitable for FS stage (e.g., load flow / short-circuit and stability screening to inform interconnection feasibility and grid code compliance pathways).
  4. HSE for PV + BESS at concept stage, including hazard identification (e.g., thermal runaway/fire) and alignment with relevant codes and local authority requirements.
      1. Submission Requirements
  1. Project organization chart with man-month allocations by phase and role.
  2. List of Key Experts with CVs indicating roles, years of experience, representative assignments, and time commitment to this project.
  3. CVs of Team Leader and Project Manager and other key management personnel.
  4. CVs of supporting personnel with reporting lines to Key Experts.
  5. Resourcing plan with expected man-days per workstream
  6. Quality Management System, with brief description of document control, internal review/verification, and risk management.
  7. Access to supplementary local expertise and partnerships, including local consulting firms or subcontractors with knowledge of Fijian land regulations, permitting processes, and other local requirements.

Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh

Department of Environment

Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP)

DoE Component-“Comprehensive Environmental Impact and Damage Assessment of Rohingya Influx in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasanchar of Chattogram Division

1st Floor, Room: 202, Poribesh Bhaban New Building

E/16 Agargaon, Sher-E-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka-1207

www.doe.gov.bd

 

Memo No.: 22.02.0000.020.14.012.26.121                                                             Date:  15/09/2026

  

Request for Expressions of Interest

(Consulting Services – Firm Selection)

 

Country: Bangladesh

Name of the Proposed Project: Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP)

Grant No.: E325-BD

Assignment Title:

Consulting Service for Development of a detailed Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) with Strategic Environment Management Plan (SEMP)

Reference No.: S-9

Project ID No: P501274

The People's Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Development of a detailed Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) for the existing and proposed Policies, Plans, Programs, and Projects in the region of Cox’sBazar District with adjoining Marine and Marine Coastal areas  as well as other impacted areas and prepare a Strategic Environmental Management Plan (SEMP) with future intervension to manage and restore the environment and ecosystem in the impacted area.

 

  1. The broad scope of consulting services (“the Services”) includes but not limited to:
  • Inception
  • Screening
  • Scoping
  • A report on Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) along with the detailed analysis of the PPPPs
  • Strategic Environmental Management Plan (SEMP)
  • Draft Final SEA Report including SEMP
  1. The objectives of the consultancy services are to come-up with the cumulative environmental impacts of the existing and proposed Policies, Plans, Programs, and Projects (PPPPs) in Cox’s Bazar district including Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs-impacted areas so that the GoB can address them at the earliest phase of decision making alongside economic and social considerations. The specific objectives are:
  • Consideration of environmental and socio-economic consequences of existing and proposed PPPs (national and Cox’s Bazar district including Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs impacted areas) that cover the target area of this assignment and promoting that these issues be addressed when formulating and implementing future, as well as existing and proposed PPPs to promote sustainable development in the target area and conservation of their environmental and ecological value;
  • Identification of key stakeholders relevant to selected sectors and organizing consultation meetings to obtain knowledge on existing bio-physical settings and socio-economic conditions, impacts of current and proposed developments, and potential strategies for future development of the Cox’s Bazar district-Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs impacted areas;
  • Development of alternative strategies to minimize the direct/indirect, domestic/transboundary and cumulative impacts of development on the study area of the Chattogram division;
  • Prepare a SEMP with potential recommendations to improve environmental performance management in both the public and private sectors with regard to current and future development activities as well as to manage and restore the environment and ecosystem in the impacted area.
  • Formulation of a comprehensive monitoring framework as part of the Strategic Environmental Management Plan (SEMP) for the study area of the Chattogram division including Cox’s Bazar district-Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs impacted areas to support decision making and monitoring of the implementation of PPPs that are likely to affect the environment and socio-economic conditions of the target area.
  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: www.doe.gov.bd The ToR or any further information can be obtained at the address of the undersigned given below, during office hours from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm Bangladesh Standard Time (BST).
  2. The Department of Environment (DoE) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.  The shortlisting criteria are:

a)   General Experience of the Firm in providing similar services (core business and years in business);

b)   Experience in similar assignments of compatible size, complexity and technical specialty in the required areas;

c)   Experience in development partners funded similar Projects.

  1. Consultants are requested to submit, but not limited to, the following supporting documents in support of the above-mentioned criteria:

(i)  The Firm's Incorporation/Trade/registration documents from the country of the firm (ii) Firm’s brochures; (iii) description of similar consultancy contracts, including the scope, contract amount, name of Client, period of the contract (date of contract signing to date of completion), location/ country of the services, etc.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or a sub-consultancy (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). rows.contact_address: Antananarivo
rows.notice_text:
APPEL À MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN(E) SPECIALISTE EN GESTION DES RISQUES ENVIRONNEMENTAUX DE L’UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET PRODUIRE

 

Pays : MADAGASCAR

AMI N : 04 -2026/MATSF/PRODUIRE

Projet : PROJET DE DEVELOPPEMENT URBAIN INTEGRE ET RESILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI

Crédit : IDA 8089 MG

Date de lancement : 16 septembre 2026

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de 225 millions USD de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) au profit du Projet de Développement Urbain Integré et Résilient pour l’Emploi (PRODUIRE) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour financer le contrat de services d’un Spécialiste en gestion des risques environnementaux de l’Unité de Gestion de Projet à Antananarivo.

L’Objectif de Développement du Projet (ODP) est de renforcer la résilience climatique des communautés urbaines, d'améliorer l'administration foncière et de soutenir l'emploi dans certaines villes.

2. Les services du consultant (« les services ») consistent à fournir une expertise au projet  pour assurer que (a) les activités du projet soient conformes au Cadre environnemental et social et plus particulièrement aux documents cadres du projet (Plan d’Engagement Environnemental et Social , Cadre de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale, Cadre de Réinstallation du projet, et aux outils de gestion sociaux (Plan de Gestion de la Main d’œuvre, Plan de Mobilisation des Parties Prenantes et que (b) les principes et les activités liés à l’engagement civique et citoyen dans le cadre du projet soient respectés et mis en œuvre .

3. Le mandat fera l’objet d’un contrat de 60 mois assorti d’une tranche ferme de douze mois et de 04 tranches conditionnelles de 12 mois dont la condition d’affermissement sera l’évaluation positive de la perfomance du consultant. Un période d’essai de 6 mois est prévue dans la tranche ferme. Le lieu de travail est au siège du projet à Antananarivo.

4. Le Spécialiste en gestion des risques environnementaux doit répondre au profil suivant:

- Titulaire d’un diplôme Bacc + 4 en sciences environnementales ou agroforesterie ou en écologie ou en géographie ou Ingéniorat ou équivalents

- Au minimum dix (10) ans d’expériences professionnelles avec des expériences probantes dans de projet similaire ;

- Très bonne maîtrise des normes environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale avec certificat de réussite de la formation sur Open Learning Campus à l’appui .;

- Expériences d’au moins trois (03) ans dans un poste similaire dans un projet financé par la Banque mondiale ou références similaires des autres bailleurs

- Connaissance des textes règlementaires et légaux en vigueur régissant le domaine de l’environnement au niveau national

- Expériences dans les projets financés par la Banque mondiale ;

- Ayant des expériences dans la conduite et le suivi de la mise en œuvre des EIES/PGES ainsi que des rapports de suivi environnemental associés ;

- Excellente capacité rédactionnelle ;

- Excellente maitrise du Français, du Malagasy et bonne connaissance de l’Anglais ;

- Bonne capacité d’analyse et synthèse ;

- Bonne capacité d’écoute et de communication ;

- Excellente maîtrise des outils informatiques de bureautique et de messagerie électronique.

5. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous de 08 heures à 16 heures pendant les jours ouvrables.

6. Le MATSF invite les consultants individuels qualifiés à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services decrits ci-dessus. Les consultants interessés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Son dossier de candidature comprendra entre autre :

a. Lettre de motivation

b. Curriculum vitae avec coordonnées ( adresse, téléphone, e-mail)

c. Copie des diplômes, attestation de formations

d. Certificat/ attestation de prestations similaires

e. Trois références professionnelles

En cas d’envoi de manifestation par e-mail, le Candidat fournira toutes les pièces en un seul fichier PDF.

7. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) » septième édition septembre 2025, relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts sont applicables.

8. Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode Sélection de Consultant Individuel telle que décrite dans le Règlement. Les candidats présélectionnés à l’issue de l’examen des dossiers seront convoqués à un entretien.

9. Les consultants Individuels interessés sont invités à demander par courriel la version électronique des termes de référence de la mission à l’adresse ci-dessous. Le nom, le contact ainsi que l’adresse physique et électronique du consultant individuel devront être spécifiés dans la demande.

10. Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être déposés et/ou envoyés par courriel , au plus tard le 08 octobre 2026 à 16 heures à l’adresse ci-dessous, en mentionnant la référence :

Ministry of Environment

Cambodia Sustainable Landscape and Ecotourism Project (CSLEP)

IDA Credit number 6433-KH

Project ID: P165344

­­­­­­­­­­­­­         ______________________________________________________________________________________________

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

SHORT-TERM INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT

National Project Beneficiary Satisfaction Survey Consultant (MOE-CS-2026-01-BSSC)

  1. Background

The World Bank and the Global Environment Facility (GEF) are supporting the Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) on IDA-financed and GEF-additional financed project entitled “Cambodia Sustainable Landscape and Ecotourism Project”. The project commenced on October 17, 2019, with an expected closing date on December 31, 2027.  The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve protected area management and enhance ecotourism services in selected sites in the Cardamom Mountains–Tonle Sap Landscape.

The Project is seeking a qualified Individual Consultant to undertake the Project Beneficiary Satisfaction Survey.

  1. Objective of the assignment

The objective of this short-term assignment is to conduct an independent assessment of the satisfaction of CSLEP target beneficiaries with relevant project interventions, with results disaggregated by gender and age, in accordance with the Project’s Results Framework. Specifically, the survey will assess beneficiaries’ satisfaction with project interventions that they have received, participated in, used, or directly benefited from, including:

  1. Business Development Services (BDS) support,
  2. Community livelihood and NTFP value-chain support,
  3. Ecotourism development and Regulatory Framework support,
  4. Public infrastructure investments support.

The survey will also identify the main factors influencing beneficiaries’ satisfaction or dissatisfaction, capture beneficiaries’ views on the relevance, accessibility, benefits and quality of the support received, and obtain their feedback and recommendations for improving ongoing project implementation.

  1. Scope of the Assignment.

     The assignment will cover relevant CSLEP target beneficiaries across the Project’s selected PAs, CPAs and CBET sites in the six target provinces. The survey shall take into account that project interventions differ across locations and beneficiary groups; therefore, respondents should be assessed only in relation to the interventions from which they have directly benefited, participated in, or used. The selected consultant will be responsible for organizing and managing the assignment, including determining and arranging the necessary technical and field support required to undertake the survey and deliver the expected outputs within the agreed timeframe. 

     For details, please clink the link to download the Terms of Reference: https://shorturl.at/SYZk8

  1. Expected Output/Deliverables:
  1. Deliverable 1: Inception Report (including the refined methodology and sampling approach, finalized data collection instruments, data quality and analysis approach, detailed work plan and implementation schedule, and proposed disbursement plan; 
  2. Deliverable 2: Draft beneficiary Satisfaction Survey Report and presentation of Findings;
  3. Deliverable 3: Final Beneficiary Satisfaction Survey Report and required supporting materials.
  1. Duration of Assignment. October till Mid-December 2026.
  2. Required Qualification and Experiences: Interest candidates should have:

Interested candidates should possess the following qualifications and experience:

  • Advanced university degree (Master's degree or higher) in social sciences, economics, statistics, development studies, monitoring and evaluation, natural resource management, tourism, or another relevant field;
  • At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in socio-economic research, beneficiary surveys, evaluations, monitoring and evaluation, or similar assignments;
  • Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing household or beneficiary surveys using quantitative and qualitative methods;
  • Strong experience in sampling, survey instrument development, data quality assurance, data management, analysis and interpretation;
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting or managing FGDs and KIIs and synthesizing qualitative findings;
  • Strong analytical, report-writing, presentation, coordination and assignment-management skills;
  • Good knowledge of Cambodia's development context and experience working with rural communities and diverse beneficiary groups;
  • Relevant experience in community development, livelihoods, tourism/ ecotourism, natural resource management or similar development projects would be an advantage; and
  • Proficiency in Khmer and English, particularly in analysis and report preparation.
  1. Submission of Expression of Interest: Interested and qualified candidates are invited to submit:
  • A letter of Expression of Interest, indicating ‘’ Expression of Interest-Short-Term Individual Consultant’’) in the subject line.
  • An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV) clearly demonstrating relevant qualification and experiences; and
  • Contact details of the candidate.

The CV should clearly Identify assignments and experience that are directly to the proposed short-term consultancy.

  • Deadline on/before: 25 September 2026 at 17:00 P.M (Cambodia time).
  • Submission:  Can be both by email or hard copy to the below address.
  1. Address:     Ministry of Environment, Project Implementation Unit, Cambodia Sustainable Landscape and Ecotourism Project (CSLEP), Room Tung, 3rd Floor, Morodok Techo Building (Lot 503), Tonle Bassac, Chamkarmorn, Phnom Penh, Cambodia. Email: sok.rathna@moe.gov.kh; taing.porchhay@moe.gov.kh; tes.samnanag@moe.gov.kh. and  cc: khin.mengkheang@moe.gov.kh; srey.sunleang@moe.gov.kh

UNITÉ DE GESTION DU PROJET

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

N°0124/E/2/AMI/MINHDU/SG/PVGFD/REAF/RPM/RPMJC2/2026 DU 11 SEPTEMBRE 2026

Pays :                      Cameroun

Projet :                     Projet Villes et Gestion Foncière Durable (PVGFD)

Financement :          Crédit IDA A-7793 et B-7794-CM

Titre de la mission :  Recrutement d’une maîtrise d’œuvre privée pour la digitalisation des services, procédures et produits domaniaux, cadastraux, fonciers et patrimoniaux.

N° de référence :      CM-MINHDU-561022-CS-QCBS du Plan de Passation de Marchés approuvé du 23 juillet 2026

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Cameroun a obtenu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA), pour couvrir le coût du Projet Villes et Gestion Foncière Durable (PVGFD) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de Consultants pour le recrutement d’une maîtrise d’œuvre privée pour la digitalisation des services, procédures et produits domaniaux, cadastraux, fonciers et patrimoniaux.

 

  1. Les services de consultants comprennent entre autres le contrôle et surveillance du déroulement de toutes les étapes et la qualité des prestations et livrables produits par le prestataire chargé de la digitalisation des services, procédures et produits domaniaux, cadastraux, fonciers et patrimoniaux pour le compte du Ministère des Domaines, du Cadastre et des Affaires Foncières. Ces services comprennent les missions suivantes :
  • Appuyer / conseiller le MINDCAF dans les stratégies et préconisations en vue de la bonne exécution des activités ;
  • Proposer un plan de contrôle de la qualité basé sur les spécifications techniques et prescriptions du contrat ;
  • Examiner la méthodologie globale au début dudit projet ;
  • Contrôler les travaux de terrain ;
  • Valider chaque étape du projet et faire le contrôle qualité des différents livrables produits par le prestataire ;
  • Examiner les rapports d’étapes et livrables produits par le prestataire ;
  • Contrôler toutes les étapes de la réalisation de chacune des composantes ci-dessous citées pour qu’elles correspondent aux exigences du cahier de charges soumis au prestataire.

 

Les prestations techniques attendues par ces services de maîtrise d’œuvre privée sont regroupées en trois (03) principales composantes qui interagissent entre elles ; à savoir :

 

  • Composante 1 : Conception, fourniture et installation d’un système d’information foncière (SIF) à Yaoundé et à Douala ;
  • Audit technique : examen des infrastructures, logiciels, hébergement, cybersécurité ;
  • Audit fonctionnel : revue des processus de collecte, traitement et mise à jour des données, ainsi que les flux d’information ;
  • Vérification sur site : inspection de guichets fonciers, entrevues avec les agents ;
  • Analyse juridique : conformité aux lois foncières, gestion des droits et conflits ;
  • Analyse de la gouvernance et des responsabilités des acteurs du secteur foncier et domanial ;
  • Evaluation de l’interopérabilité avec les autres systèmes indiqués dans le cahier de charges du prestataire ;
  • Appui aux réformes : propositions de mise à jour du cadre législatif et réglementaire, organisationnel et opérationnel.

 

  • Composante 2 : Numérisation des archives cadastrales et foncières de Yaoundé et Douala
  1. Audit du processus de numérisation
  2. Contrôle de la qualité des données converties
  3. Audit de la sécurité et de la traçabilité
  4. Revue documentaire et organisationnelle
  • Composante 3 : Mise en place de deux (02) stations GNSS permanentes ou stations CORS.
  1. Audit technique de la station GNSS
  1. Audit du centre de diffusion et contrôle
  1. Examen des protocoles et procédures
  1. Revue documentaire et organisationnelle
  2. Essais de performance

Les Termes de Référence détaillés pour la mission peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

  1. La durée de cette prestation est de trente-sept (37) mois à compter de la date indiquée sur l’ordre de service de commencer les prestations.

 

  1. Le Ministre de l’Habitat et du Développement Urbain, invite les firmes de consultants (ci-après désignés Consultants) à manifester leur intérêt pour la réalisation des présentes prestations. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution desdites prestations (brochures, description de missions semblables, expérience dans des conditions similaires, disponibilité des compétences parmi le personnel, …).

N.B. : Bien vouloir justifier par les pages de garde et de signature du contrat, ainsi que les attestations de bonne fin ou tout autre document attestant que le contrat a été exécuté dans de bonnes conditions. La liste détaillée des références, faisant ressortir pour chacune, l'intitulé de la mission, l'année de réalisation, les dates de début et de fin de mission, le montant des travaux supervisés et le commanditaire.

Les critères de présélection sont les suivants :

 

  • Justifier d'une expérience dans le domaine de la mise en œuvre et/ou suivi de l’implémentation des systèmes d’information foncière (SIF) ou géographique (SIG), de conversion des données et numérisation des documents, ainsi que des stations GNSS permanentes d’au moins cinq (05) ans ;
  • - Avoir réalisé, au cours des dix (10) dernières années, au moins trois (03) projets similaires, couvrant collectivement les composantes suivantes : (i) SIF/SIG, (ii) numérisation/gestion électronique de document (GED), (iii) stations permanentes/CORS. Une expérience intégrant plusieurs de ces composantes au sein d'un même projet, ainsi qu'une expérience en Afrique, seront considérées comme des atouts ;
  • Avoir une expérience antérieure sur des projets financés par la Banque mondiale ou d'autres institutions financières internationales constituera un atout.

 

  1. Il est porté à l'attention des consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.15, 3.16 et 3.17 de la Section III du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d'Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de septembre 2025 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés relatifs aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d'intérêt ») sont applicables et disponibles sur le site web de la Banque à l’adresse : www.worldbank.org.

 

  1. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer avec d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives en la forme d’un groupement solidaire ou d’un accord de sous-traitant.

APPEL À MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN(E) SPECIALISTE EN GESTION DES RISQUES SOCIAUX DE L’UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET PRODUIRE

 

Pays : MADAGASCAR

AMI N : 05-2026/MATSF/PRODUIRE

Projet : Projet de Développement Urbain Intégré ET RESILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI

Crédit : IDA 8089 MG

Date de lancement : 16 septembre 2026

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de 225 millions USD de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) au profit du Projet de Développement Urbain Integré et Résilient pour l’Emploi (PRODUIRE) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour financer le contrat de services d’un Spécialiste en gestion des risques sociaux de l’Unité de Gestion de Projet à Antananarivo.

L’Objectif de Développement du Projet (ODP) est de renforcer la résilience climatique des communautés urbaines, d'améliorer l'administration foncière et de soutenir l'emploi dans certaines villes.

2. Les services du consultant (« les services ») consistent à fournir une expertise au projet  pour assurer que (a) les activités du projet soient conformes au Cadre environnemental et social et plus particulièrement aux documents cadres du projet (Plan d’Engagement Environnemental et Social , Cadre de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale, Cadre de Réinstallation du projet, et aux outils de gestion sociaux (Plan de Gestion de la Main d’œuvre, Plan de Mobilisation des Parties Prenantes et que (b) les principes et les activités liés à l’engagement civique et citoyen dans le cadre du projet soient respectés et mis en œuvre

3. Le mandat fera l’objet d’un contrat de 60 mois assorti d’une tranche ferme de douze mois et de 04 tranches conditionnelles de 12 mois dont la condition d’affermissement sera l’évaluation positive de la perfomance du consultant. Un période d’essai de 6 mois est prévue dans la tranche ferme. Le lieu de travail est au siège du projet à Antananarivo.

4. Le Spécialiste en gestion des risques sociaux doit répondre au profil suivant :

- Titulaire d’un diplôme BAC + 5 dans le domaine social, d’études d’impacts environnemental et social ou ingénierie sociale, en études d’impacts sociaux et d’appui aux projets de développement sociaux ;

­ - Expériences probantes et réussies dans le domaine du développement social et plus particulièrement : gestion de risques sociaux (particulièrement réinstallation involontaire de personnes), inclusion sociale (incluant genre), engagement citoyen/redevabilité sociale et développement communautaire, gestion des conflits et des plaintes ;

­-  Expériences d’au moins trois (03) ans dans un poste similaire dans un projet financé par la Banque mondiale

­-  Connaissance des textes règlementaires et légaux en vigueur régissant le domaine de l’expropriation ;

­-  Connaissance du contexte national et des nouvelles normes environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale en vigueur avec certificat de réussite de la formation sur Open Learning Campus à l’appui .;

­ - Capacité de planification, d’anticipation, d’analyse, de synthèse, de rédaction et d’organisation ;

­-  Fortes expériences en suivi et évaluation de projets considérées comme un atout ;

- ­ Excellente capacité rédactionnelle et orale en langue malagasy et française et bonne connaissance de l’anglais;

­-  Maitrise des outils informatiques.

5. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous de 08 heures à 16 heures pendant les jours ouvrables.

6. Le MATSF invite les consultants individuels qualifiés à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services decrits ci-dessus. Les consultants interessés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Son dossier de candidature comprendra entre autre :

a. Lettre de motivation

b. Curriculum vitae avec coordonnées ( adresse, téléphone, e-mail)

c. Copie des diplômes, attestation de formations

d. Certificat/ attestation de prestations similaires

e. Trois références professionnelles

En cas d’envoi de manifestation par e-mail, le Candidat fournira toutes les pièces en un seul fichier PDF.

7. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) » septième édition septembre 2025, relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts sont applicables.

8. Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode Sélection de Consultant Individuel telle que décrite dans le Règlement. Les candidats présélectionnés à l’issue de l’examen des dossiers seront convoqués à un entretien.

9. Les consultants Individuels interessés sont invités à demander par courriel la version électronique des termes de référence de la mission à l’adresse ci-dessous. Le nom, le contact ainsi que l’adresse physique et électronique du consultant individuel devront être spécifiés dans la demande.

10. Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être déposés et/ou envoyés par courriel , au plus tard le 08 octobre 2026 à 16 heures à l’adresse ci-dessous, en mentionnant la référence :

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

AMI N°05 - 2026/MATSF/PRODUIRE

Recrutement d’un Spécialiste en gestion des risques sociaux

 

11. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est:

Contract Title: Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Kyiv HPP / PSP, Kaniv, Kremenchuk and Seredniodniprovska Hydropower Plants, including related services (training of UHE staff) (hereinafter referred to ‘the Contract’) comprising the following lots:

Lot 1: Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Kyiv HPP / PSP, including related services (training of UHE staff) (46 MW BESS capacity).

Lot 2: Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Kaniv HPP, including related services (training of UHE staff) (66 MW BESS capacity).

Lot 3: Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Kremenchuk HPP, including related services (training of UHE staff) (60 MW BESS capacity).

Lot 4: Design, Supply and Installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with Energy Management Systems (EMS) and Ancillary Equipment at Seredniodniprovska HPP, including related services (training of UHE staff) (25 MW BESS capacity).

Source of financing:

IBRD Loan No.: 9284-UA;

CTF Loan No.: TF0B5994;

CTF Loan No.: TF0C5903-UA; and

CTF Grant No.: TF-0B5724.

Project ID: P176114

RFB reference No.: UHE-IPSR-DSI-1

1. Private Joint Stock Company “Ukrhydroenergo” (PJSC “Ukrhydroenergo” or UHE) has received financing from the World Bank (hereinafter referred to as the “Bank”) toward the cost of the Project “Ukraine – Improving Power System Resilience for European Power Grid Integration (Installation of Hybrid Systems for Electricity Production in Ukrhydroenergo)” and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the Contract. Under this Contract, UHE intends to make payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.

2. PJSC “Ukrhydroenergo” now invites eligible Bidders to submit Bids for the Contract. Bidders can bid for any one lot, more than one lot or all the four lots. The Time for Completion shall be between 420 and 510 calendar days from the Effective Date of the Contract. No credit will be given for early completion, and Bids offering a Time for Completion exceeding 510 days shall be rejected.

3. Prospective Bidders shall meet the following minimum qualification requirements:

(a) General Experience: Experience in activities related to the design, supply and installation of equipment for energy infrastructure facilities, including generating facilities, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and MV and HV grids, under contracts in the role of contractor, subcontractor, or management contractor since at least January 2020. Design and construction experience may be from different contracts.

(b) Financial Capabilities: The Bidder shall submit audited balance sheets or, if not required by the law of the Bidder’s country, other financial statements acceptable to UHE for the last five (5) fiscal years to demonstrate the current soundness of the Bidder’s financial position and its prospective long-term profitability.

(c) Average Annual Turnover:

The Bidder shall demonstrate a minimum average annual turnover for the last three (3) fiscal years as follows:

Lot 1 – USD 36 million;

Lot 2 – USD 51 million;

Lot 3 – USD 46 million;

Lot 4 – USD 20 million.

Bidders submitting Bids for multiple Lots shall meet the cumulative average annual turnover requirements applicable to those Lots.

The Bidder must demonstrate access to, or availability of, financial resources such as liquid assets, unencumbered real assets, lines of credit, and other financial means, other than any contractual advance payments, to meet the following minimum cash-flow requirements:

Lot 1 – USD 9 million;

Lot 2 – USD 13 million;

Lot 3 – USD 12 million;

Lot 4 – USD 5 million.

Bidders submitting Bids for multiple Lots shall meet the combined financial resources requirements applicable to those Lots.

(d) Specific Experience:

(i) The Bidder shall demonstrate participation as contractor, joint venture member, subcontractor, or management contractor in at least two (2) contracts since 01.01.2020, each of which has been successfully and fully completed and has a minimum power and energy capacity of at least:

Lot 1 – 35 MW / 35 MWh;

Lot 2 – 50 MW / 50 MWh;

Lot 3 – 48 MW / 48 MWh;

Lot 4 – 20 MW / 20 MWh.

Completion shall be based on obtaining of the Operational Acceptance Certificate, Commissioning Certificate, Taking Over Certificate, Commercial Operation Certificate, Facility Readiness Certificate, or equivalent documents demonstrating successful completion.

The similarity of the contracts shall be based on experience in the design, supply and installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems, either as a stand-alone facility or as part of a larger power project, including but not limited to a hybrid renewable energy project.

The referenced contracts shall demonstrate experience covering design, supply and installation of the relevant facility under the Bidder’s overall contractual responsibility.

A Bidder submitting Bids for more than one Lot shall meet the specific experience requirement for the largest individual Lot for which it is bidding. The experience related to design could have been met even through a specialized subcontractor.

(ii) For the contracts specified above and/or other relevant contracts, the Bidder shall demonstrate experience in, inter alia, the following activities:

A. For any Lot: at least one (1) successfully and fully completed contract involving the performance of/participation in an IEC 62443 Security Risk Assessment and implementation of Cyber Security concepts in accordance with IEC 62443-3-3, SL-2/3 level.

B. For Lots 1, 2 and 4: design, construction and commissioning of at least one (1) HV substation of at least 110 (150) kV class. New-build, refurbishment, rehabilitation, extension, reconstruction and modernization projects shall be acceptable.

C. For any Lot: design and construction of at least one (1) successfully and fully completed BESS project with a total installed capacity of at least 10 MW, with confirmed integration of the BESS into a power system operating in accordance with ENTSO-E requirements.

D. Design, with proof of positive state expertise, of at least one (1) project of the applicable consequences class in the field of industry or energy (production facilities; generation, distribution, transmission):

for Lots 2 and 3 – CC3;

for Lots 1 and 4 – CC2.

E. For any Lot: design in accordance with the requirements of Order No. 45 of the Ministry of Regional Development and Construction dated November 16, 2011, in the field of industry or energy (production facilities; generation, distribution, transmission) – at least one (1) project.

F. For Lot 4: design of projects involving connection to the Transmission System Operator (TSO) and/or Distribution System Operator networks – at least one (1) project.

These experience requirements listed under item (ii) may also be met through proposed specialized subcontractor(s).

Full and detailed qualification requirements, as well as additional information on the scope of the Contract and the technical, commercial and other requirements, are provided in the Bidding Document.

 

4. Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (November 2020 edition) (Procurement Regulations) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

The procurement process will be conducted through the national electronic procurement system Prozorro, available at https://prozorro.gov.ua/, including authorized electronic marketplaces through which UHE and Bidders shall interact with the system. The RFB documents, amendments and clarifications will be published on the Prozorro website and on all authorized electronic marketplaces with free access at the following link: https://prozorro.gov.ua/uk/tender/UA-2026-09-15-013943-a

In order to submit the Bid and/or request clarifications, the Bidder shall register at one of the authorized electronic marketplaces of the Bidder’s choice in accordance with the terms and conditions of the selected marketplace.

5. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the Bidding Document. The weight assigned to the Rated Criteria (technical and non-price factors) is: 50% (fifty percent); the weight assigned to the Cost factors is: 50% (fifty percent). 

[NOTE: Due to Prozorro system limitations the weight assigned to the Cost factors is shown as 100% (hundred percent), which should be ignored. For details, refer to the Bidding Documents.]

The Rated Criteria include:

()  Cyber security and supply chain risks management approach;

() Availability of a technical support center to provide technical support related to the maintenance and repair of the key equipment;

() Organization of Construction and Installation Works Under Wartime Conditions; and

(iv) Implementation of sustainable development and environmental responsibility policies.

6. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain additional information from the Bidding Document published at the link provided above. Requests for clarification shall be submitted by the Bidder no later than 14 days before the deadline for submission of Bids specified in the electronic procurement system. Prospective Bidders are invited to attend the pre-Bid meeting, which will be organized by UHE in the format of a video conference. Detailed information about the date, time and registration is provided in the Bidding Document.

7. Bids shall be submitted by uploading the complete Bid through the electronic procurement system before the Bid submission deadline, which is 16:00 (Kyiv time) on November 12, 2026. After the deadline, Bidders will not be able to submit Bids and this option will be automatically closed by the system. Further details on the electronic Bid submission process are provided in the Bidding Document.

8. A Bid Security shall not be required. Each Bid shall be accompanied by a Bid-Securing Declaration using the form provided in the Bidding Document.

9. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring UHE to disclose information on the successful Bidder’s beneficial ownership in the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form included in the Bidding Document.

Anuncio Específico de Adquisiciones

 

Solicitud de Ofertas

Obras

(Poscalificación | Una etapa - Un sobre)

 

Contratante: Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Provincial del Guayas

Proyecto: VÍAS RURALES RESILIENTES

Título del contrato: “REHABILITACION DE LA VÍA EL DESEO – LA INMACULADA - CRUCE BUENO, CANTÓN YAGUACHI”

País: Ecuador

N.° de préstamo: IBRD-97220

SDO n.°: EC-PREFGUAYAS-498815-CW-RFB.

Emitido el: 16 de septiembre de 2026

1.      Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Provincial del Guayas ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para financiar parcialmente el costo de Proyecto Vías Rurales Resilientes P504400 BM, y se propone utilizar parte de los fondos de este para efectuar los pagos estipulados en el Contrato[1] para REHABILITACION DE LA VÍA EL DESEO – LA INMACULADA - CRUCE BUENO, CANTÓN YAGUACHI.

2.      El Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Provincial del Guayas invita a los Licitantes elegibles a presentar Ofertas en sobres cerrados para REHABILITACION DE LA VÍA EL DESEO – LA INMACULADA - CRUCE BUENO, CANTÓN YAGUACHI, obra que contribuirá a garantizar la conectividad vial permanente, segura y resiliente de la vía San Joaquín – San Luis, así como a mejorar la movilidad rural y las condiciones socioeconómicas de los habitantes del sector.

3.      La Licitación se llevará a cabo mediante adquisiciones competitivas nacionales utilizando el método de Solicitud de Ofertas (SDO), conforme a lo previsto en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, Séptima Edición, septiembre 2025  de las “Regulaciones de Adquisiciones”), y se encuentra abierta a todos los Licitantes elegibles, como se los define en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones en la SECCIÓN VI. “Métodos De Selección Aprobados: Bienes, Obras Y Servicios De No Consultoría” en su numeral 6.29 “Una Etapa, Un Sobre”.

4.      Los licitantes elegibles que estén interesados podrán obtener los documentos de solicitud de ofertas en la siguiente    página web institucional: https://guayas.gob.ec/vias-rurales-resilientes-en-la-provincia-del-guayas-banco-mundial/contrataciones-documentos/

5.      Los Licitantes podrán formular solicitudes de aclaración hasta el 28 de septiembre de 2026, las cuales deberán remitirse exclusivamente por correo electrónico a la siguiente dirección: adquisiciones.bm@guayas.gob.ec  

6.      Se celebrará una reunión de información para posibles aclaraciones previo a la presentación de ofertas. La reunión se llevará cabo el día 22 de septiembre de 2026, a las 15h00, mediante la herramienta de teams, a la que libremente podrán asistir todos los interesados que así lo deseen, más información en https://guayas.gob.ec/vias-rurales-resilientes-en-la-provincia-del-guayas-banco-mundial/contrataciones-documentos/

7.      Las ofertas deberán hacerse llegar en sobre cerrado a la dirección indicada abajo, hasta las 14h00 del 05 de noviembre de 2026. Las ofertas electrónicas no serán permitidas. Las ofertas que se reciban fuera de plazo serán rechazadas. Las ofertas se abrirán una (01) hora después del cierre de presentación de ofertas en presencia de los representantes de los licitantes que deseen asistir en persona en la dirección indicada al final de este llamado.

 8.      La dirección referida arriba es:

 

Luque 406 y Pichincha, Edificio Banco Park, piso 14, Sala de reuniones de la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto del Banco Mundial, adquisiciones.bm@guayas.gob.ec

    

 

Atentamente,

rows.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT – FIRMS SELECTION)

Regional Emergency Preparedness and Access to Inclusive Recovery (REPAIR) Program Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA)

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.: TF0C5097-3E

Assignment Title: Third-Party Monitoring Agent (TPMA) for the REPAIR Program - Framework Agreement

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MZ-REPAIR-549332-CS-QBS

ARC Ltd, acting on behalf of the participating countries, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Emergency Preparedness and Access to Inclusive Recovery (REPAIR) Program, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") consist of engaging one or more Third-Party Monitoring Agent(s) (TPMA) to: (i) verify that funds disbursed under REPAIR's Regional Climate Risk Fund (RCRF) financial instruments, following an eligible shock activation, are used by Delivery Channels for their intended purposes and reach targeted beneficiaries, in compliance with the REPAIR Governance Framework; (ii) confirm compliance of the activities implemented by Delivery Channels with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework and applicable national regulations; (iii) evaluate the impact of the response on selected beneficiaries; and (iv) document lessons learned and recommendations to strengthen future REPAIR activations. Services will be delivered across up to eight participating countries (Mozambique, Madagascar, Comoros, Burundi, Angola, Malawi, Zambia, and Seychelles) under a Framework Agreement with an initial term of two years and renewable based on performance. During the framework term, the selected Firm(s) will submit technical and financial proposals in response to country-specific call-off orders issued following individual REPAIR activations.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

ARC Ltd now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

1. Internationally recognized expertise in financial auditing of public institutions and in environmental and social (E&S) monitoring and auditing, evidenced by recognized professional certifications in auditing and financial management and demonstrated fluency in applicable international or national auditing standards.

2. At least 10 years of proven experience in financial management, E&S monitoring, and operational auditing in Sub-Saharan Africa, including in contexts of fragility and crisis response, with a minimum of two completed Third-Party Monitoring Agent (or equivalent third-party monitoring) assignments. Experience in disaster response will be considered a competitive advantage.

3. Demonstrated organizational capacity to deliver assignments across all eight REPAIR countries (Mozambique, Madagascar, Comoros, Burundi, Angola, Malawi, Zambia, and Seychelles); consortia of firms are encouraged to apply to achieve the required geographic coverage.

4. Demonstrated ability to mobilize experts fluent in English, French, and Portuguese across all REPAIR countries. This is a mandatory requirement; single firms or consortia that cannot collectively demonstrate full trilingual operational capacity will not be considered for the Framework Agreement.

5. Demonstrated knowledge of the World Bank's fiduciary and environmental and social frameworks, evidenced by at least one completed assignment under a World Bank- or donor-financed project within the last seven years.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlist will contain 5 to 8 firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, first published in July 2016 and revised in September 2025, Seventh Edition ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

For the purposes of this assignment, a conflict of interest exists where a firm, consortium member, or any of their proposed key personnel has a financial, contractual, institutional, or other relationship - whether current or recent - that could affect, or be reasonably perceived to affect, their ability to carry out this assignment with full independence, objectivity, and impartiality. This includes any ongoing or recent engagement with the Ministries of Finance and Planning, delivery channel operators, project contractors, or other entities directly involved in the implementation of the REPAIR Program in any of the eight participating countries.

Interested firms are requested to identify and disclose, as part of their Expression of Interest submission, any actual or potential conflict of interest relevant to this assignment and to indicate how such conflict has been or could be mitigated.

Any undisclosed conflict of interest identified at any stage may result in disqualification

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Framework Agreement arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Further information can be obtained by sending an inquiry to the following e-mail address: procurementrepair@ltd.arc.int.

Expressions of interest must be submitted by e-mail to procurementrepair@ltd.arc.int no later than the 05th of October 2026 at17h00 hours (South Africa time). The e-mail subject line should clearly state: "MZ-REPAIR-549332-CS-QBS – Third-Party Monitoring Agent (TPMA) for the REPAIR Program – Framework Agreement".

APPEL À MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN(E) SPECIALISTE EN SUIVI EVALUATION DE L’UNITE DE GESTION DU PROJET PRODUIRE

Pays : MADAGASCAR

AMI N : 06-2026/MATSF/PRODUIRE

Projet : PROJET DE DEVELOPPEMENT URBAIN INTEGRE ET RESILIENT POUR L’EMPLOI

Crédit : IDA 8089 MG

Date de lancement : 16 septembre 2026

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de 225 millions USD de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) au profit du Projet de Développement Urbain Integré et Résilient pour l’Emploi (PRODUIRE) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour financer le contrat de services d’un Spécialiste en Suivi Evaluation de l’Unité de Gestion de Projet à Antananarivo.

L’Objectif de Développement du Projet (ODP) est de renforcer la résilience climatique des communautés urbaines, d'améliorer l'administration foncière et de soutenir l'emploi dans certaines villes.

2. Les services du consultant (« les services ») consistent à fournir une expertise au projet pour assurer la coordination et le suivi technique de toutes les activités programmatiques, les reporting ainsi que le suivi évaluation de toutes les activités du projet : planification, suivi de la mise en œuvre et évaluation interne des résultats des activités des composantes.

3. Le mandat fera l’objet d’un contrat de 60 mois assorti d’une tranche ferme de douze mois et de 04 tranches conditionnelles de 12 mois dont la condition d’affermissement sera l’évaluation positive de la perfomance du consultant. Un période d’essai de 6 mois est prévue dans la tranche ferme. Le lieu de travail est au siège du projet à Antananarivo.

4. Le Spécialiste en Suivi Evaluation doit répondre au profil suivant :

Être titulaire d’un Diplôme de Maîtrise en économie, statistique ou dans une discipline et/ou expérience similaire ;

Disposer d’une expérience probante d’au moins 5 ans dans le domaine du Suivi et Evaluation de projets de développement, incluant la conception et la mise en place de systèmes de S&E, la gestion d'enquêtes terrain (baseline et endline), et le reporting vers des bailleurs de fonds internationaux ;

Avoir des compétences et expériences avérées dans le développement, planification et gestion des programmes ;

Avoir des compétences et expériences avérées dans la collecte et l'analyse de données issues de sources variées : enquêtes ménages, entretiens avec des informateurs clés (KII), groupes de discussion (FGD), et données administratives ou institutionnelles ;

Avoir une connaissance des méthodes quantitatives d'évaluation d'impact (différence-en-différences, appariement par score de propension, ou méthodes quasi-expérimentales équivalentes), nécessaire pour superviser la conception et l'analyse des enquêtes baseline et endline prévues dans le cadre de l'évaluation d'impact des activités foncières du Projet

Avoir une forte capacité rédactionnelle, de communication, d’analyse et de synthèse ;

Avoir une maîtrise parfaite parlée et écrite du français et de malagasy ;

Être familier avec les projets financés par les bailleurs de fonds :

o Une maîtrise de l’approche du cadre logique et d’autres approches stratégiques de planification ;

o Une maîtrise des méthodes et approche de suivi évaluation (quantitative, qualitative et participatif) des projets ;

o Une maîtrise de l’élaboration et de la mise en place de système de suivi évaluation et de planification.

Disposer des références au cours des 2 dernières années faisant état d'une aptitude à organiser son travail ainsi que d’une discrétion et d'une intégrité professionnelle. Une enquête de moralité sera effectuée avant signature du contrat.

 

Atouts :

Expériences avec les projets de développement financés par la Banque Mondiale ;

Expérience en suivi-évaluation dans les domaines foncier, habitat et/ou gestion des risques de catastrophes (DRM) ;

Expérience en gestion et analyse de données qualitatives, quantitatives et géospatiales;

Maîtrise d'outils de collecte de données mobiles (KoBoToolbox, ODK, Survey CTO ou équivalent) pour les enquêtes terrain, les études baseline et endline et le suivi des indicateurs sur les sites d'intervention du Projet

Une bonne compréhension de l’Anglais.

5. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous de 08 heures à 16 heures pendant les jours ouvrables.

6. Le MATSF invite les consultants individuels qualifiés à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services decrits ci-dessus. Les consultants interessés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des Services. Son dossier de candidature comprendra entre autre :

a.Lettre de motivation

b.Curriculum vitae avec coordonnées ( adresse, téléphone, e-mail)

c.Copie des diplômes, attestation de formations

d.Certificat/ attestation de prestations similaires

e.Trois références professionnelles

En cas d’envoi de manifestation par e-mail, le Candidat fournira toutes les pièces en un seul fichier PDF.

7. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) » septième édition septembre 2025, relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts sont applicables.

8. Un consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode Sélection de Consultant Individuel telle que décrite dans le Règlement. Les candidats présélectionnés à l’issue de l’examen des dossiers seront convoqués à un entretien.

9. Les consultants Individuels interessés sont invités à demander par courriel la version électronique des termes de référence de la mission à l’adresse ci-dessous. Le nom, le contact ainsi que l’adresse physique et électronique du consultant individuel devront être spécifiés dans la demande.

10. Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être déposés et/ou envoyés par courriel , au plus tard le 08 octobre 2026 à 16 heures à l’adresse ci-dessous, en mentionnant la référence :

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

AMI N°06- 2026/MATSF/PRODUIRE

Recrutement d’un Spécialiste en Suivi Evaluation

 

11. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est :

MINISTRY OF PLANNING

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Assignment Title: CONSULTING SERVICES FOR NEEDS ASSESSMENT, TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS, AND SUPPORT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTEGRATED BORDER INTELLIGENCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT SOLUTION

Reference No. 98CS1/MINPLAN/26

The Government of Angola has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Needs Assessment, Technical Specifications, and Support for the Development of an Integrated Border Intelligence and Risk Management Solution.

Consulting Services (“the Services”) aim to provide technical support to the Coordinated Border Management Committee (CGCF) in all phases prior to and during the development of an Integrated Border Intelligence and Risk Management Solution. The role of the consulting firm includes:

  1. Identifying the functional and operational needs at the borders, mapping and reviewing existing processes, and inventorying technological systems in use;
  2. Developing the functional and technical architecture of the solution, defining interoperability requirements, creating a data dictionary and data model, and estimating the development and implementation costs;
  3. Assisting in the preparation of the bidding documents for the selection of the technology development company and issuing a substantiated technical opinion on the recommended proposal;
  4. Technically supervising the development of the solution by the contracted company, verifying compliance with the approved technical specifications, validating deliverables and progress reports, and supporting the testing and implementation at border points;
  5. Evaluating the national legal and regulatory framework relevant to the implementation of the solution, identifying gaps, and providing advice and support to the CGCF to address them;
  6. Preparing detailed technical specifications for the core module of the solution, covering general principles, the complete risk management cycle, the risk management engine, the alert system, intelligence governance and human review, auditing, monitoring and performance, and the incorporation of artificial intelligence.

The expected duration of the consultancy contract will be twenty-four (24) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • A minimum of 7 years of proven experience in process reengineering and/or IT systems specification projects;
  • Demonstrable experience in projects related to border management, customs, immigration, or public safety;
  • Preference given to companies with MININT pre-approval to handle confidential government data;
  • PMP (Project Management Professional) certification, which validates project management skills;
  • ITIL Service Strategy Certification, which demonstrates skills in IT service strategy;
  • TOGAF® Certification Program, which demonstrates expertise in the development and implementation of enterprise architecture, essential for ensuring data integration and efficiency in the integration of complex systems;
  • Must be formally registered with the APD, ensuring compliance with current regulations regarding data protection and privacy;
  • Preference will be given to companies that hold the “Made in Angola” seal in the areas of telecommunications and/or information systems, in accordance with Presidential Decree No. 213/23, which establishes the Legal Framework for Incentives to Domestic Production;
  • Must be duly registered with the National Institute for the Promotion of the Information Society (INFOSI), ensuring that it operates in accordance with national guidelines for technological development;
  • Submit a certificate of tax compliance, proving its good standing with the tax authorities and ensuring its suitability to perform the contract.
  • Demonstrate institutional, technical, and reputational suitability consistent with national security projects and the management of sensitive information;
  • Ensure that its key employees involved in the project undergo background checks, in accordance with applicable law;
  • Comply with any additional guidelines, restrictions, or requirements established by MININT regarding the protection of national security
