Terms of Reference

Individual Consultant for Final Review of the “Sustainable Fisheries Development in Red Sea and Gulf of Aden” Project (SFISH Project)

 

Program/Project Number:

P178143

Activity Code:

PERSGA-2403-CS-INDV

Type of contract; and expected start/end dates of assignment

Lump-sum, based on linked deliverables;

During October 2026 -February 2027

 

  1. Background

1.1. Context

The Regional Organization for Conservation of the Marine Environment of the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden (PERSGA) is an intergovernmental organization established since 1995. PERSGA institutional framework is based on the Regional Convention for the Conservation of the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden Environment (Jeddah Convention 1982), which joins seven member states, including Djibouti, Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, and Yemen. Rational use of marine resources and the protection of coastal marine environment from pollution and overexploitation are central objectives of Jeddah Convention (1982) and its derived Action Plan Regional Protocols and Action Plan. PERSGA runs regional programs and projects that support regional capacities and coordination to achieve these objectives.

This consultancy is carried out in the framework of the implementation of the regional project “Sustainable Fisheries Development in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden”, referred to hereafter as SFISH project. The project is financed by the World Bank (WB), and executed by PERSGA for its regional component. In accordance with the M&E policies and procedures of WB, a Final Evaluation of the SFISH project is required.  The project has started on August 2022 and is approaching its closing by March 2027. This TOR sets out the prospect for the project Final Evaluation.

1.2 Background on SFISH project (Regional Component)

PERSGA is executing the SFISH project Regional Component, which composes the subject of this Final Evaluation TOR. This Component aims to strengthen regional collaboration in management of marine fisheries and aquaculture in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. Its focus is to improve and sustain regional collaboration through further development of PERSGA’s capacities for monitoring, assessment, knowledge management and sharing to support science-based management of fisheries in the RSGA. It supports the development of a regional platform for coordination of policies, legislation, management plans and measures for responsible fisheries and aquaculture and use of ecosystems approaches. It also supports regional level capacity building and technical assistance program on management of living marine resources responding to both anthropogenic and climate induced changes. This would include training, providing technical guidelines, support the development of policies, legislation, management plans and completion, ratification and implementation of relevant regional conventions, action plans and protocols. The project regional component interventions were designed to be through the following interlinked subcomponents:

  1. PERSGA Regional Information Management System (RIMS), monitoring network and institutional capacity. This subcomponent aims to strengthen the capacity of PERSGA, as a regional organization, to compile fisheries and related data collected or received from the countries and make this information available to all member states. It provides goods and services to improve IT hardware and software of the RIMS housed in PERSGA, and networking to allow it to perform integrated functions. The subcomponent also supports PERSGA system capacity for monitoring marine environment, including on climate change impact in the RSGA area, tracking pollution spills, and coordination of emergency response that have implications to protection of fisheries and their critical habitats. It also supports updating PERSGA institutional guidelines as needed, such as for finance and procurement policy and procedures, project cycle management, and environmental and social risks assessment and management.
  2. Regional platforms for capacity building and regional coordination of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in the regional management mechanism. This subcomponent supports capacity development, technical assistance and setting up of platforms for effective coordination on fishery management at the regional level. It supports PERSGA to develop technical manuals for cost-effective approaches of harmonized fisheries data and information collection and management adapted to the region, incorporating supplementary guidelines for monitoring, and assessing IUU fishing, fish stock status etc., and a regional mechanism to share information with member states on fishery statistics and knowledge. It will also support PERSGA to develop technical guidelines to promote capacities to effectively coordinate efforts for fisheries management, policies, and legislation; protection and restoration of critical fish habitat; environmental and biosecurity best practices in aquaculture, building climate resilience and regional mechanism to interact with relevant international efforts. The activity will also include support to PERSGA in developing a Regional Plan of Action for combating IUU fishing (RPOA-IUU), and other specific action plans concerning conservation of vulnerable non target species such as sharks, turtles, seabirds and marine mammals. These action plans would provide an umbrella mechanism for cooperation and coordination of measures to combat IUU fishing, and other conservation measures related to RSGA fisheries.
  3. Enhanced knowledge management, communication strategies and awareness for citizen, private sector and development partner engagement in the regional sustainable fishery mechanism. This subcomponent includes technical assistance, consultations, and operating costs for supporting citizen, private sector and development partner engagement and raising awareness through effective communication on regional cooperation actions, including improved activities that demonstrate cooperation and coordination among the regional countries. It also supports the development of special awareness activities, including production and dissemination of educational materials (videos, media toolkits, brochures, pamphlets, etc.) addressing fishery issues due to anthropogenic actions and climate change, and communication workshops to enhance their engagement.

Further detailed information on the project, and related project documents can be reached at the following link: https://sfish.persga.org/

  1. Consultancy

2.1 Objectives of the Final Evaluation (FE)

The objective of the FE is to provide an independent assessment of the project’s achievements, outcomes and potential longer-term impacts. As an end-of-project evaluation undertaken during the final implementation period, the FE will assess performance over the implementation period up to an evaluation cut-off date agreed during inception, with material implementation developments and final results updated through completion of the evaluation where any evidence becomes available. It will consider forward-looking in capturing lessons learned and providing evidence on the nature and extent of results, their likely sustainability, and implications for future programming.

The evaluation will thus assess the project design, scope, implementation and achievements. It will collate and analyse lessons learnt, challenges faced and best practices obtained during implementation, which will inform the next programming strategy in response to its priorities, and make recommendations regarding the specific actions in this regard. These should emphasize, for example issues to be addressed in the future follow up interventions, significant outcomes and success stories for potential expansion and replication. 

2.2 Scope and Approach of the FE

The FE should provide evidence-based information that is credible, reliable and useful. The consultant is expected to follow a participatory and consultative approach ensuring close engagement with the Project team at PERSGA, and government counterparts of the member countries including PERSGA Focal Points, National Coordinators of the project, and key stakeholders. The review consultant is expected to conduct a field mission to view project interventions and achievements, and partake in meetings and workshop organized in the framework of the FE process. Interviews will be held with the following organizations and individuals at a minimum:

    • PERSGA staff who have project responsibilities;
    • Project National Coordinators
    • Stakeholders, including the beneficiaries in at least two of the Participating Countries,

The consultant will review all relevant sources of information, such as the project documents, project implementation progress reports, financial reports, activities’ reports, strategic and legal documents, World Bank aide memoires from support meetings, outputs and products and any other material that he / she considers useful for this evidence-based review and evaluation.

The FE shall review and validate the project's Theory of Change (ToC). In this connection, the evaluation shall assess whether the assumptions and causal pathways underlying project design remained valid during implementation, and examine the extent to which project interventions, outputs, and intermediate results contributed to the achievement of intended outcomes and development objectives. The assessment should identify key enabling factors and constraints that influenced results achievement and sustainability.

The Project FE will assess the effectiveness of the implementation strategy and the results. This will include the implementation modalities, responsibilities and co-financing roles, coordination and partnership arrangements, institutional strengthening, beneficiary participation, training and workshop attendance and outcomes, replication and sustainability of the project outcomes. The evaluation will include review of the project design and assumptions made at the beginning of the project development process; project management including the implementation strategies; project activities, so as to assess the extent to which the project results have been achieved, partnerships established, capacities built, and cross cutting issues of mainstreaming development issues. It will also assess whether the project implementation strategy has been optimum and recommend areas for improvement and learning for future programming interventions.

To achieve the FE objectives following relevant World Bank and PERSGA guidelines, the consultant will consider the following categories of project performance. For each of the Relevance, Efficacy and Efficiency categories, and for the overall assessment, the consultant is required to apply the rating scales set out below. The sustainability and risks to development outcomes will be assessed descriptively, i.e. rating is not required; however, the main risks and enabling factors should be clearly identified and prioritized.

      1. Relevance

The FE will assess the extent to which the project objectives, design and focus are relevant to the identified problem and needs. It will also assess how the project interventions approached are realistic, appropriate, and responsive to changes for achieving project objectives. Thus, the Relevance of objectives assesses: (i) the alignment with the partnership framework of the World Bank and PERSGA  and pertaining development strategy at the time the operation is closed; (ii) appropriateness of the PDO given the client’s implementation capacity; and (iii) the extent to which the PDO was responsive to the changing circumstances. The explanation of the alignment of the PDO includes a description of the development problem the project sought to address and how this problem was addressed through the project’s interventions given the context and existing capacity.

Rating:  Considering the above, the Relevance of PDO will be rated using a four-point scale, including High, Substantial, Modest, and Negligible, as follows

 

High:

Full alignment with the priorities of the regional framework and development strategy; PDO was appropriately pitched and responsive to changing circumstances 

Substantial:

Largely aligned with the priorities of the regional framework and development strategy, with minor shortcomings in appropriateness or responsiveness.

Modest:

Partial alignment with the priorities of the regional framework and development strategy, or notable shortcomings in appropriateness or responsiveness

Negligible:

Very limited alignment with the priorities of the regional framework and development strategy, with major shortcomings in appropriateness or responsiveness

2.2.2 Efficacy

Assessing the project Efficacy is the core section in this Final Evaluation, as well as in the Learning and Results Note (LRN) for Investment Project Financing Operation of the World Bank. Efficacy is defined as the extent to which the project objectives were achieved, or are expected to be achieved, and that achievement is attributable to the activities or actions supported by the project, or to what extent the project’s activities contributed to the achievement of the objective(s). The PDO statement conveys the benefits (changes) expected to flow to the beneficiaries, expressed in terms of development outcomes, rather than stating financed activities and outputs.  Thus, to examine the project Efficacy, the FE will consider several aspects, such as:

  • Achievement of the Project development objectives: including through Results Framework (RF) Indicators, outputs and outcomes assessments. The RF can provide logical information to measure achievement of each expected outcome in the PDO statement through examining data on indicators document, observed achievements and compare them to baselines and targets.  However, it is important to assess efficacy at the level of expected outcomes rather than just presenting data of the project’s results indicators. It will be useful to also look beyond the Results Framework to any other available data and evidence. Where applicable, the efficacy section would also discuss here achievement of cross-cutting and corporate objectives, such as contribution to institutional strengthening and other development objectives (e.g. relevant SDGs
  • Project management performance by PERSGA: including through assessing management processes and appropriateness in supporting implementation and delivering results; Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) quality assessment; implementation strategies; responding to the needs of the beneficiaries; involving stakeholders; adaptive management to overcome obstacles/challenges, or grasping opportunity to upscale/ expand results;

Rating:  Considering the above, the project Efficacy will be rated using a four-point scale, including High, Substantial, Modest, and Negligible, as follows:

High:

The Project fully achieved or exceeded its objectives (or intended outcomes) or is likely to do so

Substantial:

The Project almost fully achieved its objectives (or intended outcomes) or is likely to do so

Modest:

The Project partly achieved its objectives (or intended outcomes) or is likely to do so

Negligible:

The Project barely achieved its objectives (or intended outcomes) or is likely to do so

2.2.3 Efficiency

The FE will assess the efficiency of the project implementation with regard to:

  • Utilizing the fund resources, where actual/ expected results justify costs incurred;
  • Synergy and coordination with other overlapping and similar interventions (funded nationally and /or by other donors);
  • Considering collaboration with the national institutions and development partners;
  • Management structures, procedure and accountability;
  • Performance in project management, coordination, procurement and financial management, reporting, stakeholder engagement, and responsiveness to implementation challenges.

Rating:  Considering the above, the project Efficiency will be rated using a four-point scale, including High, Substantial, Modest, and Negligible, as follows:

High:

Efficiency exceeds expectations

Substantial:

Efficiency is what would be expected in the project/ operation’s sector.

Modest:

Efficiency is below expectations in the project/ operation’s sector.

Negligible:

Efficiency is very low in comparison with both the benefits (if any) and with recognized norms in the project/ operation’s sector.

2.2.4 Overall Outcome

This FE will assess the Overall Outcome in a very brief (1-2 sentences) description. This will be based on the integrated assessment of Relevance, Efficacy, and Efficiency above.

Rating:  Overall Outcome rating is derived by combining the assessments of Relevance, Efficacy, and Efficiency, using a 6-point scale, as follows:

Highly Satisfactory:

There were no shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

Satisfactory:

There were minor shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

Moderately Satisfactory:

There were moderate shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

Moderately Unsatisfactory:

There were significant shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

Unsatisfactory:

There were major shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance.

Highly Unsatisfactory:

There were severe shortcomings in the project’s achievement of its objectives, in its efficiency, or in its relevance

2.2.5 Sustainability and Risks to Development Outcomes

The FE will assess how sustainability issues were considered in the project design, planning and implementation, examining:

  • The extent that the benefits of the project are likely to be sustained after the completion of this project; exit strategies, and approaches to phase out assistance provided by the project including contributing factors and constraints
  • key risks that may affect maintenance of project outcomes after project closure, including institutional, financial, technical, and regional cooperation risks
  •  Key factors that will require attention in order to improve prospects of sustainability of Project outcome
  • Success stories and potential for their replication/ scaling up of the approaches and outcomes
  • Sustainability of capacities built at the individual and organizational level including a focus on IT systems, data collection and analysis and sustainability of regional data sharing.
  • The extent to which technical manuals, guidelines, and training programs developed under the project incorporate and promote principles of resource efficiency in living marine resources, fisheries and aquaculture management.
  • Assessment of Environmental and Social Performance: the Final Evaluation shall assess the extent to which project implementation complied with the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and relevant Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), including the integration of ESF requirements into project regulatory procedures, implementation, and management. The assessment should review the effectiveness of stakeholder engagement and consultation processes, operation of grievance redress mechanisms, management of labor and working conditions risks, and the extent to which technical assistance activities were designed and implemented in a manner consistent with ESF principles and requirements. The evaluation should identify any environmental or social implementation challenges encountered, assess how they were addressed, and document lessons learned for future operations, main lessons and recommendations for harmonizing or comparable/ interventions in future, e.g. comprehensive proposals for future interventions based on the current evaluation findings.
  • Document cross-cutting outcomes: Assess contributions to institutional strengthening, regional cooperation, capacity building, climate resilience, private sector engagement, and other relevant cross-cutting objectives supported by the project.

 

2.3 Key Evaluation Questions

Articulating the above, the following core questions can guide assessments in the FE. The consultant may refine, add to and operationalize for the inception report and evaluation matrix, which will be subject to agreement with PERSGA:

  • Theory of Change and contribution: To what extent did the project’s assumptions and causal pathways remain valid, and how did project interventions contribute to observed outcomes?
  • Relevance: To what extent did the project objectives, design and interventions remain aligned with regional fisheries and aquaculture priorities, World Bank and PERSGA strategic priorities, beneficiary needs and changing circumstances?
  • Efficacy: To what extent were the PDO and intended outcomes achieved, or are likely to be achieved by project closure, based on the Results Framework and other credible evidence?
  • Efficiency: How efficiently were financial, human and institutional resources, implementation arrangements, procurement, financial management and partnerships used to deliver results?
  • Implementation and management performance: How effective were project governance, coordination, M&E, stakeholder engagement, adaptive management and regional cooperation arrangements?
  • Sustainability and risks: How likely are project benefits, institutional capacities, regional platforms, data systems, partnerships and other results to be sustained after project closure, and what are the principal risks?
  • Environmental, social and cross-cutting performance: To what extent were relevant ESF/ESS requirements and cross-cutting objectives, including institutional strengthening, climate resilience, capacity building and private-sector engagement, effectively addressed?
  • Lessons and future programming: What evidence-based lessons, scalable practices and recommendations should inform future regional fisheries and marine resource management interventions?

3. Expected Deliverables

The following deliverables are expected (see schedule of deliverables below):

3.1 Inception report

The FE consultant will prepare an inception report, which details his/her conception of the assessment, the approach and how the evaluation questions will be addressed. This is to ensure that the evaluator and the stakeholders have a shared view of the assessment. The inception report will include an evaluation matrix summarizing the evaluation design, methodology, questions, data sources, collection and analysis tools, and measures by which questions will be evaluated. The report will include the scope of work, work plan, timeframe after starting the evaluation process. The inception report should include a proposed schedule of tasks; activities and deliverables, with clear responsibilities for each task or product. The inception report will be discussed and agreed upon with PERSGA and project stakeholders.

3.2 Draft assessment report

The FE consultant will prepare a draft Project Assessment Report, cognizant of the proposed format of the report and checklist used for the assessment (outlined in 3.3 below). The draft report will be submitted to PERSGA for review and comments by its review panel and stakeholders, and to validate that the evaluation considered all relevant information and meets the required approach and quality criteria. The report will be produced in English. PERSGA is responsible for ensuring timely arrangement for the review and validation of the report involving stakeholders’ remarks within the allocated time-frame. Within undertaking the assessment and preparation of the draft report, the consultant is expected to carry out field mission to the region in order to collect and confer data and information.

The assessment report should provide extra detailed information as annexes, such as tables with Indicator> Baseline> Target> Actual> Assessment of Achievement, and other similar data. The appraisal should also discuss whether indicators were appropriate measures of the intended outcomes.

3.3 Final FE Report and regional workshop

The consultant shall consider above comments on the draft report to develop the final assessment report. The content and the structure of the final analytical report with findings, recommendations and lessons learnt should cover the above scope of the evaluation and should meet the requirements of M & E for PERSGA and World Bank. Following clearance of the assessment report, the consultant will be invited to participate and present assessment findings and recommendations in the project FE regional workshop.

The content is expected to include (at least) the following:

  • Executive summary (2-4 pages)
  • Introduction (1-2 page)
  • Description of the evaluation approach and methodology (6-8 pages)
  • Project context and rationale (4-6 pages)
  • Achievement of outcomes against objectives
  • Analysis regarding the project progress and achievements of the objectives, outputs and outcomes; challenges, impacts, etc., considering the scope outlined above (10-12 pages)
  • Analysis of opportunities and options for guidance in relevant future interventions (6-8 pages)
  • Other key findings; practices, lessons learned and potential success stories (4-6 pages): Lessons should be evidence-based, actionable, and relevant for future regional fisheries and marine resource management operations, with clear implications for successor interventions.
  • PERSGA performance (2-4 pages)
  • Conclusions and recommendations (4-6 pages)
  • Appendices (charts, tables, terms of reference, itinerary, people interviewed, documents reviewed, further readings, etc)

3.4 Tentative schedule of the consultancy Deliverables

Deliverable

Time Frame

Inception Report

Within one week after signing of contract

Review and agreement on Inception Report

Within one week after submission of the report

Draft Assessment Report (including field mission)

Within six weeks after approval of the inception report

Review of Draft Assessment Report

Within two weeks after submission of the draft report

Final Report with review comments addressed

Within two weeks after receiving PERSGA comments on draft report

Presentation of the key findings and recommendations in FE regional workshop

Within a month from clearing the Final Report

4. Management, Coordination and PERSGA Inputs

4.1 Supervision and review of deliverables

The consultant will report to the designated PERSGA Project Coordinator/official responsible for the SFISH Regional Component. PERSGA will designate a review panel for the assignment and will provide consolidated comments on deliverables within the review periods stated in Section 3.4. Acceptance of deliverables will be based on conformity with this TOR, the agreed inception report and evaluation matrix, and applicable PERSGA and World Bank requirements.

4.2 PERSGA inputs and facilitation

PERSGA will facilitate the assignment by providing or arranging timely access, subject to applicable confidentiality requirements, to relevant project documentation and data, including the Project Appraisal/implementation documents, Results Framework data, progress and financial reports, procurement information, M&E records, aide-memoires, activity reports, technical outputs and other relevant project records. PERSGA will also facilitate contact with National Coordinators, Focal Points and other key stakeholders and support coordination of mission meetings and the regional workshop.

4.3 Independence, confidentiality and conflict of interest

The consultant shall conduct the evaluation independently, impartially and with professional integrity. Any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest shall be disclosed promptly to PERSGA. Information obtained through the assignment shall be treated confidentially where appropriate, and stakeholder views shall be presented in a manner that protects respondents where confidentiality has been requested. Evaluation findings and ratings shall be evidence-based and shall remain the professional responsibility of the consultant.

5. Type of contract, duty station and payment

This contract falls under short-term consultant category system of PERGSA. It is on a lump sum basis, and payment will be in instalments linked with deliverables as specified below.

The consultant will work from homebase, where he/she has access to the relevant technical literature, to prepare for the evaluation. The consultant will undertake a mission to PERSGA region to conduct field assessments and establish required arrangement and networking with review team at PERSGA, and undertaking interviews with relevant participants/beneficiaries, examine project outputs; review & update input information/data, and discuss, thematic approach, layout, analysis results, content, etc. of the draft document.

The payment instalments will be owed as follows:

  • 25% after adoption of the inception report
  • 50% after undertaking the field mission and submission of the draft assessment report
  • 25% after the approval of the final report, participation in the final evaluation workshop and submission of workshop report

6. Required qualifications/expertise and application procedure

  • Advanced degree (preferable PhD) in marine environmental policies, living marine resources/ fisheries management, marine sciences, development policies, economic planning, economics, project management or other related fields.
  • Extensive knowledge and expertise in the field of evaluation of development projects and programs, including working with international organizations and donors, relevant technical areas for at least 15 years.
  • Experience with assessment of similar World Bank and PERSGA projects is preferable. Experience and familiarity with working in the region will be an added value.
  • Knowledge and experience with result-based management and evaluation methodologies, applying indicators and reconstructing or validating baseline scenarios;
  • Demonstrable analytical and reporting skills of international standards;
  • Excellent English communication skills. Arabic and French are advantages.

 

Qualified candidates are requested to submit their updated CVs, together with expression of interest (EOI) to PERSGA in Jeddah, Kingdome of Saudi Arabia, at the email address: sourcing@persga.org. Deadline for receiving application is 26 September 2026.

rows.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Sri Lanka

Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project

Loan No.: 9290-LK

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Detailed Engineering Estimates, Environmental & Social Screening Reports (ESSRs) and Environmental & Social Management Plans (ESMPs) Preparation for 720km Rural Roads

Reference No: LK-RDA-567082-CS-QCBS

The Government of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka (GOSL) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") include engaging a qualified national consultancy firm to prepare Detailed Engineering Estimates (DEEs), Environmental and Social Screening Reports (ESSRs), and Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) or Codes of Environmental and Social Good Practice (CESGPs) for the rehabilitation and improvement of approximately 720 kilometres of rural roads across eight (8) districts in five (5) provinces under the Post-Disaster Recovery Additional Financing component of the ICDP. The Services shall also include conducting a comprehensive economic analysis of the proposed rural road investments and ensuring full integration of climate-resilient design principles, geotechnical assessments, and World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) compliance. The duration of the assignment shall be eight (8) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained from the undersigned or via the following website: https://rda.gov.lk/index.php?option=com_inquiries&view=biddetail&Itemid=130&lang=en.

The Road Development Authority (RDA) now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications, relevant experience, and technical capacity to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core business and years in business; relevant experience; technical and managerial capability of the firm; quality assurance systems and relevant certifications;
  2. General experience of the firm and its capacity to deploy a Team Leader; Environmental Specialist; Social Specialist; Civil Engineers; Geotechnical Specialist; Climate Resilient Expert; and a GIS Officer for the assignment;
  3. Experience in World Bank-funded Environmental and Social Screening; experience in engineering estimates and BOQ preparation; E&S screening/management assignments; Geotechnical and climate-resilient design assignment;
  4. Financial strength based on audited financials; average annual turnover and demonstrated financial capacity to undertake the assignment; and
  5. Relevant experience in Sri Lanka; and/or relevant experience in South Asian countries and/or the wider regional context.

 

Note: 

  1. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.
  2. When providing information relating to (b), it shall be made clear whether the experience of the firm was in the capacity of a principal firm (lead partner) or as an associated firm (sub-consultant/JV partner), with detail regarding the scope of the services.
  3. Firms submitting their EoI response as a Joint Venture (JV) will be evaluated individually for all of the above criteria, while only the lead firm will be evaluated in case of a submission with sub-consultancy or consortium. 

Consultants are requested to submit the following supporting documents against the above- mentioned shortlisting criteria: 

  1. Registration paper of the firm(s).
  2. JV agreement/letter of intent (if applicable).
  3. Firm’s profile / Brochure.
  4. Audited financial reports for the last three years.
  5. Service experience record (including nature, total cost, total input in terms of staff-months, employer, location of service, scope of services, etc.) 
  6. The experience of a parent company, subsidiary company, group company or associates (whatever the name) of the Applicant shall not be considered in evaluation. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.16, 3.17, and 3.18 of the World Bank’s "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" Fifth Edition, September 2023 (Procurement Regulations), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) arrangements described in the Procurement Regulations and to be specifically set out in the Request for Proposals.

Further information can be obtained from the office of the Project Director, Inclusive Connectivity & Development Project (ICDP), during office hours from 09:00 to 15:00 hrs at Inclusive Connectivity & Development Project (ICDP), Road Development Authority, 3rd Floor, 1st Stage, Sethsiripaya, Battaramulla. Telephone: +94 11 2885765 / +94 11 2885766; Facsimile number: +94 11 2885765; Electronic mail address: wbicdpbid@gmail.com

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by email[EB1] ). rows.bid_description: Design and Supervision of the Construction of Three (3) Animal Quarantine Facilities at Gbalamuya (Gbinleh Chiefdom), Limbaya (Sulima Chiefdom), and Kombayendeh (Lei Chiefdom), to Strengthen Animal Health, Disease Surveillance, and Safe Livestock Trade
rows.contact_address:
23 Cantonment Road
 Freetown, Sierra Leone
rows.notice_text:
GOVERNMENT OF SIERRA LEONE
MINISTRY OF HEALTH
INTEGRATED HEALTH PROJECTS ADMINISTRATION UNIT (IHPAU)

Country:                                       Sierra Leone

Name of Project:                         Quality Essential Health Services and Systems Support Project

Project ID:                                   P172102

Assignment Title:                        Recruitment of Consultant for the Design and Supervision of the                                                      Construction of Three (3) Animal Quarantine Facilities at                                                                Gbalamuya (Gbinleh Chiefdom), Limbaya (Sulima Chiefdom),                                                        and Kombayendeh (Lei Chiefdom), to Strengthen Animal                                                               Health, Disease Surveillance, and Safe Livestock Trade   

Reference No:                              SL-MOHS-565445-CS-QCBS

REOI Issued Date:                       Friday 11th September 2026

REOI Closing Date:                     Friday 25th September 2026

  1. The Government of Sierra Leone (GoSL) (hereinafter called "Borrower") has received financing from the Pandemic Fund (hereinafter called Grant") toward the cost of Quality Essential Health Services and Systems Support Project (QEHSSSP). The Borrower intends to apply a portion of the funds to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Proposal is issued.
  2. The Ministry of Health (MoH) Integrated Health Projects Administration Unit (IHPAU) (hereinafter referred to as the "Client") invites you to submit proposals to provide the following consulting services:

The consulting services (“the Services”) include:

  1. Architectural and engineering design services
  2. Preparation of tender documentation
  3. Construction supervision and contract administration
  4. Quality assurance and project monitoring services

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained via email from asumah@mohsihpau.gov.sl  OR from the address given below.

  1. The Ministry of Health now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The main shortlisting criteria are:

  • The qualifications and experience of the firm and
  • The availability of qualified and experienced staff as defined and stipulated in the TOR.
  1. The consulting firm/company shall possess the following qualifications and/or general requirements. The relevant qualification and detail selection criteria shall include, but not limited to:
  • Valid Company Registration Documents.
  • The consulting firm shall have a minimum of 5–10 years of proven experience in architectural and engineering design, and construction supervision services for building & infrastructure projects
  • Adequate multidisciplinary staffing resources availability to carry out the services. The indicative description of required key staffing schedule are Team Leader/Architect, Structural Engineer, Veterinary Specialist, Electrical Engineer, Mechanical Engineer, Environmental Officer, Clerk of Works x 3 and Surveyor
  • 3-5 years proven experience with similar projects in accordance with the building principles of Sierra Leone (Local Code of Standards) or international code of standards.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 , September 2023, February 2025 and September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Quality and Cost Base Selection (QCBS) method as set out in the “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 , September 2023, February 2025 and September 2025

Further information (TOR) can be obtained at the address below. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or courier or e-mail) by 1700 hrs, Friday 25th September 2026.

Attn:  Mr. Alpha Umaru Jalloh

          Team Lead /Fund Management Specialist

          Integrated Health Projects Administration Unit (IHPAU)

          23 Cantonment Road

          Freetown, Sierra Leone

rows.notice_text:
MINISTRY OF LANDS, PUBLIC WORKS, HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

STATE DEPARTMENT FOR HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Consulting Services – Firm Selection

_______________________________________________________________________­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­

COUNTRY:                                    The Republic of Kenya

PROJECT TITLE:                       Second Kenya Urban Support Program (KUSP II)

PROJECT ID:                                P177048                                                       

CREDIT NO.:                               7349-KE; 7350-KE; IDA Grant Number E208-KE

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:             Consulting Services for Preparation of System Design Requirements, Procurement Documents, and Supervision of Deployment of an Electronic Documents and Records Management System (e-DRMS) at the Urban Development Department and Three Municipalities in Kenya

CONTRACT NO.:                        KE-MOTI-567492-CS-QCBS

1. The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank (the Bank) towards the cost of        the  Second Kenya Urban Support Program (KUSP II) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The aim of the consulting services (“the Services”) is to strengthen records and archives management systems within the Urban Development Department (UDD) of the State Department for Housing and Urban Development (SDHUD) and selected municipalities by enhancing institutional capacity, standardising records management practices, and supporting the design and supervised deployment of Electronic Document and Records Management Systems (EDRMS), with a view to improving efficiency, accessibility, compliance, transparency, and accountability in urban management. The consulting services are expected to be for a period of eight (8) calendar months in two phases, from the date of contract commencement.

3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR’s) for the assignment can be found at the following websites – www.housingandurban.go.ke and www.kusp.go.ke or can be obtained at the address given below;

4. The State Department for Housing and Urban Development (the Client) in the Ministry of Lands, Public Works, Housing and Urban Development – now invites eligible Consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services; Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and experience to perform the services (attach evidence). The shortlisting criteria are:

a) Core business and years in business: The firm shall be registered/incorporated as a consulting firm        with core business in the field of records management and information technology or equivalent for a                period of at least 10 years.

b) Consulting Firm Experience: The firm shall demonstrate as having successfully executed and                  completed at least two (2) assignments of similar nature, complexity and in a similar operating                        environment in the last seven (7) Details of similar assignments—including the name and address of the client, scope of services, contract value, implementation period, and key outputs/deliverables—should be provided in  the submitted Expression of Interest (EOI), together with a clear description of the relevance of the                   assignments to the scope of this consultancy

c) Technical and managerial capability of the firm: The firm shall demonstrate as having the                    requisite technical and managerial capacity to undertake the assignment in the submitted company                     profile(s).

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

5. The attention of Consultants’ is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and Revised Fourth Edition November 2020 (Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6.The Consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

7. Further information can be obtained at the address given below from 0900hrs to 1700hrs East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300hrs-1400hrs) and public holidays.

8. Expression of interest should be delivered by Wednesday 14th October 2026 at 1000hrs EAT using one of the following modalities:

a) Deposit in the Tender Box located on 6th Floor, Ardhi House in Nairobi, Kenya;

b) Send via email to; kusp2proc@housingandurban.go.ke .

9. Expressions of Interest must be delivered in written form to either the tender box located at located on 6th Floor, Ardhi House in Nairobi, Kenya or e-mail: kusp2proc@housingandurban.go.ke  and clearly marked with the Assignment Title and Contract Number as indicated above and addressed to:

rows.contact_address: PIU-PMD, Saidpur, Islamabad
rows.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

 

 

Country

Pakistan

 

Name of Project

Integrated Flood Resilience and Adaptation Project (IFRAP) (Component-II Strengthening Hydromet and Climate Services) / Modernization of Hydromet Services of PMD in Pakistan (MHSP)

 

Loan No. / Credit No. / Grant No.

IDA-73330

 

Assignment Title

Selection of Software Engineer

 

Reference No.

PK-PMD-562886-CS-INDV

 

1.  The Islamic Republic of Pakistan has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Strengthening Hydromet and Climate Services under the Component-II of Integrated Flood Resilience and Adaptation Project (IFRAP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for the subject consulting services.

Title/ Position

Qualifications

Experience

Software Engineer

The Consultant shall possess at least a Bachelor's degree (preferably Master's) in one of the following disciplines:

  • Software Engineering
  • Computer Science
  • Information Technology
  • Computer Engineering
  • Computational Science
  • At least 8 years of progressively responsible professional experience in software engineering, systems integration and digital solution development.
  • Demonstrated experience in software architecture/enterprise application development and integration.
  • Experience in Linux operating systems, databases and server administration.
  • Experience in cloud computing, virtualization and containerized environments.
  • Experience in API development, middleware and enterprise interoperability.
  • Experience in software implementation, systems integration, quality assurance, technical testing or user-acceptance support for complex information systems.
  • Familiarity with data governance, information security, backup, disaster recovery and business-continuity arrangements.
  • Experience with scientific, meteorological, hydrological, environmental or other mission-critical operational information systems will be highly desirable.
  • Strong technical documentation, coordination, communication and problem-solving skills.

 

2.  The Project Implementation Unit – Pakistan Meteorological Department (PIU-PMD) invites eligible Individuals (“Consultants”), to indicate their interest in providing the Services as per ToRs. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services by providing and submitting the following:

         a. A letter of Expression of Interest (EOI), providing information  regarding the Consultant’s qualifications, relevant skills, professional experience, and demonstrated capacity to successfully undertake and deliver the assignment in accordance with the requirements of the ToRs.

        b. A detailed, dated and signed Curriculum Vitae (CV) highlighting qualifications and experience in carrying out similar assignments, as well as references for possible checks.

3.   The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

4.   The Consultant will be selected in accordance with Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method as set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” November 2020.

5.   The Consultant will be employed on Contract, working on full-time basis in PIU PMD, Saidpur, Islamabad.

6.   Detailed/ respective Terms of Reference are available at https://weather.gov.pk/home/circulars

7.   The Expression of Interest (EOI) and Curriculum Vitae (CV) must be delivered in a written hard form to the address below by 28th of September, 2026 till 1600 hours Pakistan Standard Time. In case any personal interaction is required, it would be undertaken virtually or in person as the requirements may be. Applicants are therefore advised to ensure that updated and complete contact information has been provided in their EOI and CV.

8.    The address(es) referred to above is (are):

 

Project Implementation Unit (PIU)

Strengthening Hydromet and Climate Services

Email: ps.mhsp@pmd.gov.pk

PO Box No. 528, Post Mall

F-7/M, Islamabad, Pakistan

ATO ADMINISTRATIVO: SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE PARA SELEÇÃO DE EMPRESA DE CONSULTORIA
Edição: 7538 | 1ª Edição | Ano XXXII | Publicada em: 11/07/2026 SMOBI - Secretaria Municipal de Obras e Infraestrutura

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE PARA SELEÇÃO DE EMPRESA DE CONSULTORIA

BRASIL
BELO HORIZONTE – MG
PROJETO DE MELHORIA DA MOBILIDADE E INCLUSÃO URBANA DO BRT AMAZONAS
ACORDO DE EMPRÉSTIMO LOAN – 9069-BR
TÍTULO DO SERVIÇO: CONTRATAÇÃO DE EMPRESA ESPECIALIZADA PARA PRESTAÇÃO DE SERVIÇOS TÉCNICOS ESPECIALIZADOS DE ENGENHARIA PARA A ATUAÇÃO COMO O “ENGENHEIRO”, CONFORME A MODALIDADE DE EXECUÇÃO CONTRATUAL DO LIVRO AMARELO (YELLOW BOOK) DA FEDERAÇÃO INTERNACIONAL DE ENGENHEIROS DE CONSULTORIA FIDIC, EDIÇÃO 2017, PARA DESIGN E CONSTRUÇÃO DO TERMINAL DE INTEGRAÇÃO PARA O BRT AMAZONAS E SISTEMA VIÁRIO DO ENTORNO.
NÚMERO DE REFERÊNCIA: Manifestação de Interesse SMOBI 96.034/2026
PROCESSO ADMINISTRATIVO: 31.00456633/2026-37

A Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte, representada pela Secretaria Municipal de Obras e Infraestrutura – SMOBI, assinou um Acordo de Empréstimo, LOAN – 9069-BR, junto ao Banco Internacional para a Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento (BIRD), Banco Mundial, para a realização do PROJETO DE MELHORIA DA MOBILIDADE E INCLUSÃO URBANA DO CORREDOR AMAZONAS e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos em Serviços de Consultoria, em conformidade com o Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento - Aquisições em Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento - Bens, Obras, Serviços Técnicos e Serviços de Consultoria, datado de julho de 2016 e revisado em agosto de 2018, março e setembro de 2025.
A versão do "Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento" revisada em setembro de 2025 se encontra no seguinte link: https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/c84273d1b230aeb2b0b8134de5dc8cd7-0290012025/original/Procurement-Regulations-7th-Edition-Sep-2025.pdf. A contratação da Consultoria tem como objeto os SERVIÇOS TÉCNICOS ESPECIALIZADOS DE ENGENHARIA PARA A ATUAÇÃO COMO ENGENHEIRO, CONFORME A MODALIDADE DE EXECUÇÃO CONTRATUAL DO LIVRO AMARELO (YELLOW BOOK) DA FEDERAÇÃO INTERNACIONAL DE ENGENHEIROS DE CONSULTORIA FIDIC, EDIÇÃO 2017, PARA DESIGN E CONSTRUÇÃO DO TERMINAL DE INTEGRAÇÃO PARA O BRT AMAZONAS E SISTEMA VIÁRIO DO ENTORNO.
O Termo de Referência (TdR) detalhado e seus anexos encontram-se disponíveis para os interessados no site https://prefeitura.pbh.gov.br/licitacoes, no link relativo ao instrumento de seleção SMOBI 96.034/2026 (processo 7576). Também será disponibilizado no referido link, uma versão traduzida para o português do "Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento", revisão de setembro de 2025.
A Secretaria Municipal de Obras e Infraestrutura (SMOBI), na qualidade de órgão executor do Acordo e Empréstimo, através da Comissão Especial de Licitação instituída pela Portaria Conjunta SMOBI/SUDECAP nº 017/2026, convida firmas de Consultoria elegíveis para manifestarem seu interesse em participar do processo de seleção para realizar os serviços.
As Consultorias interessadas devem apresentar informações (portfólios, lista de contratos executados e outros documentos similares) que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações necessárias e experiência para prestar os serviços. Devem ser informados nome, cargo, telefone e e-mail do gestor técnico do contratante para os contratos apresentados.

As experiências necessárias para serem consideradas para a lista curta são:
1. Ter experiência em Fiscalização e Supervisão de obras de construção de terminais de integração multimodal (BRT com Ônibus, BRT/Ônibus com Metrô/Trem/VLT) ou de grandes obras, tais como: aeroportos, rodoviárias, estações metro/ferroviárias, centros logísticos de grande volume de tráfego.
2. Ter experiência na elaboração ou análise/validação de projetos de terminal de integração multimodal (BRT com Ônibus, BRT/Ônibus com Metrô/Trem/VLT) ou de grandes obras, tais como: aeroportos, rodoviárias, estações metro/ferroviárias, centros logísticos de grande volume de tráfego;
3. Ter experiência em projetos que demandaram necessidade de obtenção de licenciamento ambiental e/ou urbanístico.

Experiências desejáveis, não obrigatórias que poderão ser um diferencial para compor a Lista Curta:
1. Ter Experiência em Fiscalização/Supervisão de obras de qualquer natureza que utilizaram Condições de Contrato FIDIC (Fédération Internationale des Ingénieurs-Conseils, ou Federação Internacional de Engenheiros de Consultoria).
2. Ter experiência na elaboração ou análise/validação de Estudos e Projetos de Terminais de Integração Multimodal que tenham previsto empreendimento associado aos terminais.

As Consultorias interessadas devem se atentar aos parágrafos 3.13, 3.15 e 3.16, da ‘Seção III – Governança’, do Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial, citado acima, onde está estabelecida a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.
As Consultorias podem associar-se a outras empresas na forma de um empreendimento conjunto ou subconsultoria para aprimorar suas qualificações, mas devem indicar claramente se a associação está na forma de uma Joint Venture e/ou uma subconsultoria.
Uma consultoria será selecionada de acordo com o método de Seleção Baseada na Qualidade e Custo (SBQC), estabelecido no Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial citado acima.

Dúvidas/esclarecimentos e mais informações poderão ser obtidas através do endereço eletrônico comissao.engenheiroterminal@pbh.gov.br.

As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser encaminhadas através do endereço eletrônico comissao.engenheiroterminal@pbh.gov.br, no período de 11 de julho até o dia 04 de agosto de 2026, tendo com o Assunto “Manifestação de Interesse SMOBI 96.034/2026”

Leonardo José Gomes Neto
Secretaria Municipal de obras e Infraestrutura

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-IC-NIO-2.4-2 – Content Development Project Manager 3 (upper secondary school, content for educational domains))

Market Approach - Open, National

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Grant No. TF0C5794

 

Assignment Title: Content Development Project Manager 3 (upper secondary school, content for educational domains)

Reference No. LEARN-IC-NIO-2.4-2

Ukraine signed with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) the agreements for the Program "Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine" (hereinafter referred to as LEARN, or the Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The Content Development Project Manager 3 is responsible for leading and coordinating the development of educational content for upper secondary school (grades 10–12) within the New Ukrainian School (NUS) reform. The manager ensures that all content is aligned with the State Standard for Upper Secondary Education, supports competency-based learning, and is tailored to the diverse needs of students in academic lyceums.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are available at the link https://bit.ly/4gX5JVf

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference. The deadline for submission of applications is 11:00 am Kyiv time September 25, 2026.

rows.project_name: Lebanon Green Agrifood Transformation for Economic Recovery (GATE)
rows.bid_description: Senior Credit Analyst
rows.contact_address: Beirut, Lebanon
rows.notice_text:
The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), acting on behalf of the Republic of Lebanon (the Borrower), will implement the Green Agri-food Transformation for Economic Recovery (GATE) Project, financed by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD). The total Project cost is US$200 million, and the Project is scheduled to close in December 2028.

Under a Subsidiary Agreement signed with CDR, Kafalat S.A.L. is mandated by the Gov. of Lebanon to implement Subcomponent 1.2 and has established a Project Management Unit (PMU) responsible for the overall management and implementation of the subcomponent. Kafalat will provide direct loans to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating in Lebanon's agri-food and agro-tourism sectors. It will also be responsible for procurement, financial management, environmental and social (E&S) risk management and safeguards compliance, monitoring and evaluation, and overall oversight of the SME lending program.

  1.  OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The objective of this assignment is to engage a full-time Senior Credit Analyst to support the GATE PMU Credit activities to the end of the GATE Project. The Senior Credit Analyst shall be responsible for the end-to-end credit appraisal, structuring, and recommendation of SME loan applications under Subcomponent 1.2, ensuring full compliance with the Lending Manual, Project Operations Manual (POM), and internal policies.

  1. SCOPE OF WORK AND RESPONSIBILITIES

In order to strengthen the Project Management Unit (PMU), Kafalat is recruiting a officer to support the team in fulfilling the objectives of Sub-component 1.2 under the Gate Project. The Senior Credit Officer responsibilities will be as follows:

Overall responsibilities

The Senior Credit Analyst will serve as the primary relationship interface between Kafalat and SME clients across the full loan lifecycle, from initial outreach through to loan closure. Specific responsibilities include:

  • The Senior Credit Analyst holds an integrated mandate spanning the full loan lifecycle. The officer serves as Kafalat's primary client-facing contact, conducting outreach, guiding applicants through the application process, communicating Credit Committee decisions, and maintaining ongoing borrower relationships through to loan closure;
  • Proactively identify and target eligible SME borrowers within the GATE Project's defined sectors and eligibility requirements
  • Conduct field visits to prospective clients' business premises to assess operational reality and eligibility.
  • Request and verify completeness of all required documentation in accordance with the approved checklist, Lending Manual, and project eligibility criteria;
  • Review and validate all legal documentation of the borrower, including legal existence, ownership structure, authorized signatories, borrowing powers, and any litigation or legal encumbrances;
  • Conduct credit background checks through available sources (credit bureau, banking system, public registries) to assess the borrower’s credit history and reputation;
  • perform Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) checks, including completion of all required forms, verification of customer identity and beneficial ownership, screening against applicable sanction lists, and ensure accurate submission and record of all KYC/AML information within the Loan Management System (LMS);
  • Analyze the business profile of the borrower, including operational history, ownership evolution, and key structural changes;
  • Review, input, and analyze financial statements for at least three consecutive years, generate and interpret key financial ratios, and assess overall financial performance and sustainability;
  • Evaluate repayment capacity through detailed cash flow analysis and debt service capacity assessment, including stress considerations where relevant;
  • Review and analyze bank account statements to validate turnover, cash flow patterns, and consistency with declared financials;
  • Structure the proposed loan facility, including amount, tenor, repayment schedule, and purpose, ensuring alignment with project parameters and borrower capacity;
  • Prepare a comprehensive and well-documented credit appraisal incorporating financial, operational, and E&S considerations, with a clear recommendation (approval, rejection, or conditional approval) for submission to the Credit Manager;
  • Coordinate closely with the Environmental and Social (E&S) Officer to support E&S screening, categorization of subprojects, and identification of required risk mitigation measures in line with the ESMS and project requirements;
  • Assess proposed collateral to ensure compliance with internal policies, adequacy of coverage, and proper valuation by qualified third parties;
  • Monitor loan performance post-disbursement, including tracking repayments, identifying early warning signals, and supporting collection and recovery actions in coordination with the relevant internal units, in line with established procedures;
  • Ensure that all credit analysis, documentation, and decisions are accurately recorded and maintained within the Loan Management System (LMS);
  • Support the credit approval process by addressing queries and providing clarifications to the Credit Manager, Credit Risk Manager, and/or Credit Committee;
  • Follow up on approved loans to ensure fulfillment of all conditions precedent to disbursement, in coordination with the Credit Operations Function;
  • Ensure proper filing, archiving, and maintenance of complete and audit-ready credit files;
  • Ensure that loan proceeds are utilized strictly for the approved purposes by reviewing supporting documentation, including invoices and expenditure records, and verifying consistency between disbursements and underlying eligible expenditures in compliance with the Lending Manual, the POM and the Subsidiary agreement;
  • Conduct periodic portfolio reviews to assess SME performance and recommend corrective measures as needed.
  • Respond to enquiries from potential applicants, explain facility terms, eligibility criteria, and application procedures;
  • Guide SME applicants through the application and onboarding process, assisting with completion of the loan application package and required documentation checklist;
  • Maintain professional, ongoing client relationships with active borrowers, serving as their named point of contact at Kafalat for all operational matters;
  • Communicate Credit Committee decisions (approvals, conditions, rejections) to applicants in a clear, professional, and timely manner;
  • Manage borrower notifications for disbursement conditions, repayment schedules, annual review requirements, and any amendments to loan terms;
  • Maintain accurate client contact records and correspondence logs in the Loan Management System (LMS);
  • Support capacity building for SMEs to strengthen financial management and repayment discipline.
  1. QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS
  • Higher degree in Economics, finance, Business or a related field. A master’s degree or relevant professional certification is an asset
  • Minimum of 7 years of relevant working experience in Commercial lending operations loan portfolio management, and SME financing, preferably within a commercial bank.
  • Good understanding and familiarity with the World Bank safeguard policies.
  • Demonstrated experience in credit risk assessment, loan structuring, and monitoring of SME loans.
  • Excellent command of Arabic and English (written and spoken); knowledge of French is an asset.
  • Knowledge of the Lebanese banking sector, Lebanese Commercial Laws, SME financing challenges, and relevant regulatory environment.
  • Strong analytical, negotiation, and decision-making skills Working experience with the
  • Excellent communication and liaison skills.
  • Proven ability to negotiate, reschedule and troubleshoot relationships with SMEs.
  • Strong computer skills, including proficiency in loan tracking and management systems, and database management.

V. Reporting and Deliverables

  • The Senior Credit Analyst is expected to report to the Credit and Operations Manager.
  • Prepare quarterly portfolio review reports assessing SME performance, collateral coverage, covenant compliance, and recommending corrective measures where applicable.
  • Provide ad hoc reports, data extracts, and file documentation as requested by the PMU Manager, internal auditors, external auditors, or World Bank supervision missions.

  VI. COMMENCEMENT OF ASSIGNMENT AND dURATION  

The Senior Credit Analyst is expected to start his/her duties as soon as possible following contract signature. The initial Time-based contract duration is one year on a full-time basis, renewable annually based on satisfactory performance and availability of project funds.

rows.notice_text:
Specific Procurement Notice

Request for Bids-Works-(Two-envelope Bidding Process Without Prequalification)

Employer: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management – Directorate for Water Republic of Serbia

Project: Sava and Drina Rivers Corridors Integrated Development Program (SDIP)

Contract title: Rehabilitation works of the Galovica canal

Country: Republic of Serbia

Loan No.: 9128 YF

RFB No: SER-SDIP-RFB-W-24-38

  1. The Republic of Serbia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sava and Drina Rivers Corridors Integrated Development Program and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Rehabilitation works of the Galovica canal.
  2. The The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management – Directorate for Water now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Rehabilitation works of the Galovica canal. The Galovica channel is the main channel of the Galovica hydromelioration system, it has a catchment area of 71.600 ha. The channel route from the pumping station (PS) Galovica, on the left bank of the Sava River, to the settlement of Buanovci has a length of 46,88 km. In its current state, the channel is extremely muddy, with a poor flow profile and extremely overgrown with woody and aquatic vegetation. The existing culverts on the channel route are also silted up, and there is aquatic vegetation on the bottom of the channel. All this leads to a slowdown in the flow of water.

The scope of the assignment comprises:

      • Topographic surveys
      • Cleaning of vegetation,
      • Earth works for cleaning of the channel
      • Building of access roads in length of 2.4 km;
      • Rehabilitation of existing roads,
      • Concrete works of the culvatures,
      • Removal of the earthen landfills.
      • Removal of existing illegal unsanitary landfills
      • As-Built Records

All the details are provided in the respective Request for Bids document.

3. Bidding will be conducted through international competitive procurement using Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers- Procurement in Investment Projects Financing” July 2016, revised November 2017 and August 2018) (“Procurement Regulations”) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 50% and for Bid cost: 50 %.

rows.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN

TASHKENT-ANDIJAN TOLL ROAD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT

GFPP Grant No. TF0C8878

Project ID: P181937

 

Assignment Title: Preparation of Environmental and Social Reports and Studies for Phase 1 of the Tashkent-Andijan Toll Road Construction Project

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-TAR-GFPP-01

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the preparatory activities for the Tashkent-Andijan Toll Road Construction Project (“the Project”), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include Environmental and Social (E&S) Assessment, as well as Scoping Study for the Tashkent-Andijan Toll Road Construction Project, following the requirements of the International Finance Corporation (IFC) Sustainability Framework (“IFC SF”), the World Bank E&S Framework (“WB ESF”), and Uzbekistan’s regulatory requirements. The services are expected to be carried out during 3-month period, starting from December 2026.

 

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

 

The “Avtoyulinvest” Agency under the Committee for Roads now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

Criterion 1 - Legal and Regulatory Expertise in PPP and Transport

The firm shall provide evidence of:

(a) A minimum of 5 years of institutional experience in legal advisory services related to PPP and transport transactions, including demonstrated expertise in Uzbekistan's national legislative framework governing PPP arrangements and road tolling.

(b) Successful completion of a minimum of 2 assignments in which the firm provided legal advice on PPP or transport sector projects subject to World Bank Group operational policies and standards. Each reference assignment shall be substantiated by a brief description of the scope of services rendered, the applicable standards, and the resulting deliverables (e.g., legal memoranda, regulatory gap assessments, environmental and social due diligence reports).

 

Criterion 2 — Environmental, Social, and Climate Due Diligence Experience in the Transport Sector

The firm shall provide evidence of successful completion of a minimum of 2 assignments within the transport sector involving environmental and social (E&S) and/or climate due diligence, including E&S scoping studies, Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) and Livelihood Restoration Framework (LRF), Livelihood Restoration Plan (LRP), rendered under IFI financing within the last 10 years. For each qualifying reference assignment, the submission shall include:

(a) Name of the client and a brief description of the project and services provided;

(b) Explicit confirmation that IFC Performance Standards and/or World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines were applied as the governing international framework; and

(c) A description of the deliverables produced, which may include, inter alia, E&S scoping reports, RPF, RAP, LRF, LRP, Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), and other due diligence assessments.

Criterion 3 — Experience with ESIA Preparation in Uzbekistan

The firm shall provide evidence of recent and relevant experience in Uzbekistan by demonstrating successful completion of a minimum of 2 Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) within the last 10 years, where each qualifying ESIA satisfies all of the following conditions:

(a) The assessment satisfied the ESIA requirements of the WBG, as applicable; and

(b) The underlying project was situated in the transport sector, preferably structured or financed as a public-private partnership (PPP).

For each qualifying reference assignment, the submission shall indicate: the project name and location; the client; the national and international standards applied; the firm's role and scope of services; and the year of completion.

 

Key team members should form a gender diverse team with local knowledge and relevant language skills. Since documentation and applicable laws and regulation in Uzbek, the Consultant’s team should be capable of reviewing documents in such languages.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The shortlist will contain 5 to 8 firms.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method, as set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and as further detailed in the Request for Proposals (RFP).

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by September 25, 2026.

rows.notice_text:
Specific Procurement Notice

MINISTRY OF WORKS, HOUSING AND WATER RESOURCES

Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development Project

IDA CREDIT No.: 64100

 

CONSTRUCTION OF ATOMIC-EAST DETENTION POND AT GAEC

RFB No: GH-MWH-413765-CW-RFB

Request for Bids (RFB) Works

 

INTERNATIONAL COMPETITIVE BIDDING

 

Issued on: September 15, 2026

  1. The Government of Ghana has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Greater Accra Resilient and Integrated Development Project  and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Construction of Atomic-East Detention Pond at GAEC. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.
  2. The Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for the construction of the Atomic East detention pond at Ghana Atomic Energy Commission (GAEC). Moroni-Mboueni
